candidates.title: Deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 contributes to lung fibroblast activation and pulmonary fibrosis by interacting with and triggering focal adhesion kinase phosphorylation.
candidates.abstract: The etiology of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unknown, and therapeutic interventions are currently restricted. The activation of lung fibroblasts and the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling pathway are crucial to the pathogenesis of IPF, yet the exact molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Our study shows that the deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 (DLEU2) is elevated in the peripheral blood of patients with IPF, as well as in the lung tissues of mice with pulmonary fibrosis. Functional assays revealed that overexpression of DLEU2 facilitated fibrogenesis, whereas its suppression attenuated lung fibrosis in vivo and impeded fibroblast activation in vitro, predominantly through the regulation of FAK phosphorylation. Mechanistically, our findings reveal that DLEU2 regulates lung fibroblast activation by targeting miR-29a-3p. Conversely, inhibition of miR-29a-3p reversed the anti-fibrotic effects observed upon DLEU2 knockdown. Furthermore, DLEU2 was shown to directly interact with FAK, enhancing its phosphorylation and thereby facilitating fibrogenesis; inhibition of FAK phosphorylation counteracted the pro-fibrotic effects induced by DLEU2 overexpression. Taken together, these findings clarify the function of DLEU2 in facilitating FAK phosphorylation via its interactions with miR-29a-3p and FAK. The findings of this study suggest that DLEU2 may serve as a novel diagnostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of IPF.
candidates.fulltext: IntroductionIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a fatal interstitial lung disease of unknown cause, characterized histopathologically by usual interstitial pneumonia and clinically by a steady decline in lung function. The condition mainly impacts individuals over 50, with a higher prevalence in males. Conservative epidemiological estimates report a prevalence of 3 to 9 cases per 100,000 individuals, with incidence rates demonstrating an upward trend [1]. The median survival following diagnosis ranges from approximately 2.5 to 3.5 years [2]. Approved pharmacological treatments for IPF, pirfenidone and nintedanib, have demonstrated efficacy in decelerating disease progression and decreasing mortality rates. Nonetheless, these treatments do not offer a definitive cure for the disorder [3, 4]. Pathophysiologically, the persistent activation of pulmonary fibroblasts leads to an abnormal accumulation of extracellular matrix (ECM). This process is critically influenced by the dysregulation of the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling pathway, which plays a key role in the activation of fibroblasts [5–14]. Notably, phosphorylation of FAK constitutes a critical event in the initiation of downstream signaling cascades. Despite this, the upstream regulatory mechanisms controlling FAK activation remain inadequately understood. Elucidating these upstream signaling pathways may facilitate the identification of novel clinical biomarkers and therapeutic targets for IPF.Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) demonstrate substantial biological roles despite their limited capacity for protein coding. Emerging evidence indicates that lncRNAs are integral to the activation of lung fibroblasts, thereby impacting the pathogenesis of pulmonary fibrosis. lncITPF associates with heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein L (hnRNP L) to promote histone H3 and H4 acetylation at the ITGBL1 gene promoter. This epigenetic modification enhances lung fibroblast differentiation, proliferation, and migration, thus promoting fibrotic processes [15]. DNM3OS enhances the expression of miR-199a-5p, miR-199a-3p, and miR-214-3p, promoting lung fibroblast differentiation via canonical TGF-β/Smad and non-Smad pathways, thereby worsening pulmonary fibrosis [16]. Research on lncRNAs in IPF pathophysiology is still in early stages, with their regulatory roles and mechanisms not yet fully understood.Mechanistically, they modulate gene expression through diverse pathways such as direct protein interactions, alteration of histone modifications, interference with mRNA splicing, and functioning as molecular sponges for microRNAs [17]. The lncRNA deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 (DLEU2) was initially identified for its regulatory role in leukemia. Subsequent studies have implicated DLEU2 in various solid tumors, including breast, endometrial, esophageal, pancreatic, gastric cancers, glioma, and non-small cell lung cancer [18]. In chronic lymphocytic leukemia, DLEU2 overexpression upregulates miR-15a and miR-16-1, which suppress cyclins E1 and D1, inhibiting tumor cell proliferation and colony formation [19]. Additionally, DLEU2 contributes to cancer progression by sponging miR-30a-5p to regulate ETS2 in gastric cancer [20] and interacting with EZH2 in hepatocellular carcinoma [21]. Collectively, these findings underscore the significant regulatory functions and translational potential of DLEU2 in oncological contexts. However, investigations into the role of DLEU2 in non-neoplastic diseases remain limited, and its involvement in lung fibroblast activation and associated molecular mechanisms requires further exploration.This study revealed a significant upregulation of DLEU2 expression in the peripheral blood of patients with IPF as well as in the lung tissues of bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse models, suggesting a potentially pivotal role for DLEU2 in the pathogenesis of pulmonary fibrosis. The inhibition of DLEU2 expression substantially suppressed lung fibroblast activation and mitigated pulmonary fibrosis in vivo. INTRODUCTION: Juvenile systemic sclerosis (jSSc) is an orphan multisystem autoimmune disease that can cause significant morbidity during childhood and can lead to significant worsening of quality of life. The pathophysiological features are identical with adult-onset systemic sclerosis (SSc), jSSc exhibits a distinct clinical phenotype characterized by a significantly higher prevalence of diffuse cutaneous involvement, frequent overlap syndromes, distinct autoantibody profiles, and different long-term survival trajectories. Additionally, we analyze severity scores like the Juvenile Systemic Sclerosis Severity Score (J4S) alongside modern consensus metrics derived from the international Hamburg symposia. We emphasize the integration of pediatric-adapted clinical assessments, quantitative imaging, and patient and physician related outcomes.

candidates.fulltext: IntroductionJuvenile systemic sclerosis (jSSc) is an extremely rare pediatric autoimmune condition, with an estimated prevalence of 3 per million children and a female-to-male ratio of roughly 4.3:1 [1].The disease can severely impair physical function and psychosocial well-being in affected children, potentially leading to long-term disability if disease activity is not identified early and target-directed therapy is not initiated prior to irreversible tissue damage [2, 3].JSSc is characterized by a high frequency of the diffuse cutaneous subtype (~ 70%) and overlap features (~ 1/3 of cases), primarily with juvenile dermatomyositis [4, 5].Due to the orphan nature of the disease, conducting adequately powered, large-scale clinical trials is extremely challenging due to the small and geographically dispersed patient population. Moreover, given the high frequency of visceral organ involvement and the marked phenotypical heterogeneity within individual patients, robust outcome tools must comprehensively capture multi-organ complexity.Therefore, many of the outcome measures currently applied in clinical practice and clinical trial settings have been extrapolated from in adult studies.However, direct application of adult-derived outcome measures to pediatric populations remains problematic, as children undergo continuous physical growth and developmental shifts. Consequently, physiological parameters such as creatinine clearance or lung volumes and diffusion capacity (DLCO) changes and evolve naturally with somatic growth, necessitating pediatric-specific normative corrections and age-appropriate feasibility considerations [6].To overcome these combined barriers, the integration of highly sensitive, age-specific, responsive and stringently standardized outcome measures is essential to capture clinically meaningful modifications in disease activity.Nowadays, we do not have any validated outcome measure for jSSc resulting from the application of a formal and standardized methodology like OMERACT [7].The SHARE guidelines for the management of patients with jSSc use a worsening in the JSSc Severity Score (J4S) after at least 6 months of MTX therapy as a measure of response to treatment and to define “refractory” disease. However, this score has several limitations and has never been validated in multi-center cohorts as an outcome measure [8].The recently published guidelines from British Society of Rheumatology (BSR) for SSc [9]– which for the first time expanded management along all ages – do not propose any measure to define disease activity in pediatric patients and the definition of refractory disease is delegated to treating physician [10].Recently, the International Juvenile Systemic Sclerosis Outcome Group (IJOG), in collaboration with the Childhood Arthritis and Rheumatology Research Alliance (CARRA) and the Pediatric Rheumatology European Society (PReS), launched an international initiative to identify outcome measures specifically designed for jSSc [5]. The results of this project will be available in the next years while the initial findings will be reported in this report.Therefore, given the lack of robust, pediatric-specific data from clinical trials, our work will provide clear and standardized guidelines for longitudinal clinical monitoring. The establishment of these routine monitoring parameters is particularly crucial for physicians from centers clinically following only a very limited number of patients with jSSc. [11]. candidates.title: A novel inhalable tanshinone IIA lipid nanocrystal formulation for the enhanced treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive, fatal interstitial lung disease marked by relentless deterioration of pulmonary function. Clinically, oral pharmacotherapy for IPF is hampered by two major limitations: inefficient drug delivery to the lung parenchyma and systemic exposure leading to unavoidable off-target side effects. In this study, we developed an inhalable tanshinone IIA (TA) formulation based on lipid nanocrystals to address these challenges. Leveraging the high drug loading capacity and structural stability of lipid nanocrystals, this platform overcomes the intrinsic hydrophobicity of TA, thereby markedly improving its aqueous dispersibility, aerosolization performance, and regional deposition in the deep lung. In vitro, TA lipid nanocrystals significantly enhanced cellular uptake in both pulmonary epithelial cells and lung fibroblasts. In vivo, they achieved substantially high and sustained pulmonary drug exposure. In a bleomycin-induced mouse model of IPF, inhaled TA lipid nanocrystals attenuated histopathological fibrosis, preserved lung function, and suppressed chronic inflammation via modulating the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway and the coagulation-fibrinolysis system. Collectively, this study establishes TA as a promising inhaled therapeutic agent for IPF and introduces lipid nanocrystals as a versatile, scalable, and clinically translatable platform for targeted pulmonary delivery in fibrotic and other chronic respiratory diseases.
candidates.fulltext: IntroductionIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic progressive interstitial lung disease caused by a variety of lung injuries, including toxic, autoimmune, infectious, traumatic, and drug-induced causes [1–3]. Accumulating evidence indicates that persistent alveolar epithelial cell injury, activation, and dysregulated repair processes are key contributors to the onset and progression of IPF [4]. Persistent alveolar epithelial cell injury leads to aberrant activation, resulting in the dysregulated production of multiple pro-inflammatory and profibrotic mediators, including tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), chemokine C-C motif ligand 2 (CCL2), and transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) [5]. These cytokines promote fibroblast proliferation, migration, and differentiation into myofibroblasts. Activated fibroblasts and myofibroblasts subsequently secrete excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) components, including fibronectin, collagen, and matrix metalloproteinases. Excessive deposition of ECM disrupts normal lung architecture, leading to alveolar destruction, reduced pulmonary compliance, and progressive impairment of gas exchange [6, 7]. As a result, patients with IPF experience an irreversible decline in lung function, leading to symptoms such as dyspnea that can ultimately be life-threatening. Its average life expectancy after diagnosis is only 3 ~ 5 years, and the five-year survival rate is less than 30% [8, 9]. Although lung transplantation remains the most effective treatment for IPF, only a small proportion of patients are able to undergo this intervention due to economic constraints, postoperative complications and age-related eligibility criteria [10, 11]. Current evidence-based guidelines for the treatment of IPF recommend the use of pirfenidone and nintedanib. These two drugs can delay the progression of IPF to a certain extent and reduce the mortality rate of IPF. However, the oral administration of high doses of these drugs may lead to adverse effects in the gastrointestinal tract and liver, imposing significant psychological and physiological burdens on patients [11–13]. Recently, PDE4B inhibitors nerandomilast has been approved for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis. Meanwhile, new anti-fibrotic drugs such as Lysophosphatidic acids (LPA) antagonist BMS-986020 and novel Autotaxin (ATX) inhibitor BBT-877 are under development [14, 15]. Obviously, the development of more effective, reliable, and cost-effective therapeutic regimens for IPF remains a key focus in clinical research.Tanshinone ⅡA (TA) is a hydrophobic diterpenoid compound extracted from the traditional Chinese medicinal herb Salvia miltiorrhiza. Previous studies have shown that TA exhibits anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidative stress, anti-apoptotic, and anti-angiogenic effects, and has attracted widespread attention in the treatment of fibrosis in organs such as the lungs, heart, liver and kidneys [16]. Inhalation administration enables direct delivery of drugs to the pulmonary disease site without systemic circulation, offering advantages such as targeted and localized treatment, rapid clinical response, improved drug utilization, and enhanced patient convenience, which also reduces adverse reactions associated with oral or intravenous administration, making it a promising drug delivery approach for the treatment of IPF [17, 18]. However, drugs delivered to the respiratory tract following inhalation must overcome multiple pulmonary physiological barriers, such as mucociliary clearance, alveolar macrophage uptake, and epithelial permeability limitations, before reaching the target lung tissue to exert their therapeutic effects. Specifically, drug particles deposited in the conducting airways may interact with mucus and subsequently be cleared via mucociliary transport. Inhaled particles that reach the respiratory zone may encounter pulmonary surfactants, which can promote the formation of a “protein corona” and increase their recognition and uptake by alveolar macrophages, leading to phagocytosis and clearance [17, 19, 20]. Therefore, developing an inhalable formulation of TA capable of overcoming these physiological barriers is essential for achieving efficient drug delivery to the lungs, a critical step toward improving the therapeutic outcomes of IPF.Nanocrystal, as a classic nano-formulation, have been extensively validated and successfully commercialized to address the solubility challenges of poorly water-soluble drugs across oral, parenteral, and other drug delivery routes. Nanocrystal technology reduces drug particle size to the nanoscale, thereby increasing the surface area of the particles and significantly enhancing the drug’s saturation solubility and dissolution rate. Compared with other nano drug delivery systems, nanocrystal formulations consist primarily of drug with stabilizers, offering the distinct advantage of high drug loading efficiency, which is suitable for the development of inhalable formulations. candidates.title: MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 Signaling in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Genetic Susceptibility to Profibrotic Progression and Clinical Perspectives.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disorder strongly mediated by genetic susceptibility and aberrant epithelial repair mechanisms. Among the identified genetic factors, the MUC5B promoter polymorphism rs35705950 represents the most significant and frequently replicated risk variant associated with both familial and sporadic IPF. This review focuses on the mechanistic role of MUC5B dysregulation in promoting epithelial dysfunction and profibrotic signalling, with particular emphasis on its interaction with transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signalling and KL-6-associated epithelial injury. Excessive MUC5B expression within distal airways disrupts mucociliary homeostasis, prolongs epithelial exposure to inhaled toxic stimuli, and enhances persistent alveolar stress, thereby facilitating chronic epithelial injury and aberrant tissue repair. Sustained epithelial damage subsequently activates TGF-β-mediated SMAD signalling pathways, promoting fibroblast activation, myofibroblast differentiation, and extracellular matrix deposition. Emerging evidence further suggests a close relationship between MUC5B-associated epithelial dysfunction and elevated KL-6 expression, indicating that KL-6 may function as a downstream biomarker indicating ongoing epithelial injury and fibrotic progression. The proposed MUC5B/TGF-β/KL-6 mechanistic signaling provides an integrated molecular network linking genetic susceptibility, epithelial dysfunction, biomarker elevation, and progressive fibrosis in IPF. In addition, telomere-related and surfactant-associated gene mutations further lead to epithelial instability and impaired regenerative capacity. Together, these interconnected molecular mechanisms provide significant insights into IPF progression and may support the development of biomarker-driven prognostic approaches and targeted precision therapies for improved disease management.
candidates.fulltext: IntroductionIdiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive, chronic and irreversible interstitial lung disease (ILD) characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition and destruction of the normal lung architecture, resulting in impaired gas exchange and respiratory failure [1]. Histopathologically, IPF is characterized by usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) exhibiting patchy subpleural fibrosis, fibroblastic foci, and honeycomb cyst formation. IPF primarily affects individuals over 50 years of age and is more commonly observed in males. Significant advances in diagnosis and management, the disease remains associated with poor clinical outcomes, with a median survival of approximately 3–5 years following diagnosis [2]. The global incidence and prevalence of IPF continue to rise due to population aging, increased environmental exposure, improved diagnostic approaches, and greater clinical awareness [3]. The pathogenesis of IPF is complex and involves repeated injury to alveolar epithelial cells followed by dysregulated tissue repair and progressive fibrotic remodeling. Injured epithelial cells release several profibrotic mediators; transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β), plays a major role in fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts. These activated myofibroblasts produce excessive amounts of collagen, fibronectin, and other ECM proteins, leading to irreversible scar formation and loss of lung elasticity. In contrast to normal wound healing, fibroblasts in IPF exhibit resistance to apoptosis, resulting in persistent fibrosis and progressive deterioration of pulmonary function [4]. Additional mechanisms, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and telomere shortening, further cause epithelial injury and abnormal tissue remodeling. Although currently approved antifibrotic agents such as Pirfenidone and Nintedanib can slow disease progression, they are unable to reverse the fibrosis, highlighting the urgent need for targeted molecular therapies [5].Both environmental and genetic factors significantly contribute to IPF susceptibility and progression. Cigarette smoking remains the strongest environmental risk factor, while chronic exposure to wood dust, silica, asbestos, metal dust, agricultural pollutants, and air pollutants such as particulate matter and ozone further enhances the disease risk. Aging-related cellular alterations, including stem cell exhaustion and telomere attrition, also promote fibrotic responses in the lung [6]. These environmental factors interact with genetic predisposition, supporting the widely accepted “two-hit hypothesis” in IPF pathogenesis. Among the molecular determinants of IPF, genetic susceptibility is emerged as a critical cause of disease initiation and progression [7]. The MUC5B promoter polymorphism (rs35705950) represents the most significant genetic risk factor identified to date and leads to a substantial proportion of inherited susceptibility to IPF. MUC5B encodes mucin 5B, a major gel-forming mucin involved in airway mucus production and mucociliary clearance. Aberrant overexpression of MUC5B disrupts mucosal homeostasis, impairs clearance of inhaled particles and cellular debris, and promotes persistent epithelial stress within distal airways. This altered epithelial microenvironment enhances susceptibility to chronic injury and facilitates progressive fibrotic remodeling. Importantly, the rs35705950 polymorphism is consistently associated with both familial and sporadic forms of IPF, highlighting its central role in disease pathogenesis [8, 9].In addition to MUC5B, mutations in telomere-associated genes, including TERT, TERC, RTEL1, and PARN, are strongly associated with IPF, particularly familial and sporadic forms of the disease. These genes are essential for maintaining telomere integrity and chromosomal stability. Defective telomeres cause accelerated telomere shortening, premature cellular senescence, impaired epithelial renewal, and defective tissue repair mechanisms. Alveolar epithelial cells with critically shortened telomeres exhibit reduced regenerative capacity and increased susceptibility to apoptosis, thereby perpetuating chronic epithelial injury and fibroblast activation [10]. Emerging evidence also indicates that telomere dysfunction causes mitochondrial abnormalities, oxidative stress, and inflammatory signaling pathways that further intensify fibrogenesis. Mutations in surfactant-related genes, including SFTPA1, SFTPA2, and SFTPC, also play an important role in familial and early-onset forms of IPF. These genes encode surfactant proteins essential for maintaining alveolar stability and reducing surface tension within the lungs [11]. Genetic alterations affecting surfactant protein synthesis and processing lead to protein misfolding, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and activation of the unfolded protein response in alveolar epithelial cells. candidates.title: Antibody-Drug Conjugates in Biliary Tract Cancer: Current Evidence, Emerging Targets, and Future Directions.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Biliary tract cancer (BTC) is a heterogeneous group of malignancies with limited systemic treatment options and poor prognosis. While immunochemotherapy has become the first-line standard, second-line therapy remains inadequate. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality leveraging antigen-specific targeting to deliver potent cytotoxic payloads. This review provides a comprehensive, multi-target appraisal of the ADC landscape in BTC.
RECENT FINDINGS: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), supported by DESTINY-PanTumor02 (ORR 22%) and HERB (ORR 36.4%) trials, received 2024 FDA tumor-agnostic approval for HER2-positive solid tumors including BTC. Zanidatamab achieved 41.3% ORR in HERIZON-BTC-01, securing BTC-specific regulatory approval. BL-B01D1, an EGFR×HER3 bispecific ADC, demonstrated preliminary BTC activity (ORR 28.6%) without reported interstitial lung disease in the BTC cohort, though sample size and follow-up remain limited, while its phase III nasopharyngeal carcinoma trial established proof of concept for bispecific ADCs. BL-M05D1 phase I results (ASCO 2026) provided the first clinical evidence for Claudin18.2 ADCs in BTC (ORR 42.5%). Trop2-directed ADCs show theoretical applicability across solid tumors given 69.5% high-expression prevalence, but BTC-specific clinical data are absent. B7-H3 and CD44v5 represent emerging targets with early clinical or preclinical validation. This review provides a unified framework for navigating the rapidly evolving multi-target ADC landscape in BTC. Critical challenges remain, including the absence of phase III randomized trials, tumor heterogeneity, optimal biomarker-guided patient selection, and rational combination strategies with immunotherapy. Standardization of HER2 testing and broader molecular profiling will be essential to realize the clinical potential of ADCs in this historically treatment-refractory disease. candidates.title: RNA therapeutics in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and systemic sclerosis: a compartment-aware translational framework.
candidates.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus/lupus nephritis (SLE/LN), and systemic sclerosis (SSc) remain major causes of chronic inflammation, disability, organ damage, and treatment burden despite therapeutic advances. RNA therapeutics offer programmable transcript suppression, network-level microRNA modulation, transient restoration of protective proteins, and targeting-ligand functions. Existing reviews largely catalogue modalities or individual delivery systems; this review instead asks whether a candidate forms an interpretable translational program across target biology, disease compartment, intended cell, productive intracellular access, direct target engagement, pathway pharmacodynamics, repeat-dose safety, and manufacturing feasibility. RA is primarily a synovial immune-stromal delivery problem in which RNA programs must also demonstrate an advantage over effective biologic or targeted synthetic therapies. SLE/LN offers interferon, B-cell, co-stimulatory, microRNA, messenger RNA (mRNA), and complement opportunities, but therapeutic nucleic acids and carriers must not intensify nucleic-acid sensing, interferon activity, or complement-associated injury. SSc combines strong antifibrotic RNA biology with an accessible skin proof-of-mechanism window, whereas lung, vascular, and internal-organ programs remain more delivery-limited. We separate human pathway validation, RNA-platform evidence outside the target disease, disease-specific RNA evidence, and patient efficacy. Recent human complement-factor-B pharmacodynamic data strengthen the platform-level evidence but do not establish efficacy in RA or LN. The most informative early trials will therefore be biomarker-enriched and mechanism-rich, with prespecified criteria that distinguish target failure from delivery, dose, endotype, or safety failure.

candidates.title: Potential risk of occupational exposure to respirable crystalline silica in Saudi Arabia: a comprehensive review of the current status and future challenges.
candidates.abstract: Respirable crystalline silica (RCS) is a major occupational health hazard associated with silicosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), lung cancer, autoimmune diseases, and other systemic disorders. Saudi Arabia is undergoing rapid industrial expansion in sectors with substantial potential for RCS exposure, including mining, construction, cement production, glass manufacturing, oil and gas, engineered stone fabrication, and photovoltaic manufacturing. This review evaluates the potential risk of occupational RCS exposure in Saudi Arabia by integrating evidence from the scientific literature, government reports, labor and mining statistics, mineralogical data, and regulatory documents. The novel silica Hazard triangle framework was applied to assess three principal determinants of occupational exposure: workforce distribution, silica-containing materials, and high-risk industrial activities. Saudi Arabia possesses extensive reserves of high-purity silica sand, and continued expansion of mining and downstream silica-based industries may increase occupational exposure potential. The kingdom's arid climate may also contribute to dust generation and increase the occupational exposure of RCS. Although documented cases of silicosis confirm that silica-related disease exists in Saudi Arabia, published evidence on occupational exposure assessment, epidemiology, and health surveillance remains limited. International regulatory developments demonstrate the importance of health-based occupational exposure limits (OELs), exposure monitoring, engineering controls, and medical surveillance. Current Saudi labor law, National Council for occupational safety and health (NCOSH) policies, and General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) occupational disease frameworks provide an important legal and institutional foundation for the future development of silica-specific occupational health regulations. candidates.title: Early recognition of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis in outpatient settings: musculoskeletal and gastrointestinal clues beyond respiratory disease.
candidates.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a multisystem immune-mediated disease characterized by adult-onset asthma, eosinophilic inflammation, and necrotizing vasculitis of small-to-medium-sized vessels. Diagnosis is frequently prompted by clinically overt neurological, cardiac, renal, cutaneous, or gastrointestinal involvement. However, potentially informative manifestations may already be recognizable earlier, particularly when asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and blood eosinophilia coexist with otherwise nonspecific extrapulmonary findings. Most cohorts describe manifestations at diagnosis or during established disease and provide limited information on their early temporal appearance across different specialties. This gap is particularly relevant to arthralgia and myalgia, which are common but poorly characterized, and to eosinophilic gastrointestinal manifestations that may initially be classified as organ-restricted eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders. Biopsy-proven myositis is rare but has occasionally been reported at presentation or before clinically recognizable neuropathy. This review examines early and potentially recognizable manifestations of EGPA across outpatient settings, with particular attention to musculoskeletal symptoms, objective muscle involvement, eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease, and the therapeutic implications of distinguishing organ-restricted eosinophilic disease from systemic EGPA.

candidates.title: The application of Chicago classification 4.0 in esophageal motility disorders of scleroderma: a case-control study in China.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by multi-organ fibrosis and vasculopathy that frequently involves the esophagus. This study assessed esophageal motility disorders in patients with SSc using High-resolution manometry (HRM) and classified these disorders according to the Chicago Classification version 4.0, aims to investigate the associations between esophageal dysfunction and clinical phenotypes in Chinese SSc patients, while exploring potential modifications to enhance the applicability of the Chicago v4.0 protocol in SSc patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified SSc patients fulfilling 2013 ACR criteria who underwent HRM classified by Chicago v4.0 at our center (2021-2023). Demographics, organ involvement, pulmonary-function tests, echocardiography and reflux symptom scores (RDQ/GERDQ) were extracted from the hospital information system; age and sex matched non-SSc HRM subjects served as controls. Associations between Chicago categories and clinical variables were examined by multinomial logistic regression.
RESULTS: In our study, esophageal motility disorders were present in 76.7% of patients with systemic sclerosis, predominantly characterized by ineffective esophageal motility (IEM) (35%) and absent contractility (AC) (36.67%). The occurrence rate of AC rose with age. Symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux were more common in the AC group [Odds Ratio: 3.23 (1.02-10.22) vs 1.43(0.52-3.95), P<0.05, E value=2.99]. Diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) was significantly reduced in both IEM and AC (-2.03 vs -2.70, P value<0.05), with a more pronounced decrease in AC. Total lung capacity (TLC) and forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) exhibited stronger associations with AC (-1.04 and -0.8 respectively, p value<0.05). candidates.title: Single‑cell and spatial transcriptomics in chronic lung disease: cellular heterogeneity and molecular mechanisms in IPF and COPD.
candidates.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) have advanced the study of complex lung diseases by resolving cellular heterogeneity, tissue architecture, and intercellular communication. These technologies are particularly informative in chronic respiratory disorders, where pathological remodeling involves coordinated alterations across epithelial, stromal, immune, and endothelial compartments. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a rare fatal fibrotic disorder, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a prevalent heterogeneous respiratory condition, represent distinct chronic lung diseases shaped by persistent injury, maladaptive repair, and progressive tissue remodeling. However, current understanding of their pathogenesis remains incomplete, and conventional approaches lack the resolution to define disease-associated cell states, spatially restricted niches, or compartment-specific interactions. This review synthesizes recent scRNA-seq and ST studies in IPF and COPD, emphasizing how high-resolution atlases refine established pathobiological frameworks and reveal shared and disease-specific cellular programs. We highlight epithelial dysfunction and impaired progenitor repair as shared mechanistic features of IPF and COPD, while emphasizing alveolar regenerative failure, fibroblast activation, and profibrotic niche formation as central features of IPF, and compartment-specific airway remodeling, inflammatory epithelial states, and emphysema-associated parenchymal injury as prominent features of COPD. We further discuss stromal and immune remodeling, hypoxia-associated vascular remodeling, and the translational implications of these findings for molecular stratification, target prioritization, and mechanism-informed therapeutic development, while noting limitations related to end-stage tissue sampling, platform constraints, and mouse-human correspondence. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding the cellular an

candidates.title: [Analysis of Clinical Characteristics in 49 Patients of Lung Cancer  Combined with Interstitial Lung Disease].
candidates.journal: Zhongguo fei ai za zhi = Chinese journal of lung cancer
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The patients of lung cancer combined with interstitial lung disease (LC-ILD) account for a high proportion, and their prognosis is poor. Currently, no standard treatment regimen had been established for this population. This study aimed to summarize the clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes of patients with LC-ILD, and to explore factors associated with marked ILD progression under different tumor treatment strategies.
METHODS: The clinical characteristics, tumor treatment, and follow-up data of 49 LC-ILD patients hospitalized in the Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine at Peking Union Medical College Hospital from January 2018 to December 2024 were collected. The efficacy and follow-up outcomes of different treatment modalities were observed; the survival analysis was performed, and the potential influencing factors for the significant progression of ILD were analyzed.
RESULTS: LC-ILD is most commonly of the usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern, with tumors frequently located in fibrotic regions. The median progression-free survival (PFS) was 7.0 months for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 4.0 months for small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Of the 36 patients with completed follow-up and treatment, 10 showed radiographic progression of interstitial lesions, with 4 deaths occurring in this subgroup. Logistic regression analysis indicated that radiotherapy was significantly correlated radiological progression of ILD (P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: For patients with LC-ILD, individualized evaluation including chest high resolution computed tomography and pulmonary function test (particularly diffusing capacity) should be performed before initiating therapy. The therapeutic approach should balance efficacy and safety, and special attention should be given to the risk of radiological progression of ILD associated with radiotherapy.

candidates.title: Isolated Bilateral Periocular Lupus Miliaris Disseminatus Faciei: A Clinicopathological Mimicker of Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis.
candidates.journal: The American journal of case reports
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND Lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei (LMDF) is a rare idiopathic granulomatous dermatosis that presents as discrete yellow-brown, erythematous, or skin-colored papules on the central face, with a recognized preference for the eyelids and periorbital region. CASE REPORT We report a case of isolated bilateral periocular LMDF in a healthy young adult man whose initial eyelid biopsy revealed suppurative necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, raising histopathological concern for granulomatosis with polyangiitis and other systemic granulomatous diseases. Autoimmune, vasculitic, infectious, urinary, orbital, and thoracic evaluations were otherwise negative, apart from only mild inflammatory marker elevation, with an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 21 mm/h (reference range, 0-20 mm/h) and C-reactive protein level of 0.94 mg/dL (reference range, 0.1-0.5 mg/dL). The final diagnosis was supported by the clinicopathological combination of symmetrical folliculocentric periocular papules, perifollicular necrobiotic suppurative granulomas, absence of true vasculitis, negative infectious studies, and absence of systemic disease. After 1 month of extended-release oral minocycline, the patient had marked flattening of papules and near-complete resolution of crusted inflammatory lesions. Adverse effects were monitored clinically during routine follow-up after completion of the 1-month treatment course; the patient reported no treatment-related adverse effects, and no adverse effects were observed. CONCLUSIONS Clinicopathological correlation and comprehensive systemic evaluation are necessary to differentiate this rare dermatosis from infectious or vasculitic mimics. In this patient, oral minocycline was associated with marked short-term clinical improvement after 1 month, but this single observation does not establish broader therapeutic efficacy for LMDF.

candidates.title: Type 2 Inflammation in Airway Diseases: Eosinophilic Bronchiectasis as an Emerging Phenotype.
candidates.abstract: Bronchiectasis is a chronic and highly heterogeneous airway disease traditionally regarded as a neutrophil-dominated condition driven by persistent infection and dysregulated innate immunity. Over the last decade, this traditional view has been increasingly challenged by the identification of distinct inflammatory phenotypes with important biological and therapeutic implications.Among these, eosinophilic bronchiectasis has emerged as a clinically meaningful and mechanistically distinct phenotype, characterized by type 2 (T2) immune activation, eosinophil-driven airway inflammation, and differential responsiveness to targeted therapies.In this narrative review, we provide an overview of eosinophilic bronchiectasis, emphasizing epidemiology, immunopathogenesis, and cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying airway damage and remodelling. We discuss key pathways involving eosinophils, epithelial-immune interactions, and T2 cytokine signalling, as well as established and emerging biomarkers for phenotype identification.We proposed a diagnostic framework and definitions for eosinophilic bronchiectasis, i.e. definite (airway eosinophilia with sputum or bronchoalveolar lavage eosinophils ≥ 3%), probable (persistent peripheral blood eosinophilia ≥ 300 cells/µL), and possible (a single elevated blood eosinophil count of ≥ 150-300 cells/µL or elevated FeNO > 25 ppb in the absence of asthma), to be provisionally used in the absence of shared consensus criteria.Particular attention is devoted to therapeutic implications, including biologic agents targeting the IL-5/IL-5r axes and novel disease-modifying strategies for eosinophilic disorders. Finally, we highlight unmet needs and future research directions toward precision medicine approaches aimed at improving outcomes in this increasingly recognized bronchiectasis phenotype.

candidates.title: Making trade-offs explicit: development and pilot of a Belgian MCDA framework for orphan drug appraisal.
candidates.journal: International journal of technology assessment in health care
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Orphan drug reimbursement remains a contested area in health technology assessment (HTA), as decision makers must balance limited evidence, high unmet need, patient-relevant value, and affordability. Multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) has been proposed to make such trade-offs more explicit and transparent, yet empirical applications in European national HTA settings remain scarce.
METHODS: We developed and piloted an MCDA framework for orphan drug reimbursement in Belgium. Candidate criteria were identified through a systematic literature review. A multidisciplinary expert panel (comprising representatives from the national reimbursement agency, sickness funds, patient organizations, pharmaceutical companies, clinicians, and bioethicists) participated in four focus group discussions to select and define criteria. Criterion weights were elicited through a three-round Delphi process. The framework was piloted on four orphan drugs previously appraised in Belgium: ponatinib, pirfenidone, onasemnogene abeparvovec, and metreleptin.
RESULTS: Seven quantitative and three qualitative contextual criteria were selected. Unmet medical need received the highest weight, followed by comparative effectiveness and impact on patient-reported outcomes. Onasemnogene abeparvovec achieved the highest overall MCDA score (0.77), followed by metreleptin (0.65), pirfenidone (0.47), and ponatinib (0.39). The pilot also generated policy-relevant insights on criterion design, handling residual uncertainty, separating value assessment from reimbursement feasibility (through cost criteria), and using scores to support-rather than replace-deliberation.
CONCLUSION: This study presents the first MCDA framework for orphan drug reimbursement in Belgium and illustrates how criterion weights and scores can structure committee deliberation, complemented by contextual appraisal, to support more transparent, consistent, and accountable decision making.

candidates.title: Cystic pulmonary amyloidosis with lymphoid interstitial pneumonia in Sjögren's disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interstitial lung diseases are commonly seen in association with Sjögren's disease, especially lymphoproliferative disorders, such as lymphoid interstitial pneumonia. In occasional and rare cases, pulmonary amyloidosis with cysts, nodules, and/or ground-glass opacites as radiological features, can also become a complication of Sjögren's disease. On the other hand, diffuse cystic lung disease, without nodules, concomitant with chylous fluid accumulation in female leads to initial suspicion of lymphangioleiomyomatosis. Interestingly, it's challenging to differentiate if diffuse cystic lung lesion absent of nodules, chylous fluid accumulation and Sjögren's disease happen simultaneously.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 34-year-old female, with diffuse cystic lung disease, chylous reflux lymphedema and Sjögren's disease, was eventually diagnosed with cystic pulmonary amyloidosis with lymphoid interstitial pneumonia, secondary to Sjögren's disease, and chylous reflux lymphedema as comorbidity. The case presented with atypical pulmonary amyloidosis radiological features of lung lesion, where diffuse cysts existed without nodules or ground-glass opacites, apart from the scarcely seen size of the biggest cyst. The patient was diagnosed with CPA with LIP, secondary to SjD. Clinical symptoms were relieved after thoracoscopic lobectomy of the right lower lobe, where located the biggest cyst. The immunosuppressants that she had been taking were recommended again for disease stabilization.
CONCLUSION: Cystic pulmonary amyloidosis is a rare complication of Sjögren's disease, while lymphoid interstitial pneumonia is comparatively well-known. There can be cystic pulmonary amyloidosis cases where the lung lesion only consists of diffuse, thin-walled, and variably-sized cysts, with the absence of nodules or ground-glass opacities, which warrants a lung biopsy. Clinicians should be alerted to the cyst-only radiological features of the cystic pulmonary amyloidosis with Sjögren's diseas

candidates.title: Indirect Echocardiographic Signs of Increased Right-sided Afterload in Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis: Insights from a Multicentre Italian Study.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pulmonary vascular involvement is a determinant of worse outcomes in fibrotic lung diseases. Its prevalence and prognostic relevance in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) is unknown. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of indirect echocardiographic abnormalities in progressive pulmonary fibrosis before antifibrotic therapy, characterize a baseline high-risk cardiopulmonary functional profile, and assess 12-month clinical trajectories.
METHODS: Observational, retrospective, multicentre study.
RESULTS: 158 patients (median (IQR) age of 71 (65.2-77.0) years) with PPF were enrolled. Thirty (19.0%) had ≥ 1 echocardiographic indirect sign of increased right-sided afterload, 15 (9.5%) ≥ 2, 9 (5.7%) ≥ 3 and 1 (0.6%) all four. A shortened right ventricular outflow tract acceleration time (< 105 ms) was the most frequent alteration (12.7%), followed by right atrial dilation (10.8%). In univariable analysis, ≥1 sign was associated with male sex, a lower DLCO% predicted, a higher FVC%/DLCO% ratio and a shorter 6MWD; in the multivariable model only, male sex remained independently associated (aOR 3.45, 95% CI 0.99-12.07; p = 0.052). Twelve-month FVC trajectories did not differ by baseline echocardiographic status; nonetheless, ≥1 sign was associated with shorter time to acute exacerbation (log-rank p = 0.007) and all-cause hospitalisation (p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic signs suggestive of increased right-sided afterload are present in a substantial proportion of PPF patients at the time of antifibrotic initiation. They identified patients at higher risk of acute exacerbation and hospitalisation, regardless of FVC decline. This higher-risk subgroup warrants specific pulmonary vascular evaluation and tighter clinical follow-up.

candidates.title: Spatial Neighborhood Construction and NICHES Connectomics for Differential Ligand-Receptor Analysis in Fibrotic Human Lung.
candidates.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables measurement of gene expression within intact tissue architecture, yet most analytical workflows emphasize cell-type classification over cellular interaction. Workflows that do infer intercellular signaling typically aggregate inferred interactions across clusters, regions, or spots, and fix neighborhood definitions, ligand-receptor (LR) databases, and scoring functions that users cannot easily inspect or change. The unmet need is therefore an analysis workflow that preserves signaling inference at the resolution of individual cell-cell pairs, constrains candidate interactions using measured physical distance, and exposes every modeling choice as a user-set parameter. Here, we describe a computational protocol that meets these requirements by inferring LR signaling at cell-cell pair resolution, grounded in physical tissue space, from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data. The workflow defines spatial neighborhoods and constructs a directed connectomics graph in which edges represent the set of inferred LR interactions between cells. Using the NICHES (Niche Interactions and Communication Heterogeneity in Extracellular Signaling) package, three complementary representations are derived: a Cell-to-Cell (C2C) edge-level connectome, a Cell-to-Neighborhood (C2N) outgoing signaling summary, and a Neighborhood-to-Cell (N2C) incoming signaling summary. A parallel Neighborhood Composition assay characterizes the local tissue architecture of the spatial neighborhoods. The framework is modular and tunable: users may adjust neighborhood definitions, select alternative LR databases, and modify scoring and aggregation methods. These node- and edge-aligned data layers support visualization, clustering, and differential analysis of spatially organized signaling patterns. Applied to fibrotic lung tissue, the workflow segregates architecturally defined neighborhoods and identifies differential LR mechanisms that distinguish fibrotic regions from sur

candidates.title: COVID-19 severity and early inflammatory biomarkers in patients with immune-mediated inflammatory rheumatic diseases: a multicenter cohort study.
candidates.abstract: Patients with immune-mediated inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IMIRDs) may be more vulnerable to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection because of underlying immune dysregulation. However, it remains unclear which factors determine coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity in this population, especially in Eastern European settings. We conducted a retrospective, multicenter observational study including 211 patients with IMIRDs diagnosed with COVID-19 between 01.03.2020 and 31.12.2024. We collected clinical, demographic, and laboratory data within the first 72 hours of symptom onset and classified COVID-19 severity into three ordered categories. Associations with severity were examined using separate univariable ordinal logistic regression models and an additional multivariable model including age and IMIRD subtype. The main factors linked to more severe COVID-19 were older age (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.06; 95% confidence interval [CI]:1.03-1.09) and comorbidity burden (OR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.12-1.31). Among patients with available laboratory measurements, higher levels of acute-phase reactants, as well as a higher derived neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (dNLR) (OR = 1.30; 95% CI, 1.10-1.54) and lower monocyte counts (OR = 0.08; 95% CI, 0.02-0.36), remained associated with increased severity after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Accounting for age, patients with SLE had lower odds of greater COVID-19 severity than those with RA (OR = 0.35; 95% CI, 0.13-0.90). COVID-19 severity was associated with age, comorbidity burden, and early inflammatory response, with an age-adjusted difference also observed between SLE and RA. Routine inflammatory parameters and composite indices may contribute to early risk stratification in this population.

candidates.title: Preferential phosphodiesterase inhibition as a novel strategy to modulate key pathways in systemic sclerosis.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a complex autoimmune disease marked by vasculopathy, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. The high disease burden and impact on quality of life highlight the need for therapies that target underlying pathogenic mechanisms rather than merely treating organ-specific symptoms. Phosphodiesterases, including phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B), are key regulators of cellular function and inflammatory responses of several cell types central to SSc pathogenesis. Given PDE4B's broad effects, targeting it may provide benefits beyond organ-specific manifestations and improve current care. Selective PDE4B inhibition represents a novel therapeutic approach for SSc, with improved subtype selectivity compared with earlier pan-PDE4 inhibitors. Nerandomilast preferentially inhibits PDE4B (ninefold over PDE4D), potentially improving tolerability versus oral pan-PDE4 inhibitors by avoiding adverse events such as gastrointestinal intolerance. Preclinical findings in SSc-relevant mouse and cell models show that PDE4B inhibition modulates inflammatory cytokine secretion, smooth muscle cell tension, endothelial and epithelial barrier integrity, and extracellular matrix synthesis under oxidative stress; this suggests nerandomilast could attenuate immune dysregulation, fibrosis, and potentially impact vasculopathy. Two pivotal Phase III trials evaluated nerandomilast in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (FIBRONEER™-IPF; NCT05321069) and progressive pulmonary fibrosis (FIBRONEER™-ILD; NCT05321082), the latter of which included patients with SSc-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD). The ongoing CONQUEST trial (NCT06195072) is investigating the efficacy and safety of various drugs, including nerandomilast, in patients with early active SSc-ILD. This perspective highlights the rationale for targeting PDE4B in SSc therapy and explores preclinical findings in SSc and clinical findings in SSc-ILD to date.

candidates.title: Clinical variables and quantitative CT radiomics for mortality risk stratification after acute exacerbation of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbation (AE) is the most lethal event of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD). This exploratory study compared clinical, radiomics, and combined predictor strategies across five survival-learning algorithms for survival risk stratification.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 78 patients with AE-IIM-ILD and divided them into a training cohort (n = 54; 20 deaths) and a held-out internal testing cohort (n = 24; 9 deaths), stratified by observed mortality event status. Three predictor strategies were evaluated: a clinical strategy comprising PaO2/FiO2 ratio, neutrophil percentage (NEU%), and arthritis-related symptoms; a radiomics strategy comprising two selected radiomics features; and a combined strategy comprising PaO2/FiO2 ratio, arthritis-related symptoms, and a composite radiomics score (Rad-score). Each strategy was evaluated using five survival-learning algorithms. Harrell's concordance index (C-index) was the primary discrimination metric, with mean time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) used as a secondary measure.
RESULTS: During the 1-year follow-up, 29 deaths were observed. Performance rankings varied across predictor strategies, algorithms, and evaluation metrics. The combined-Random Survival Forest configuration demonstrated the highest training-cohort C-index among the 15 configurations. Its mean time-dependent AUC was 0.923 (95% CI: 0.860-0.970) in the training cohort and 0.915 (95% CI: 0.736-0.986) in the testing cohort, with corresponding C-indices of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.803-0.940) and 0.842 (95% CI: 0.673-0.971), respectively. The model stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct observed survival trajectories.

candidates.title: Association of baseline non-severe anemia with clinical outcomes following the first recorded diagnosis of systemic sclerosis: A matched cohort study.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest mortality among systemic autoimmune diseases, yet the prognostic significance of anemia around the time of the first recorded SSc diagnosis is unclear. We examined whether baseline anemia is associated with early mortality and complications. This retrospective matched cohort study identified female adults with a first recorded SSc diagnosis between January 2010 and December 2024 from the TriNetX Research Network. Patients were required to have at least 5 years of pre-index observation without a documented SSc diagnosis. The network comprised 140 healthcare organizations, with approximately 70% of patients in the United States across all 9 census regions and 30% at international sites. Anemia was defined as hemoglobin (Hb) ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL and non-anemia as ≥12.0 g/dL, measured within ±30 days of diagnosis. For the Hb-stratified analysis, the anemia cohort was categorized as Hb ≥10.0 to <12.0 g/dL or ≥8.0 to <10.0 g/dL. One-to-one propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during days 31 to 365 among patients surviving the 30-day landmark period; secondary outcomes were sepsis, acute kidney injury, intensive care unit admission, pulmonary fibrosis, and elevated C-reactive protein (≥10 mg/L). After matching, 5410 patients remained in each cohort. Baseline anemia was significantly associated with higher 1-year mortality (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.99-3.22; P < .001) and with increased risks of sepsis (HR, 3.20; 95% CI, 2.38-4.30), acute kidney injury (HR, 2.24; 95% CI, 1.80-2.78), intensive care unit admission (HR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.47-2.51), and elevated C-reactive protein (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.37-1.74; all P < .001); no significant association was observed for pulmonary fibrosis (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.96-1.17; P = .229). candidates.title: Sarcopenia in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease: A cross-sectional radiological and functional assessment.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) is a significant complication that impairs lung function and increases morbidity. Sarcopenia, characterized by the loss of muscle mass and function, is commonly found in chronic diseases such as systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of sarcopenia in patients with SSc-ILD and investigate its cross-sectional associations with pulmonary function test parameters, estimated pulmonary artery pressure and quantitative radiological lung involvement. In this cross-sectional study conducted between 2024 and 2025, 40 patients with systemic sclerosis (2013 ACR/EULAR criteria) and high-resolution computed tomography-confirmed interstitial lung disease were evaluated. Patients with overlap myositis, acute infections, severe orthopedic/neurological limitations, and end-stage organ failure were excluded. Sarcopenia was diagnosed based on European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 criteria using muscle mass (bioelectrical impedance analysis) and handgrip strength measurements. Pulmonary function tests (FVC, single-breath transfer factor of lung for carbon monoxide), echocardiographic sPAP estimations, and quantitative high-resolution computed tomography lung density analysis were performed. These findings highlight the potential impact of sarcopenia on lung function and the association of sarcopenia with radiological findings in SSc-ILD SSc-ILD. candidates.title: Divergent approaches to rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease: a comparative analysis of international clinical practice guidelines.
candidates.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. We compared international and regional clinical practice guidelines to identify agreement, differences, and gaps in RA-ILD care. We conducted a narrative comparative review of five guideline groups: ERS/EULAR, ACR/CHEST, EULAR, PANLAR, and ALAT. Recommendations were assessed across screening, diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment, together with their methodological approaches. Diagnostic recommendations showed the greatest agreement: ILD-focused guidelines emphasized high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), pulmonary function tests, and multidisciplinary evaluation. Screening recommendations differed: ERS/EULAR and ACR/CHEST favored risk-based assessment, whereas ALAT proposed a broader approach that included lung ultrasound as an adjunct, without replacing HRCT. For established RA-ILD, ACR/CHEST suggested, as implementation guidance, pulmonary function testing every 3-12 months during the first year and HRCT when clinically indicated; ERS/EULAR proposed pulmonary function testing every 3-6 months in the first years and periodic HRCT. Treatment showed the greatest divergence. ACR/CHEST conditionally recommended mycophenolate, rituximab, azathioprine, and cyclophosphamide as first-line ILD therapies, whereas ALAT emphasized integrated control of articular and pulmonary disease, particularly with abatacept or rituximab. EULAR and PANLAR primarily addressed RA treatment and did not provide dedicated RA-ILD algorithms. Antifibrotic treatment was considered mainly in progressive fibrosing disease. Guidelines converge on HRCT-based evaluation but differ in screening, monitoring intervals, and treatment priorities. These differences reflect their scope, methodology, and limited RA-ILD-specific evidence. Prospective comparative studies are needed to inform more consistent care.

candidates.title: Self-reported prevalence of tuberculosis and selected associated vulnerability factors among rural populations in six districts of India: A community-based cross-sectional study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis is a major public health challenge in India, contributing to one-fourth of global burden of TB disease. Comorbidities in uninfected individuals make them vulnerable to TB disease. This study estimates the self-reported prevalence of tuberculosis and selected vulnerability factors (HIV, current smoking, silicosis, occupational silica-dust exposure, diabetes mellitus and persistent cough >2 weeks) among the rural demography of six districts in India, with the aim of informing targeted active case finding under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP).
METHODS: The study conducted was a community-based cross-sectional survey carried out across six districts of India. Two blocks from each district was selected randomly followed by randomly selected villages under each block. A universal sampling technique was followed for including all the households of the randomly selected villages. The data were collected through a pre-tested semi-structured questionnaire schedule via face-to-face interviews at all the eligible households of the study sites. Descriptive analysis was performed, and the results were obtained in the form of frequencies and percentages.
RESULTS: The ultimate data consisted of 82,636 individuals, with males at 52% and females at 47%. 77% of the study population were 15 years of age or older. This study analyzes a large dataset. The TB prevalence was around 150 per lakh of the population, while the prevalence of HIV-reactive individuals, current smokers, silicosis, occupational exposure to silica dust, diabetes mellitus and cough of greater than two weeks is found in 0.9%, 5%, 1.2%, 1.1%, 1.4% and 4% respectively.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: The study highlights TB status and selected TB-vulnerable groups. The study has a large sample size, and it follows multipronged approach to study selected vulnerable population groups. This data may improve targeted active case finding among the high-risk groups as outlined by NTE

candidates.title: Codonopsis tangshen Attenuates Age-Related Pulmonary Fibrosis Through Senescence and Gut-Lung Axis Modulation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cellular senescence is a critical driver of chronic inflammation, tissue remodeling, and progressive fibrosis during the aging process. Codonopsis tangshen Oliv. is a widely used medicinal and edible homologous plant in traditional Chinese medicine; however, its pharmacological effects on natural aging and age-related pulmonary fibrosis, as well as the underlying mechanisms, are still not fully elucidated.
METHODS: C57BL/6J mice were randomly divided into five groups: young control (YCtrl), natural-age control (OCtrl), high-dose CT (H-O-CT, 20.8 g/kg), low-dose CT (L-O-CT, 10.4 g/kg), and positive drug YPF (O-YPF, 20.8 g/kg), with n = 10 per group. A bleomycin-induced cellular senescence model in A549 cells was established in vitro to provide complementary evidence. Additionally, the composition of gut microbiota and the expression of intestinal barrier markers were analyzed to explore potential gut-lung axis involvement.
RESULTS: The results demonstrated that C. tangshen extract significantly decreased the histological and molecular markers of pulmonary senescence, ameliorated multiple lung function parameters, and attenuated age-related pulmonary fibrosis in aged mice. Transcriptomic analysis and protein validation further revealed that these protective effects were associated with modulation of the FBXW7/TPP1 and HSF1/HSP70 signaling pathways. Moreover, the extract reshaped the gut microbiota composition and enhanced the expression of intestinal MUC2 and tight-junction proteins, which supports possible involvement of the gut-lung axis.
CONCLUSIONS: These results highlight the potential of Codonopsis tangshen Oliv. as a promising preclinical treatment for the intervention and management of aging and age-related fibrotic lung injury.

candidates.title: A Balanced Chromosomal Rearrangement Disrupting the Telomerase RNA Component Gene Causes Short Telomere-Mediated Pulmonary Fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Excessive telomere shortening contributes to pulmonary fibrosis (PF), with at least 30% of familial cases attributed to telomere biology disorders (TBDs). However, TBD-associated PF remains underdiagnosed because of unidentified disease-causing mutations and limited referral for telomere and genetic testing. Here, we combined telomeric restriction fragment analysis, telomere analysis by a long-read Nanopore sequencing method (NanoTelSeq), exome sequencing (ES), and optical genome mapping (OGM) to investigate the underlying cause of disease in a family affected by PF, microcephaly, and premature hair graying. We identified a familial balanced translocation associated with short telomeres, which involved a chromosome 3 breakpoint within the non-coding telomerase RNA component (TERC) gene, disrupting the 451-nucleotide telomerase RNA. Establishing the diagnosis enabled a TBD-tailored protocol and successful lung transplantation in the proband at age 49. These findings identified structural disruption of TERC as a previously unrecognized cause of TBD and broadened the genetic landscape of TBD beyond splicing, single nucleotide substitutions, and insertion/deletion variants. Furthermore, they demonatrate the importance of routine telomere length measurement alongside comprehensive genomic testing in familial PF.

candidates.title: Exhaled Breath Analysis for Detection of Interstitial Lung Diseases Using Real-Time PTR-TOF-MS.
candidates.abstract: Interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of diffuse parenchymal lung disorders requiring accurate non-invasive diagnostic approaches. This study evaluated real-time proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry (PTR-TOF-MS) combined with machine learning for breath-based ILD detection and characterization. Overall, 251 patients with ILD and 251 healthy controls underwent analysis of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) during normal quiet breathing and forced expiration. The ILD cohort comprised multiple clinically heterogeneous ILD subtypes. Gradient boosting models were evaluated using repeated Monte Carlo cross-validation, with additional age- and sex-matched validation, ILD subtype classification, and kernel canonical correlation analysis (KCCA). Models incorporating VOCs and demographic variables achieved AUCs of 0.900 and 0.897 for normal and forced breathing, respectively, while VOC-only models retained good discrimination (AUC 0.874 and 0.875). Four VOC-related ions (m/z 55.03859, 63.01996, 90.95284, and 107.0886) were reproducibly identified. Discrimination among individual ILD subtypes was modest, with the highest AUC observed for IPF (0.709). KCCA demonstrated significant associations between VOC signatures and clinical-functional impairment under both breathing conditions. These findings support PTR-TOF-MS breath analysis as a promising non-invasive approach for ILD detection, while subtype classification and disease severity assessment require further independent validation.

candidates.title: Safety and diagnostic yield of transbronchial lung cryobiopsy in patients with interstitial lung disease and severe pulmonary function impairment.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transbronchial lung cryobiopsy (TBLC) has become an established diagnostic modality in interstitial lung disease (ILD). However, current guidelines frequently exclude patients with severely impaired lung function due to safety concerns. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and diagnostic yield of TBLC in patients with advanced pulmonary function impairment.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of consecutive patients with suspected ILD who underwent TBLC for diagnostic evaluation at Thoraxklinik Heidelberg, University Hospital Heidelberg, between November 2017 and December 2021. All cases were reviewed in a multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) before and after biopsy. Severe pulmonary function impairment was defined as a forced vital capacity (FVC) < 50% predicted and/or a diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCOSB) < 35% predicted. Procedural complications and diagnostic yield were assessed following post-procedural MDD.
RESULTS: A total of 396 patients were included (39% female, mean age 68 ± 12 years), of whom 43 patients (10.9%) had severely physiologically impaired ILD (SPI-ILD). The incidence of pneumothorax did not statistically differ between patients with severe and less physiologically impaired ILD (LPI-ILD) (11.6% vs. 14.7%, p = 0.818), with chest tube placement required in 33 cases overall. Severe bleeding necessitating endoscopic haemostasis occurred in 25.6% of SPI-ILD and 17.8% of LPI-ILD patients (p = 0.218). No surgical interventions for procedure-related complications were required. TBLC contributed to a final diagnosis following MDD review in 318 patients (80%), including 81% in SPI-ILD and 80% in LPI-ILD (p = 1.000).
CONCLUSION: TBLC may represent a viable diagnostic option in carefully selected patients with severely impaired pulmonary function when performed in experienced centres following thorough risk-benefit assessment.

candidates.title: [Systemic sclerosis with anti-human neutrophil cytoplasm antibody associated vasculitis: A case report].
candidates.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is an autoimmune disease involving microvessels and a wide range of connective tissues. Anti-human neutrophil cytoplasm antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) is a primary, systemic necrotizing small vasculitis. The coexistence of AAV and SSc is rare. We report a case of SSc combined with AAV complicated with alveolar hemorrhage, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and cerebral hemorrhage. The patient was a 56-year-old woman with a 20-year history of Raynaud phenomenon, skin sclerosis on the fingertip and face. She developed dry cough for 1 year and shortness of breath after activity for 1month. Blood routine test showed moderate anemia, blood biochemistry showed renal function damage, and urine routine test showed positive urine protein and occult blood. Immunological examination showed that anti-topoisomerase Ⅰ (anti-SCL-70) antibody was positive. Lung CT showed interstitial fibrosis in both lower lungs. Systemic sclerosis and chronic renal injury were diagnosed and she was treated with low-dose prednisone and nifedipine. During the treatment, the patient developed rapidly progressive renal insufficiency, immunological indicator showed positive anti-myeloperoxidase antibody (MPO), and renal pathology suggested crescentic glomerulonephritis. The renal damage was considered to be caused by vasculitis, and the diagnosis was modified as systemic sclerosis complicated with AAV, with crescentic nephritis and interstitial lung disease. She was treated with methylprednisolone 500 mg. One day later, the patient developed hemoptysis, alveolar hemorrhage was considered, and treatment was adjusted to methylprednisolone 1 g for 3 days, plasma exchange and cyclophosphamide. Three days later, she had vomiting coffee-colored gastric contents and melena. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage was considered, and methylprednisolone was reduced to 80 mg. candidates.title: [Clinical characteristics of primary Sjögren syndrome with leukopenia].
candidates.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the clinical characteristics of leukopenia in a large cohort of patients with primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS), to discuss its pathogenic mechanism, and to enhance clinicians ' understanding of the disease, and reduce missed diagnosis and misdiagnosis.
METHODS: A total of 401 inpatients and outpatients who were initially diagnosed with pSS at the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, Ninth People' s Hospital, Shanghai Jiaotong University School of Medicine, from November 2019 to March 2023 were selected for this study. The clinical data and laboratory examinations of these patients were analyzed retrospectively.
RESULTS: Of the 401 patients, 107 (26.68%) were complicated with blood leukopenia. The reasons for the first diagnosis were analyzed. The patients with leukopenia had a lower xerostomia and xerophthalmia (39.25% vs. 54.76%, P=0.006), but a higher incidence of fatigue (26.17% vs. 12.59%, P=0.001) and thrombocytopenia (11.21% vs. 2.72%, P=0.001) than those without leukopenia. There were no significant differences in arthralgia, oral ulcer, caries, chest tightness, asthma and anemia between the two groups (P>0.05). The laboratory test indicators were analyzed. The patients with leukopenia had a higher prevalence of anti-SSA/Ro52+ (81.31% vs. 68.35%, P=0.040), anti-SSB+ (47.66% vs. 28.57%, P < 0.001), immunoglobulin G (IgG)+ (68.22% vs. 51.02%, P=0.002), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) elevation (67.29% vs. 41.32%, P=0.001), and thrombocytopenia (22.43% vs. 13.27%, P=0.026) than those without leukopenia. There were no significant differences in antinuclear antibody (ANA)+, anti-SSA/Ro60+, centromere protein B(CENP-B)+, rheumatoid factor (RF)+, and anemia between the two groups (P>0.05).
