candidates.title: Clinical characteristics and severity classification in mixed connective tissue disease: a nationwide retrospective study.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize clinical manifestations, major organ involvement, real-world treatment patterns and factors associated with severity classification in Japanese patients with mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), aiming to clarify its heterogeneous clinical spectrum.
METHODS: This nationwide retrospective multicentre study analyzed clinical data from 249 patients who strictly fulfilled the 2019 Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare diagnostic criteria for MCTD, derived from an initial real-world registry of 311 clinically diagnosed patients. Clinical features, autoantibodies and therapeutic regimens were summarized and compared between patients with severe vs nonsevere disease.
RESULTS: The cohort was 93.1% female (median onset age 40.6 years). Common findings, specifically Raynaud's phenomenon and/or swelling of the fingers or dorsum of the hands, were present in 100%. Phenotypically, an overlap of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-like and systemic sclerosis (SSc)-like features was most frequent (56.0%), while 32.0% had manifestations across all three phenotypic domains (SLE-, SSc- and IIM-like). Major organ involvement occurred in 32.9% of patients, including pulmonary arterial hypertension in 12.8%. Approximately 28.7% of evaluable patients were classified as severe. Off-scale-high anti-U1-RNP antibody status was not associated with severity classification (P = 0.492) or with broad phenotypic categories. Glucocorticoids and immunosuppressive agents were used in 66.7% and 56.5% of the patients, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Mixed connective tissue disease exhibits marked clinical heterogeneity. Severity classification was not associated with off-scale-high anti-U1-RNP antibody status or broad phenotypic categories. These findings support rigorous cardiopulmonary screening and management tailored to the dominant clinical phenotype.

candidates.title: Spinal Cord and Nerve Root Involvement in Histiocytic Neoplasms: A Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Histiocytic neoplasms, including Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD), Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH), and Rosai-Dorfman-Destombes disease (RDD), have frequent nervous system involvement. The aim of this study was to characterize the neurologic, radiologic, and laboratory features of spinal cord and nerve root involvement in histiocytic neoplasms.
METHODS: We evaluated patients with biopsy-proven ECD, LCH, or RDD seen at a tertiary referral center between January 1996 and December 2024. Patients were included if spinal MRI demonstrated spinal cord or nerve root involvement. Spinal MRI was performed for evaluation of myelopathic or radicular symptoms or as part of staging in patients with CNS involvement. We collected demographic variables, neurologic syndromes and imaging patterns, treatment characteristics, and outcomes including disability (Expanded Disability Status Scale [EDSS] score) and ambulatory status. The primary outcome was neurologic disability at nadir and last follow-up; secondary outcomes included radiographic patterns and clinical response to treatment. Data were summarized descriptively, with exploratory group comparisons performed using parametric or nonparametric tests as appropriate.
RESULTS: Among 415 patients with ECD (n = 183), LCH (n = 144), or RDD (n = 88), spinal cord or nerve root involvement was identified in 42 (ECD, 27; LCH, 4; RDD, 11). The median age at onset was 43.1 years (interquartile range 32.1-58.5), and 18 (43%) were female. Most cases were symptomatic (36/42, 86%), with myelopathy as the first neurologic manifestation in 26 (72%). Parenchymal infiltration predominated in the ECD group (17/27, 63%), compared with LCH (2/4, 50%) and RDD (2/11, 18%) groups (Fisher exact test across groups, p = 0.035). Root involvement was more frequent in the RDD group (8/11, 73%) than in the ECD (7/27, 26%) or LCH (1/4, 25%) group (Fisher exact test across groups, p = 0.021). candidates.title: Expert intuition vs. Algorithmic clustering: Mapping radiological subtypes in pulmonary sarcoidosis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary sarcoidosis is a heterogeneous granulomatous disease with a broad spectrum of clinical and radiological manifestations. While the traditional Scadding classification based on chest radiography remains a cornerstone of disease staging, it provides limited information regarding parenchymal involvement and poorly correlates with functional impairment. High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) offers superior sensitivity in detecting subtle and early interstitial changes, yet standardized HRCT-based classification systems for sarcoidosis remain underdeveloped.
AIM: This study aimed to propose and validate a novel HRCT-based classification of pulmonary sarcoidosis grounded in expert consensus, to assess its relationship with clinical symptoms, pulmonary function, and quality of life, and to compare it with data-driven radiological groupings obtained through cluster analysis.
METHODS: The study population included patients with confirmed pulmonary sarcoidosis managed at a tertiary referral center, either as inpatients or outpatients. HRCT scans were evaluated using a modified version of the previously published questionnaire, capturing 22 radiological features per lung lobe. Based on characteristic imaging patterns, four expert-defined subtypes were proposed: (1) Lymphonodal, (2) Disseminated-Nodular, (3) Central, and (4) Fibrotic. Symptom burden was assessed using the Fatigue Assessment Scale (FAS) and the Sarcoidosis Health Questionnaire (SHQ). Spirometric and gas transfer parameters (FEV1, FVC, TL,CO) were recorded. Statistical analyses included ANOVA, Spearman's correlation, and hierarchical clustering (Ward's method with Euclidean distances), with Cohen's kappa used to evaluate concordance between classification systems.

candidates.title: Efficacy and Safety of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors for Lung Cancer Complicated by Interstitial Pneumonia: The CS-Lung 003 Study, Branch Number 28.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve the prognosis of patients with previously treated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the efficacy and safety of ICIs for patients with NSCLC complicated with interstitial pneumonia (IP) remain unknown. This study aimed to analyze patients with NSCLC and IP treated with ICIs and to investigate the efficacy and exacerbation frequency of ICI therapy.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled patients with NSCLC and IP at multiple centers and examined progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) using the Kaplan-Meier method.
RESULTS: The median PFS was 5.8 months, and the median OS was 9.7 months. ICI-related lung injury was observed in seven of the 19 patients (36.8%). Pneumonitis was observed in one of five patients with a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern and in six of 14 patients with a non-UIP pattern; however, there was no significant difference in onset frequency. Furthermore, we observed no significant difference in PFS between patients with and without ICI-related pneumonitis (6.8 vs. 3.3 months, respectively; p = 0.826). OS tended to be shorter in patients with ICI-related pneumonitis, but the difference was not significant (8.0 vs. 16.7 months, respectively; p = 0.172).
CONCLUSIONS: The use of ICIs in patients with NSCLC and IP produces long-term responses in some cases; however, there is a high possibility of ICI-related pneumonitis. In cases where the condition worsens, post-treatment may be difficult, and the prognosis may be poor.

candidates.title: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease: immune profiling and correlation of immune cells with pulmonary function in SSc-ILD.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Connective tissue diseases (CTDs) frequently involve the lungs, with CTD-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD) representing a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, yet the immunopathological mechanisms remain incompletely defined. This study characterized immune profiles in CTD-ILD and their association with pulmonary function impairment, focusing on systemic sclerosis-associated ILD (SSc-ILD).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 217 CTD-ILD patients, 100 healthy controls, and 25 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. Peripheral lymphocyte subsets, immunoglobulins, complements, and cytokines were assessed using flow cytometry and immunoturbidimetry. Lung function was evaluated by standard spirometry and gas transfer tests.
RESULTS: Compared to healthy controls, lymphocyte counts were reduced in all ILD subtypes, lowest in polymyositis/dermatomyositis (PM/DM)-ILD. In SSc-ILD, T cell and helper T cell (Th) percentages were significantly elevated (76.2% and 49.39%, respectively). Complement C3 was lower in Sjögren's syndrome (SS)-ILD (889.92 vs. 965.49 mg/L), and C4 was significantly lower in SSc-ILD (196.74 vs. 226.70 mg/L) versus controls. SSc-ILD patients with higher Th cell proportions exhibited worse pulmonary function, with expiratory reserve volume (ERV) falling 57.21%, maximal vital capacity (VC max) 18.81%, functional residual capacity (FRC) 19.64%, forced vital capacity (FVC)17.93%, and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) 20.28%. Continuous correlation analysis further confirmed significant negative correlations between Th cell proportions and ERV, FRC, and PCO2.
CONCLUSION: Peripheral blood immune profiling revealed distinct abnormalities across CTD-ILD subtypes. Peripheral Th cell expansion is strongly associated with lung function decline in SSc-ILD, highlighting the potential of Th cells as biomarkers of disease progression in SSc-ILD.

candidates.title: Histopathologic Assessment of Pulmonary Capillaritis Using Combined Immunohistochemical and Special Stains: An Autopsy Case Double-Positive for MPO-ANCA and Anti-GBM Antibodies.
candidates.abstract: Anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) disease may coexist with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), a clinicopathologic entity termed double-positive disease, in which diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) is common but histologic confirmation of pulmonary capillaritis remains difficult. A 93-year-old woman presented with rapidly progressive renal failure, and serologic evaluation revealed markedly elevated myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA and anti-GBM antibody levels. Despite corticosteroid therapy, the patient died of progressive renal failure. At autopsy, the kidneys demonstrated diffuse crescentic glomerulonephritis with linear IgG deposition along the glomerular basement membrane, consistent with anti-GBM nephritis, together with multiple cortical scars composed of clusters of globally sclerotic glomeruli and interstitial fibrosis. The lungs exhibited DAH with focal neutrophilic infiltration along the alveolar septa, accompanied by focal destruction of capillary walls with subtle leukocytoclasia. Immunohistochemical analysis using epithelial marker (cytokeratin AE1/AE3), endothelial markers (CD31, CD34, and ERG), and platelet markers (CD61 and CD42b) highlighted alveolar epithelial injury, loss of endothelial continuity, and extravascular platelet deposition, respectively, in areas where capillaritis was suspected. Spatial concordance of these findings supported the presence of structural injury associated with pulmonary capillaritis. This case highlights the diagnostic importance of rigorous histopathologic assessment complemented by combined immunohistochemistry in patients with DAH.

candidates.title: Circulating inflammatory mediators CCL2 and CXCL16 as biomarkers in Iraqi women infected with toxoplasmosis.
candidates.abstract: The protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii is the cause of the widespread but sometimes disregarded parasitic illness toxoplasmosis. Cytokines play an indispensable role in fostering an environment that is more conducive to pregnancy. Their intricate network of interactions allows for the observation of numerous modulatory consequences, such as cell migration, invasion, and gene expression. Among these, CCL2 (MCP-1) and CXCL16 have emerged as promising immunological biomarkers reflecting disease activity, inflammation, and tissue involvement. Monocyte chemotactic protein 1 (MCP-1), another name for C-C motif ligand 2 (CCL2), is a crucial chemotactic factor that attracts macrophages for the immunological response. CXCL16 is a unique chemokine that can be found in both transmembrane and soluble forms. Numerous inflammatory conditions in humans, such as interstitial lung disease, rheumatoid arthritis, vascular disease, and hepatic injury, have been linked to CXCL16 expression. This study aimed to evaluate the correlation between T. gondii seropositivity and concentrations of plasma markers (CCL2 and CXCL16) in Iraqi pregnant women. This study comprised 68 serum samples of Iraqi women, attended Al-Yarmouk Teaching Hospital, Baghdad. The levels of CCL2 and CXCL16 were measured using sandwich ELISA. Results of circulatory marker levels revealed a significant variation across all groups. Also, results revealed that the chemokines CCL2 and CXCL16 showed distinct timing in their concentrations throughout pregnancy. Their higher levels in late pregnancy among healthy pregnancies suggested a normal immune adaptation, while their elevated early levels in aborted cases may signal inflammatory processes linked to pregnancy loss. In conclusion, these results indicated that CCL2 and CXCL16 could serve as immunological biomarkers for monitoring pregnancy progression and identifying risk of pregnancy loss.

candidates.title: Nintedanib-induced Glomerular Microangiopathy after Long-term Nintedanib Administration Presenting with Nephrotic Syndrome.
candidates.abstract: We herein report a rare case of nintedanib-induced glomerular microangiopathy (GMA) in a 77-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The patient developed nephrotic-range proteinuria (5.9 g/gCr) after 29 months of nintedanib therapy. A kidney biopsy confirmed GMA, which was characterized by endothelial injury without immune complex deposition. The discontinuation of nintedanib led to a significant reduction in proteinuria. This case demonstrates that nintedanib-induced GMA can manifest after long-term use. Given the potential for a global underdiagnosis, regular urinalysis testing is therefore essential for the early detection of irreversible renal damage, particularly in elderly patients.

candidates.title: Global emergence of novel genotypes and antifungal resistance in Trichosporon asahii revealed by IGS1 rDNA revision.
candidates.abstract: Trichosporon asahii is a basidiomycetous yeast-like fungus that emerged as the main cause of invasive trichosporonosis, exhibiting high mortality rates. Species and genotype identification rely on sequencing of the IGS1 rDNA. By examining sequences in public genomic repositories and compiling epidemiological and antifungal data from the literature, we investigated the emergence of novel genotypes (G) and their relation to antifungal resistance. We analyzed 916 sequences from 892 isolates collected from 1911 to 2024. Genotypic analysis confirmed 14 reference genotypes and described 25 novel genotypes. Geographic distribution revealed a ubiquitous presence of T. asahii in 19 territories and the prevalence of G1 worldwide. Most sequences originated from blood and urine isolates, with the prevalence of G1 in all sampled sites, G4 in respiratory isolates, and G7 in urine. Minimal inhibitory concentration analyses showed G3 and G7 with the highest geometric mean (GM) values for voriconazole (VRC), while G4 presented the highest for posaconazole (POS). Non-wild-type isolates appeared across major genotypes. Bloodstream isolates showed higher GM values and more non-wild-type isolates for fluconazole and VRC, whereas urine isolates exhibited elevated GM values for VRC and POS. Overall, our findings reveal expanded IGS1 diversity and associate G3, G4, and G7 to reduced triazole susceptibility, highlighting the need for genotype-based surveillance.

candidates.title: Nintedanib in progressive fibrosing hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Real-world effects on lung function and survival.
candidates.abstract: BackgroundFibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (f-HP) may progress despite antigen avoidance and immunosuppressive therapy. Although nintedanib is approved for progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF), real-world evidence regarding its effectiveness and safety in f-HP, particularly when combined with immunosuppression, remains limited.ObjectivesTo compare lung function trajectories, survival, and treatment safety in patients with progressive f-HP treated with nintedanib plus immunosuppressive therapy versus immunosuppressive therapy alone.DesignRetrospective, single-center cohort study with a historical control group.MethodsPatients with a multidisciplinary diagnosis of f-HP who fulfilled the INBUILD criteria for PPF were included. Patients treated with nintedanib were compared with patients managed with immunosuppressive therapy alone. Longitudinal changes in forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) over 24 months were analysed using linear mixed-effects models. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression.ResultsA total of 106 patients were included, of whom 54 received nintedanib and 52 received immunosuppressive therapy alone. Baseline characteristics were broadly comparable between groups. No statistically significant differences were observed in FVC or DLCO trajectories over 24 months, although a modest numerical trend towards relative FVC stabilisation was observed in the nintedanib group. Median survival from disease progression was longer in nintedanib-treated patients than in those not receiving antifibrotic therapy (178 vs 78 months; log-rank p = 0.001). In multivariable analysis, nintedanib use remained independently associated with improved survival (p = 0.013). Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with nintedanib but were generally mild to moderate, and treatment discontinuation due to intolerance occurred in 7.4% of patients.ConclusionIn this rea

candidates.title: [Effects of Qingzao Jiufei Decoction on bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis via JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway-mediated polarization of M2 macrophages].
candidates.journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
candidates.abstract: This study investigated the effects of Qingzao Jiufei Decoction on M2 macrophage polarization in bleomycin(BLM)-induced pulmonary fibrosis(PF) mice via the janus kinase 1(JAK1)/signal transducer and activator of transcription 6(STAT6) signaling pathway. Sixty C57BL/BJ mice were randomly divided into normal group, model group, pirfenidone group(200 mg·kg~(-1)), and low-, medium-, and high-dose Qingzao Jiufei Decoction groups(4.9, 9.8, and 19.6 g·kg~(-1)). The PF model was established in the model and treatment groups by intratracheal instillation of BLM(5 mg·kg~(-1)). Mice in each group were administered the same volume of normal saline or the corresponding dose of Qingzao Jiufei Decoction by gavage for 21 consecutive days. After 21 days, blood gas analysis was performed. ELISA was used to detect the levels of interleukin-4(IL-4), interleukin-13(IL-13), arginase-1(Arg-1), transforming growth factor-β(TGF-β), and interleukin-10(IL-10) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid(BALF). HE and Masson staining were performed to observe pathological changes in lung tissue and for histopathological scoring. Immunofluorescence staining was used to detect the expression of α-smooth muscle actin(α-SMA), type Ⅰ collagen(COL-1), the macrophage marker CD11b, and the M2 macrophage marker CD206. Western blot and RT-qPCR were used to detect the expression of JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway-related proteins and mRNA, as well as M2 macrophage-related proteins and mRNA, in lung tissue. The results showed that, compared with the normal group, the levels of IL-4, IL-13, Arg-1, TGF-β, and IL-10 in BALF were significantly increased in the model group(P<0.01). Histopathological staining revealed extensive inflammatory cell infiltration and increased collagen fiber deposition in the alveolar septa, accompanied by significantly increased Szapiel alveolitis scores and Ashcroft fibrosis scores(P<0.01). Immunofluorescence staining showed significantly increased fluorescence intensity of α-SMA, COL-1, CD

candidates.title: [Mechanism of action of steamed Polygonati Rhizoma in ameliorating pulmonary fibrosis in mice based on PI3K/AKT signaling pathway].
candidates.journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
candidates.abstract: This paper aims to investigate the therapeutic effect and mechanism of steamed Polygonati Rhizoma on pulmonary fibrosis in mice. A mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis was established and treated with steamed Polygonati Rhizoma water decoction by gavage. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated through histopathological observation of lung tissue, assessment of fibrosis severity, determination of lung hydroxyproline(HYP) content, and measurement of inflammatory cytokines(IL-1β and TNF-α) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. The targets of active components in steamed Polygonati Rhizoma were predicted using the Swiss Target Prediction database. Disease-related targets of pulmonary fibrosis were obtained from the GeneCard and OMIM databases, followed by intersection analysis with the targets of active components using the Venny 2.1.0 platform. The target network and protein-protein interaction(PPI) network were constructed. Key pathways were screened through KEGG pathway enrichment analysis. The expression levels of collagen Ⅰ, fibronectin, phosphorylated AKT(p-AKT), and phosphorylated PI3K(p-PI3K) proteins in lung tissue were detected by immunofluorescence and Western blot. RESULTS:: show that a total of 12 active components and 319 predicted targets were screened from Polygonati Rhizoma. After intersecting with 6 308 pulmonary fibrosis-related targets, 245 common targets were obtained. KEGG enrichment analysis identified the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway as the core pathway. In vivo experiments confirmed that steamed Polygonati Rhizoma significantly alleviated pathological damage in the lung tissue, reduced HYP content, suppressed inflammatory cytokine levels, and down-regulated the expression levels of collagen Ⅰ and fibronectin. Flavonoid components, such as 4',5-dihydroxyflavone and baicalein, were speculated to be potentially associated with these therapeutic effects. These findings indicate that steamed Polygonati Rhizoma exerts anti-pulmonary fibrosis effects by regulating th

candidates.title: [Supramolecular differences and pulmonary protective activity of Forsythiae Fructus-Lonicerae Japonicae Flos herb pair prepared with green Forsythiae Fructus and ripe Forsythiae Fructus].
candidates.journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
candidates.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the supramolecular differences arising from the herb pair Forsythiae Fructus-Lonicerae Japonicae Flos(LF) prepared with green Forsythiae Fructus( GF) versus ripe Forsythiae Fructus( RF), and to elucidate their respective pulmonary protective activities. The macroscopic morphology, chemical composition, and in vitro biological activities including antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti-fibrotic effects(specifically the inhibition of TGF-β1-induced fibroblast hyperproliferation and collagen deposition) were systematically compared between GF-LF and RF-LF co-decoctions. The results revealed significant morphological distinctions: the GF-LF co-decoction exhibited higher turbidity and self-assembled spherical supramolecular particles with a diameter of approximately 1 μm, whereas the RF-LF co-decoction formed smaller particles with a diameter ranging from 400 to 600 nm. HPLC and UPLC-MS/MS analyses indicated that both co-decoctions exhibited qualitatively similar phytochemical profiles. However, quantitative differences were evident: GF-LF showed higher content of forsythoside A, phillyrin, and rutin, while RF-LF exhibited higher levels of chlorogenic acid and phillygenin. Biological activity assays demonstrated that GF-LF possessed significantly stronger antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti-fibrotic activities than RF-LF. This study reveals, at the supramolecular level, that the differences in component content between GF and RF drive distinct self-assembly behaviors in the decocting with LF, consequently influencing their pulmonary protective efficacy. These findings provide an experimental basis for the rational clinical selection of Forsythiae Fructus specifications.

candidates.title: Experiences of palliative care for patients with pulmonary fibrosis: A qualitative exploration of patients and partners perspectives.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis is often a progressive disease associated with reduced life expectancy and quality of life. Palliative care aims to optimize quality of life for both patients and their informal caregivers. So far, multiple studies have shown unmet palliative care needs in patients with pulmonary fibrosis. This study explores the experiences and needs of patients with pulmonary fibrosis and their partners to identify opportunities for improving palliative care.
METHODS: A qualitative study was performed with focus groups and individual semi-structured interviews with patients and their informal caregivers. Data collection and analysis were performed iteratively. A reflexive thematic analysis was performed, following the methods of Braun and Clarke.
RESULTS: In total, fifteen patients and 10 informal caregivers participated. One focus group, 13 individual interviews, and 5 dyadic interviews were performed. Two themes were generated: 'See me as a person', and 'Guide me through the trajectory' with both two subthemes, reflecting the patient and partner perspectives. Patients seek recognition beyond their disease, valuing empathy, open communication, and holistic care. At the same time, both patients and partners express the need for clear guidance and support throughout the medical journey, from diagnosis to end of life care, including emotional, practical, and logistical aspects.
CONCLUSIONS/DISCUSSION: Patients and partners experience a 'one-size-fits-all' approach to care and reveal several gaps that can be improved. Patients expressed the importance of being acknowledged as a person beyond the disease and being supported in navigating care and anticipating future needs. Partners highlighted the need to be valued and to receive information that enables them to provide care and maintain a sense of control and security.

candidates.title: Polystyrene-associated pulmonary fibrosis: a summary based on the available evidence and prospects.
candidates.abstract: Microplastics have become a pervasive component of the atmosphere and of indoor and occupational air, and the human respiratory tract is now recognized as a major and largely unavoidable route of exposure. Polystyrene, one of the most abundant commodity plastics, is a dominant model and real-world airborne microplastic, and mounting evidence links inhaled polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) to a spectrum of pulmonary injuries that increasingly implicate fibrogenesis. This review synthesizes the current mechanistic understanding of how PS-MPs may contribute to pulmonary fibrosis, drawing primarily on preclinical experimental evidence. We first outline the sources, physicochemical determinants and respiratory deposition behavior of airborne PS-MPs, and summarize the human, epidemiological and experimental evidence for pulmonary accumulation and harm. On the basis of converging but heterogeneous evidence we propose, as a working model rather than a validated cascade, that these upstream disruptions converge on a shared profibrotic signaling hub - coupled Wnt/β-catenin and TGF-β1/Smad2/3 signaling - that orchestrates epithelial-mesenchymal transition, myofibroblast differentiation and extracellular matrix remodeling, with epigenetic and ncRNA programs stabilizing the fibrotic phenotype. Because the elements of this model rest on different levels of evidence, we grade each of them explicitly as direct PS-MP pulmonary evidence, evidence extrapolated from other particles or toxicants, or canonical fibrosis biology. No study has yet tested the complete cascade, or the causal ordering of its modules, within a single PS-MPs inhalation model. Finally, we appraise candidate therapeutic strategies, including antioxidant and ferroptosis directed approaches and repurposing of approved antifibrotics. Meanwhile, we delineate the methodological limitations including nonphysiological doses, pristi5ne monodisperse particles and short exposure windows, that must be resolved before human

candidates.title: Research progress on molecular mechanisms and signaling pathways of toxic metal exposure-induced lung fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Toxic metal exposure is a pressing global health concern, with accumulating evidence linking it to the onset and progression of pulmonary fibrosis. Mechanistically, metal-induced pulmonary fibrosis operates through a complex, interconnected signaling network rather than a single linear cascade. The initiating role of oxidative stress and the central hub function of the transforming growth factor-β/Smad (TGF-β/Smad) pathway are well-established, whereas the contributions of non-canonical mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt), Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), and mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) pathways are supported by varying degrees of preclinical evidence, with some crosstalk mechanisms remaining largely hypothetical. Concurrently, persistent Toll-like receptor 4/nuclear factor kappa-B/NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3)-driven inflammation, macrophage polarization imbalance, impaired autophagy-lysosomal function, and non-apoptotic cell death pathways including ferroptosis and pyroptosis collectively promote alveolar epithelial injury, fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. We summarize current therapeutic strategies-ranging from antioxidant/anti-inflammatory agents and TGF-β/autophagy modulators to metal chelators and emerging stem cell/nanomedicine approaches-and highlight their preclinical promise and translational challenges. Major unresolved issues include the translational gap between animal models and real-world human exposure scenarios, controversies over mixed-metal dose-response thresholds, and insufficient understanding of feedback and compensatory mechanisms within the molecular network. We outline future research directions aimed at bridging these gaps, with the goal of establishing a comprehensive theoretical framework for early warning, precision diagn

candidates.title: Eculizumab in rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis: a case-series report.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical outcomes and safety profile of eculizumab as adjunctive therapy in a case series of patients with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) due to anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) disease and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV).
METHODS: We reported 7 patients with AAV and 5 patients with anti-GBM disease who presented to our center between March 2025 and January 2026. All patients received eculizumab (900 mg, 1-4 doses) in addition to standard immunosuppressive therapy. Serum creatinine (Scr), urinary red blood cell (uRBC) count, urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR), and dialysis dependence were assessed at baseline and at 3 months. Adverse events were monitored throughout follow-up.
RESULTS: In AAV patients, mean Scr decreased from 407.38 μmol/L to 231.27 μmol/L (p = 0.025), mean uRBC from 384.27/μL to 68.75/μL (p = 0.033), and mean UPCR from 2.20 g/g to 1.64 g/g (p = 0.179) at the 3rd month. In anti-GBM patients, mean Scr declined from 575.07 μmol/L to 263.80 μmol/L (p = 0.024), mean uRBC from 1648.60/μL to 461.92/μL (p = 0.132), and mean UPCR from 10.88 g/g to 3.75 g/g (p = 0.126). At baseline, 6 patients required renal replacement therapy, and after treatment, 4 became dialysis-independent. One AAV patient progressed to hemodialysis, and one anti-GBM patient remained dialysis-dependent. All anti-GBM antibodies and MPO-ANCA (except one patient) seroconverted to negative at month 3. During follow-up, only one case of COVID-19 infection and one oral ulcer were recorded; no severe infections occurred.
CONCLUSION: In this descriptive case series, we observed trends toward improved renal function and hematuria at 3 months in patients with severe RPGN who received eculizumab in addition to standard immunosuppression, with earlier initiation and milder baseline renal impairment appearing to correlate with more favorable outcomes. Nevertheless, the lack of a control group and the marked inte

candidates.title: Extracellular RNA clearance by non-canonical cell-surface MDA5 protects against lung fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: The role of innate immune receptors, specifically RNA sensors, in non-pathogen-driven lung fibrosis remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that the cytosolic RNA sensor MDA5 could translocate to the cell surface upon bleomycin-induced damage. MDA5-deficient mice exhibited exacerbated lung fibrosis with increased IL-17A⁺ γδ T cells and neutrophils, which is independent of the canonical MAVS pathway and type I interferon signaling. Phenotypically, MDA5-deficient lung CD11b⁺ macrophages, which resemble human SPP1⁺ macrophages, showed elevated expression of CCR2 ligands. Mechanistically, cell-surface MDA5 acts as a scavenger receptor that captures extracellular self-RNA and shuttles it for lysosomal degradation. Loss of MDA5 leads to aberrant cellular RNA accumulation, triggering TLR8-dependent hyperproduction of CCR2 ligands. Analysis of human lung fibrosis samples from public datasets revealed SPP1⁺ macrophages are a major source of CCR2 ligands, suggesting their potential to activate monocytes. Our findings reveal an unrecognized protective function of MDA5 in lung fibrosis: preventing TLR8-mediated hyperinflammation through the lysosomal clearance of extracellular RNA. This mechanism provides crucial insights into the pathogenesis of fibrotic diseases like interstitial lung diseases.

candidates.title: Nedd4L-mediated stabilization of morphogenetic protein receptor 2 in lung fibroblasts confers protection against pulmonary fibrosis.
candidates.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is an interstitial lung disease that advances over time and is ultimately life-threatening. Despite advances in antifibrotic therapies, disease progression remains largely unavoidable, highlighting the necessity for advancing mechanistic research and identifying new therapeutic options. Bone morphogenetic protein receptor 2 (BMPR2) is a key receptor for BMP signaling and exerts potent antifibrotic role in lung fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms regulating BMPR2 protein stability in fibrotic lungs remain poorly understood. In this study, we identify that the E3 ubiquitin ligase neural precursor cell expressed developmentally downregulated protein 4-like (Nedd4L) as a critical regulator of BMPR2 stability in lung fibroblasts. BMPR2 levels are markedly reduced in lung fibroblasts derived from patients with IPF and in lung tissues from experimental lung fibrosis models. Mechanically, elevated lipid peroxidation in fibrotic lungs induces K48-linked ubiquitination of BMPR2, leading to its degradation and attenuation of BMPs-induced Smad1/5 phosphorylation. Notably, Nedd4L overexpression counteracts lipid peroxidation-induced BMPR2 degradation and promotes BMPs/BMPR2 signaling by shifting BMPR2 ubiquitination toward a stabilizing K63-linked polyubiquitination in lung fibroblasts. We further show that Nedd4L is regulated through threonine phosphorylated by Raf1 kinase in response to increased lipid peroxidation. In vivo, fibroblast-Nedd4L-deficient mice exacerbates experimental lung fibrosis, which is significantly alleviated by BMPR2 overexpression. Collectively, our findings reveal a previously unrecoganized regulatory mechanism of BMPR2 degradation in fibrotic lungs and indicate that stabilizing BMPR2 in lung fibroblasts may represent a promising approach for the treatment of lung fibrosis.

candidates.title: [Herbal cake-separated moxibustion combined with Bufei Tongluo decoction in treatment of diabetes-induced pulmonary fibrosis of qi-yin deficiency with blood stagnation: a randomized controlled trial].
candidates.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To observe the clinical efficacy of herbal cake-separated moxibustion combined with Bufei Tongluo decoction on diabetes-induced pulmonary fibrosis (DiPF) of qi-yin deficiency with blood stagnation.
METHODS: A total of 102 DiPF patients were randomly divided into an observation group (51 cases, 1 case dropped out) and a control group (51 cases, 1 case was eliminated and 1 case dropped out). In the control group, Bufei Tongluo decoction was administered, one dose per day; and in the observation group, herbal cake-separated moxibustion was operated at Danzhong (CV17) and bilateral Feishu (BL13), Gaohuang (BL43), Zusanli (ST36), etc. on the basis of the treatment in the control group, once every two days, three times a week. The interventions in the two groups were operated continuously for 8 weeks. The TCM symptom score, high-resolution CT (HRCT) score, the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), the indexes of pulmonary function test (the percentage of measured values of the total lung capacity [TLC], forced vital capacity [FVC], and lung carbon monoxide diffusion capacity [DLCO] relative to predicted values), and the levels of serological markers (hydroxyproline [Hyp], interleukin-10 [IL-10] and transforming growth factor-β [TGF-β]) were compared before and after treatment in the twogroups. The clinical efficacy and safety of both groups were evaluated.
RESULTS: After treatment, the scores of each symptom (dry cough with little phlegm, shortness of breath and fatigue, dry mouth and throat, feverish sensations in the palms and soles, and stabbing pain in the chest and hypochondriac region) and the total scores of TCM syndrome, HRCT scores, and the levels of serum Hyp, IL-10, and TGF-β in both groups decreased in comparison with those before treatment (P<0.05); and the scores of dry cough with little phlegm, shortness of breath and fatigue, stabbing pain in the chest and hypochondriac region, the total score of TCM syndrome, HRCT score, the levels of serum IL-10 and TGF-

candidates.title: [Pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung diseases: current state of the art].
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung diseases (PH-ILD) is a common and severe complication of interstitial lung diseases. Diagnosis is challenging and relies on a combination of clinical, functional, biological, radiological and echocardiographic findings. Definitive diagnosis is established by right heart catheterisation, which confirms the presence of pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension associated with increased pulmonary vascular resistance. Until 2021, and the INCREASE study, all randomised controlled trials evaluating therapies approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension in patients with PH-ILD yielded disappointing results. However, recent advances exploring the potential of novel therapeutic strategies have renewed interest in PH-ILD, with a progressive paradigm shift opening new perspectives for a condition that was until recently associated with a poor prognosis.

candidates.title: Antifibrotics with Cross-Indication Potential: Challenges and Progress Towards a Universal Fibrosis-Modifying Therapy.
candidates.abstract: Organ fibrosis is a chronic, progressive condition that frequently results in organ dysfunction and failure. Despite its high morbidity and mortality, substantial therapeutic gaps persist for fibrosis across all organ systems. The compartmentalization of fibrosis research by organ system has impeded the development of antifibrotic therapies with cross-organ applicability. However, the shared pathobiology of fibrosis involves convergent signaling through the TGF-β/SMAD axis, receptor tyrosine kinase-mediated fibroblast activation, Wnt/β-catenin-driven myofibroblast differentiation, and amplification of oxidative stress. These conserved mechanisms support the emerging concept of fibrotic endotypes and justify the pursuit of cross-indication antifibrotic drug development, specifically for fibrotic processes in lung, liver, kidney and heart. This review examines the cross-indication potential of currently approved antifibrotics (nintedanib, pirfenidone, nerandomilast) and emerging agents by evaluating their mechanisms of action, preclinical and clinical evidence, translational potential in non-pulmonary fibrosis, and insights from recent clinical trials. Recent data from Phase 3 trials underscore the necessity of multi-target rather than single-target strategies. Key barriers to universal antifibrotic therapy, such as target redundancy, gaps in preclinical-to-clinical translation, biological heterogeneity, and suboptimal trial design, are also discussed. We propose that an endotype guided, precision-medicine strategy using multi-omics profiling and cross-organ adaptive trial designs may help bridge this gap and remains the most promising path toward a universal fibrosis-modifying therapy.

candidates.title: Silicosis Among Engineered Stone Workers in Ontario, Canada: A Case Series of 20 Patients.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Silicosis is a preventable occupational lung disease caused by inhalation of respirable crystalline silica. Although traditionally associated with mining, it is increasingly recognized among workers who fabricate engineered stone, also referred to as artificial stone, for kitchen and other countertops. In Canada, updated surveillance data are limited, and no published case series have characterized engineered stone-associated silicosis.
METHODS: We report a retrospective case series of 20 patients diagnosed with silicosis following occupational exposure to engineered stone in Ontario, Canada, between November 2015 and September 2025. Demographic, occupational, clinical, radiologic, and functional data were extracted from medical records. Continuous variables are reported as median and interquartile range (IQR).
RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis was 52 years (IQR: 41.5-64.5), and all patients were male, predominantly immigrants from Southeast Asia. Median occupational exposure to silica was 19 years (IQR: 10.5-27.5). Although 80% reported respirator use, adherence was inconsistent, and workplace controls were often inadequate. Cough and dyspnea were the most common presenting symptoms (60% each), with a median diagnostic delay of 13.5 months. Imaging showed simple silicosis in 70% and progressive massive fibrosis in 30%. Pulmonary function tests demonstrated predominantly restrictive impairment with reduced diffusion capacity. Outcomes were significant, including 15% mortality, median age at death of 43 years, chronic hypoxia in 35%, and lung transplant referral in 30%.
CONCLUSIONS: Engineered stone-associated silicosis in Ontario is characterized by prolonged silica exposure, inadequate workplace protections, delayed diagnosis, and severe disease at presentation. These findings underscore the urgent need for strengthened regulatory measures to protect engineered stone workers: more effective occupational silica exposure controls, systematic respirator

candidates.title: A pediatric case of orbital inflammation and sinusitis- the diagnostic boundary between localized ANCA-associated vasculitis and IgG4-related disease.
candidates.abstract: ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) are characterized by necrotizing inflammation of small- and medium-sized blood vessels, frequently associated with antibodies against myeloperoxidase (MPO) or proteinase 3. In contrast, IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is an immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition that can affect virtually any organ and is histologically characterized by lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates enriched in IgG4-positive plasma cells. Both conditions may present with localized or systemic disease and share clinical and histopathological features, particularly in the head and neck region, making differential diagnosis challenging. We report the case of an 11-year-old girl who initially presented with bilateral orbital inflammation. Orbital biopsy demonstrated lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, an elevated IgG4+/IgG+ plasma cell ratio, and obliterative phlebitis, suggestive of IgG4-RD. However, markedly elevated MPO-ANCA levels raised suspicion for AAV. Although glucocorticoid therapy initially achieved clinical improvement, relapses occurred, prompting treatment with rituximab. Subsequently, the patient developed rhinosinusitis, and nasal biopsy revealed lymphoplasmacytic inflammation with multinucleated giant cells, consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). Treatment was intensified with mycophenolate mofetil and corticosteroids, resulting in remission. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges posed by overlapping features of AAV and IgG4-RD.

candidates.title: Trends, outcomes, and disparities in hospitalizations among patients with Sjögren's syndrome: a national inpatient sample analysis (2016-2020).
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Sjögren's syndrome (SS) is a systemic autoimmune disease with poorly characterized hospitalization outcomes in the United States. We aimed to characterize hospitalization trends, comorbidity profiles, organ-specific manifestations, predictors of in-hospital mortality, and racial, socioeconomic, and hospital-level disparities among SS-associated hospitalizations using the NIS 2016-2020 dataset.
METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the NIS (2016-2020). Adults with SS (ICD-10-CM M35.00-M35.0C) were identified across 40 diagnosis fields and matched 3:1 with non-autoimmune controls by age, sex, and year. Survey-weighted analyses included bivariate comparisons, Elixhauser comorbidity profiling, organ-specific phenotyping, nested multivariable logistic regression for mortality predictors, and adjusted disparities analyses using predictive margins.
RESULTS: Among 272,630 weighted SS-associated hospitalizations (91.4% female, mean age 64.2 years), extraglandular manifestations were documented in 33.8%. Despite a significantly higher baseline comorbidity burden compared with 817,890 matched control hospitalizations, SS-associated admissions exhibited paradoxically lower crude in-hospital mortality (2.13% vs. 2.59%, p<0.001). However, within the SS cohort, acute complications were associated with substantial mortality risk in the fully adjusted model: independent predictors included mechanical ventilation (OR 21.08), sepsis (OR 2.80), stroke (OR 2.78), malignancy (OR 2.46), and interstitial lung disease (OR 2.10). Significant disparities persisted after multivariable adjustment: Asian/Pacific Islander hospitalizations had higher mortality odds (OR 1.67, p=0.002) and incurred $22,643 more in adjusted charges compared with White hospitalizations. Self-pay or uninsured status was associated with doubled mortality odds (OR 2.01, p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Enhanced clinical phenotyping underscores that Sjögren's syndrome is a complex, multisystem disease with a subs

candidates.title: An explainable nomogram incorporating systemic inflammatory indicators and radiation esophagitis for risk assessment of radiation pneumonitis in lung cancer.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the value of systemic inflammatory prognostic markers and early clinical toxicity in the risk assessment of radiation pneumonitis (RP) after radiotherapy in lung cancer patients. We developed and validated an explainable, auxiliary nomogram integrating multiple features and SHAP analysis to optimize early risk monitoring and clinical decision-making.
METHODS: A least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized Cox model was used for feature selection to build a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model, which was visualized as a nomogram. A Fine-Gray competing risks model was used for sensitivity analysis. Model performance was evaluated using the C-index, 6-month time-dependent AUC, calibration, continuous NRI/IDI, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation using bootstrap resampling. Finally, SHAP analysis was performed to interpret the final Cox model through beeswarm and waterfall plots.
RESULTS: This study retrospectively collected data on 726 patients with lung cancer who received radiotherapy. The primary endpoint was grade ≥2 RP, with non-RP-related death treated as a competing risk. Multivariable Cox regression, validated by Fine-Gray competing risk analysis, identified alcohol history, radiotherapy modality, baseline lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), systemic inflammation score (SIS), and acute radiation esophagitis (RE) as independent factors (all P < 0.05). Among the three sequential models, the integrated model (Model 3) achieved the highest C-index (0.688) and 6-month AUC (0.713). Compared to the baseline model (Model 1), Model 3 improved risk reclassification (continuous NRI = 0.274, IDI = 0.037; both P < 0.05). Model 3 demonstrated optimal calibration and yielded the highest net clinical benefit within the 10%-15% threshold probability range in DCA. Furthermore, SHAP analysis enhanced model interpretability, indicating a potential association between a baseline systemic inflammation scor

candidates.title: Anaphylaxis Following Intravenous Methylprednisolone Sodium Succinate: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immediate hypersensitivity to systemic corticosteroids is rare but potentially life-threatening, and it may be overlooked when the cardiovascular presentation is atypical. Identifying the responsible determinant, whether the corticosteroid molecule, a solubilizing ester, or a formulation excipient, is often difficult.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 45-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis developed a generalized pruritic, erythematous, raised eruption, dyspnea, hypoxemia, bradycardia, and reduced consciousness within 5 minutes of starting intravenous methylprednisolone sodium succinate 250 mg. The infusion was stopped, and symptoms resolved after intramuscular epinephrine 0.4 mg. Approximately 7 hours later, because the reaction was considered unlikely to be allergic, the same formulation was re-administered in two graded steps (25%, then 75%) under continuous monitoring and direct physician supervision. This high-risk re-exposure after clinically convincing anaphylaxis reproduced the cutaneous and respiratory features, again with bradycardia (heart rate 51 beats/min) and hypoxemia (oxygen saturation 88%), and required intramuscular epinephrine 0.3 mg, an intravenous antihistamine, oxygen, and a bronchodilator. Serum tryptase and formal allergy testing were not obtained. She later reported tolerating oral prednisolone, with no recurrent symptoms during 3 months of follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Recurrence on re-exposure supports anaphylaxis to the administered methylprednisolone formulation, but without confirmatory testing the reaction cannot be attributed to methylprednisolone itself, the succinate ester, or an excipient. This patient-safety case shows that bradycardia does not exclude anaphylaxis; that a graded challenge is a diagnostic test, not desensitization, and is not a recommended strategy after convincing anaphylaxis; and that the exact implicated formulation should be documented instead of a nonspecific steroid-allergy label.

candidates.title: Prevalence of ECG-detected and previously unrecognized atrial fibrillation among older adults attending a family health center: a single-center cross-sectional screening study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an important and often unrecognized cause of ischemic stroke in older adults. The primary objective of this study was to determine the prevalence of AF detected by a single 12-lead ECG among adults aged ≥ 65 years attending primary care. Secondary objectives were the proportion previously unrecognized, thromboembolic risk and anticoagulant use, and associated characteristics.
METHODS: This single-center cross-sectional study enrolled consecutive consenting adults aged ≥ 65 years attending a family health center in Istanbul, Türkiye (May 2021-May 2022). Of 359 assessed, 2 with pacemakers were excluded, leaving 357. AF on the screening 12-lead ECG was diagnosed by the investigator and confirmed by a cardiologist; AF was classified as previously known when a prior diagnosis was reported and as previously unrecognized otherwise. The study-period anticoagulation threshold was defined as CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥ 2 in men and ≥ 3 in women. Prevalences are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs); associations were examined with chi-square or exact tests and exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression.
RESULTS: AF was detected on the screening ECG in 42 participants (11.8%; 95% CI 8.8-15.5), with similar prevalence by sex. Prevalence differed across age groups (P=.034), with the highest estimate among participants aged ≥ 80 years (26.3%; 95% CI 15.0-42.0). Twenty-two of the 42 ECG-detected AF cases were previously unrecognized (52.4%; 6.2% of all screened participants, 95% CI 4.1-9.2). In an exploratory adjusted model, heart failure (aOR 5.71; 95% CI 1.81-18.00) and chronic lung disease (aOR 2.53; 95% CI 1.24-5.19) were associated with ECG-detected AF, whereas the age estimate was attenuated after adjustment (aOR 1.69 per decade; 95% CI 0.98-2.90). The mean CHA₂DS₂-VASc score was 3.64 ± 1.53, and 37 participants with AF (88.1%) met the study-period anticoagulation threshold. Twenty were not receiving anticoagulation at screening,

candidates.title: Screening for Cough Variant Asthma Using the TabPFN Model on Routine Laboratory Data in a Multicenter Cohort: Prospective Validation Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cough variant asthma (CVA) is a prevalent but underdiagnosed subtype of chronic cough, largely due to the limited accessibility of pulmonary function tests in primary care.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and prospectively validate an interpretable machine learning model using routine laboratory data to facilitate accessible CVA screening.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter study combining retrospective model development and prospective validation using data from January 2021 to August 2025. The study included 3 sets-a retrospective development set (n=533; 428 training and 105 internal testing) and 2 prospective validation sets (internal validation: n=59 and external validation: n=78). In total, 54 routine biochemical, coagulation, and hematological markers were analyzed. A Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) model was developed and benchmarked against extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Performance was evaluated via area under the curve (AUC), accuracy, and specificity. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to assess interpretability and clinical utility.
RESULTS: In external validation, TabPFN achieved an AUC of 0.858 (95% CI 0.763-0.943), accuracy of 79.5%, sensitivity of 71.4%, and specificity of 86%. XGBoost achieved a higher external AUC of 0.912 (95% CI 0.842-0.982) and sensitivity of 91.4%, but lower accuracy (75.6%) and specificity (62.8%) at the fixed 0.5 probability threshold. TabPFN retained higher AUCs than XGBoost in internal testing (0.964 vs 0.890) and temporal validation (0.925 vs 0.846). DCA demonstrated that TabPFN provided higher net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities, with the range varying across validation cohorts.
