candidates.title: ACR lung-RADS: updates and future directions.
candidates.journal: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
candidates.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. Continued refinement, guided by emerging evidence, multidisciplinary collaboration, and technological innovation, will be critical to advancing precision screening strategies and reducing the global burden of lung cancer.Clinical trial numberNot applicable.

candidates.title: [Analysis of the effectiveness of active screening for pulmonary tuberculosis among the elderly in Guizhou Province].
candidates.journal: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi
candidates.abstract: Objective: To analyze the effectiveness of active screening for tuberculosis among the elderly in Guizhou Province and provide a basis for optimizing screening strategies. Methods: Data on active screening for pulmonary tuberculosis among the elderly and case information were collected from the Guizhou Province Smart Disease Control Cloud System and the Tuberculosis Management Information System of the China Disease Prevention and Control Information System. The study analyzed the effectiveness of active screening and examined the basic information and clinical diagnostic characteristics of patients identified through different screening methods. The χ2 test was used for intergroup comparisons of rates or proportions, and the trend χ2 test was applied for temporal trends. The spatial distribution of screening detection rates was visualized using ArcGIS software. Results: From 2023 to 2025, a total of 7 966 965 chest X-ray screenings were conducted among the elderly in Guizhou Province, identifying 6 255 cases of tuberculosis, of which 4 467 were asymptomatic, representing an average annual proportion of asymptomatic cases of 71.4%. The detection rate from active screening rose from 65.3/100 000 in 2023 to 94.9/100 000 in 2025 (trend χ2=148.17, P<0.001). The detection rate from active screening was highest in Qiannan Buyi and Miao Autonomous Prefecture (Qiannan Prefecture) (124.4/100 000) and lowest in Qianxinan Buyi and Miao Autonomous Prefecture (44.8/100 000) (χ2=588.44, P<0.001). The proportion of patients identified through active screening in the nine cities (prefectures) ranged from 12.9% to 27.1%. Among them, the proportion of patients identified through active screening in Guiyang, Zunyi, Anshun, Liupanshui, Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture, and Qiannan Prefecture all showed an upward trend (all P<0.05), while Bijie showed a downward trend (trend χ2=15.32, P<0.001). Among patients identified through active screening, males (62.6%), those aged

candidates.title: Interventions to increase participation in lung cancer screening programmes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
candidates.journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We aimed to systematically review and meta-analyse the effectiveness of interventions in increasing informed choice and participation in lung cancer screening based on low-dose computed tomography (LDCT).
METHODS: Five electronic databases, Medline (PubMed version), Embase, Cinahl (Ebsco version), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL, were searched for randomised controlled trials, nonrandomised controlled trials and before-after studies published from 2000 until 15 March 2023. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of interventions to increase rates of LDCT completion.
RESULTS: Out of 3483 studies identified, 14 completed and 21 ongoing studies were included in the review. Shared-decision making (SDM)+navigation (OR 4.34, 95% CI 2.50-7.54) and outreach+navigation (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.70-2.84) resulted in a higher proportion of LDCT performed compared to the control group. Educational/informational interventions (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.19) as well as SDM alone (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.57-2.32) did not improve LDCT uptake, despite the second improving decisional outcomes in both intervention and control groups. Multicomponent interventions showed significantly higher LDCT uptake (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.79-3.90), compared to unicomponent interventions (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.14). The vast majority of interventions, including those in ongoing trials, are patient-oriented, while community-based, provider-level and system-level interventions remain rare.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining high-intensity patient-oriented interventions, such as patient navigation, active outreach and SDM, appears to be the most promising strategy to increase lung cancer screening uptake (low certainty of evidence). However, implementation studies are needed to evaluate interventions targeting both provider and healthcare systems level.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence apps for medical image analysis using pyCERR and cancer genomics cloud.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: To provide a software resource that enables medical researchers and practitioners to develop and apply reproducible, out-of-the-box, AI-based analysis workflows for radiological and radiotherapy data.
DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION METHODS: The framework comprises two main components: the Python-native computational environment for radiological research (pyCERR) for radiological image processing, and the cancer genomics cloud (CGC), a National Cancer Institute-funded resource that supports cloud-hosted collaborative projects, with tools for managing collaborators and compute-hardware from providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud Platform. pyCERR is open-source (GNU GPL) and distributed at https://github.com/cerr/pycerr; it provides user-friendly data structures, simplified access to metadata across radiological imaging modalities, and tools for data transformation, AI-based image segmentation, radiomics, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI analysis, radiotherapy dose-volume histogram (DVH) feature extraction, and normal-tissue complication and tumor-control models. Radiomics features comply with the Image biomarker standardization initiative (IBSI) standards and are validated against published reference values. Unit tests covering data input/output, radiomics, DVH features, and visualization run on every code update. Workflows are containerized for reproducible, identical execution on the CGC and on local hardware. The CGC enables AI inference from radiological images to be combined with other data types such as genomics and proteomics. Our public CGC project (https://cgc.sbgenomics.com/u/sevenbridges/pycerr-radiological-radiotherapy-imageanalysis), accessible with free registration, currently includes apps for organ-at-risk (OAR) and lung-nodule segmentation based on published models trained in-house and clinically validated. These apps can be run interactively from a web browser or programmatically via a REST API with client support for multiple progr

candidates.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of COPD Awareness and Screening Intention among Community-Dwelling Older Adults in China.
candidates.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has recently been incorporated into the National Basic Public Health Service Program because of its high prevalence and substantial mortality burden among elderly Chinese individuals. However, little is known about COPD awareness, screening intention, and their associated factors.
METHODS: Between September 2024 and February 2025, a structured questionnaire survey was conducted among community-dwelling older adults in Jiangsu and Shandong provinces, China, to collect data on potential influencing factors, COPD awareness, and screening intention. We identified factors associated with COPD awareness and screening intention using univariable binary logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: Among the 574 participants, 116 (20.21%) had heard of COPD and 412 (71.78%) expressed willingness to undergo screening. Higher education (OR = 4.522, 95% CI: 2.198-9.947), rural residence (OR = 0.428, 95% CI: 0.274-0.658), being employed (OR = 0.246, 95% CI: 0.094-0.535), higher income (OR = 2.941, 95% CI: 1.727-4.966), and vaccination history (OR = 2.221, 95% CI: 1.426-3.437) were associated with COPD awareness. Older age (OR = 1.498, 95% CI: 1.025-2.201), rural residence (OR = 1.512, 95% CI: 1.046-2.196), higher income (OR = 0.586, 95% CI: 0.355-0.980), having a chronic condition (OR = 1.467, 95% CI: 1.019-2.117), participation in community-based chronic disease management (OR = 1.547, 95% CI: 1.073-2.241), and vaccination history (OR = 1.583, 95% CI: 1.017-2.523) were associated with screening intention.
CONCLUSION: This study provides up-to-date evidence that Chinese elderly have low COPD awareness but a relatively high screening intention, and identifies socio-demographic characteristics, physical health, and healthcare utilization as important associated factors, with public health implications for guiding community-based health education and improving early detection strategies.

candidates.title: Exhaled Breath Analysis for Lung Cancer Detection: From VOCs Signatures to EBC-Based Liquid Biopsy and Clinical Translation.
candidates.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Although low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is the current standard for early screening, its high false-positive rates and cumulative radiation exposure create a pressing clinical need for complementary, non-invasive diagnostic tools. Exhaled breath analysis represents an accessible strategy for early detection and risk stratification. Early breathomics primarily focused on gas-phase volatile organic compounds (VOCs). However, as volatile metabolites, VOCs are chemically unstable and highly susceptible to background ambient air and physiological confounders. Distinct from gas-phase analysis, exhaled breath condensate (EBC) offers enhanced biomarker stability and functions as a lung-proximal liquid biopsy. By capturing non-volatile, high-molecular-weight analytes, including tumor-derived nucleic acids and proteins, EBC more closely reflects the underlying molecular mechanisms of the respiratory microenvironment. Nevertheless, the clinical translation of EBC remains constrained by severe sample dilution, unstandardized collection device architectures, and pre-analytical inconsistencies. This review summarizes the progression from VOCs profiling to EBC-based platforms, detailing recent advances in sample harvesting, ultrasensitive detection technologies, and multi-omics integration. Advancing EBC toward routine clinical use requires consensus-driven standard operating procedures and the application of machine learning algorithms to high-dimensional datasets. Future efforts should prioritize large-scale, multicenter prospective trials to validate specific EBC signatures, thereby establishing this technology as a reliable liquid biopsy for precision pulmonary oncology.

candidates.title: Lung Cancer Screening Delivery in a Decentralized Program: Patient and Provider Perspectives.
candidates.journal: Cancer control : journal of the Moffitt Cancer Center
candidates.abstract: IntroductionLung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in Alabama, where screening uptake remains well below national benchmarks. Decentralized screening programs, in which referring providers manage eligibility identification, referrals, and follow-up without dedicated coordination infrastructure, are common across clinical settings. Yet the relationship between program design and delivery outcomes in decentralized contexts has received little attention. This study examined how a decentralized lung cancer screening program delivered screening across each step of the pathway, from patient identification through annual follow-up. The goal was to identify where and how program design produced gaps in delivery from the perspectives of patients and providers.MethodsThis qualitative study used semi-structured interviews conducted between July 2023 and May 2024 at an academic medical center in Alabama as part of a larger explanatory sequential mixed methods study. Fifteen patients who had completed screening and six providers representing primary care, pulmonology, and radiology participated. Interviews explored screening awareness, decision-making, and program delivery processes. Transcripts were analyzed using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) and constant comparative method. Reporting followed the COREQ guideline.ResultsDelivery failures were structural and concentrated at the front end of the screening pathway. Eligibility identification depended on incidental patient exposure rather than systematic outreach. Referrals reflected individual provider initiative rather than standardized workflows. Result tracking and nodule follow-up fell to ordering providers without dedicated support. Coverage gaps and geographic distance compounded these determinants.ConclusionReduced uptake in this decentralized program pointed largely to structural barriers. Closing the implementation gap may require program design changes and proactive outr

candidates.title: Lung cancer screening health beliefs among a high-risk population in China: a cross-sectional survey.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Evidence on lung cancer screening (LCS) health beliefs among high-risk populations in China remains limited. This study aimed to examine LCS health beliefs and associated factors among individuals at high risk for lung cancer in Fujian Province, China.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted from September 2020 to October 2022. High-risk individuals were recruited using a four-stage multistage sampling procedure incorporating probability-proportionate-to-size sampling. LCS health beliefs were assessed using the Chinese Lung Cancer Screening Health Belief Scale (LCSHB-C). Multiple linear regression was used to examine associated factors.
RESULTS: A total of 1,957 participants were included, with a mean overall LCSHB-C score of 95.10 (SD = 10.13). LCS-related knowledge and previous screening experience showed the most consistent positive associations with health beliefs. Rural residence, religious affiliation, and higher household income were also associated with higher overall scores, whereas female sex, current or former smoking, COPD, and participation in the national basic medical insurance program were associated with lower scores. Associations with age, education, body mass index, and occupational exposure varied across health belief domains.
CONCLUSION: LCS health beliefs were associated with screening knowledge, previous screening experience, and several sociodemographic and health-related characteristics. These findings may inform tailored LCS education and support strategies to facilitate informed participation among high-risk populations.

candidates.title: A retrospective epidemiological study of screening-derived solid cancer incidence proxy rates in South Korea before and after COVID-19 using Korean National Health Insurance Service data.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted cancer screening and diagnostic pathways globally. Aggregate screening-derived indicators require cautious interpretation because they do not represent confirmed cancer registry incidence but might reflect program participation, referral patterns, and denominator composition.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate pre- and post-COVID-19 changes in selected solid cancer screening-derived incidence proxy rates in South Korea, and to estimate model-based proxy rates through 2028.
METHODS: This retrospective ecological longitudinal study analyzed publicly available aggregate annual cancer-screening statistics from the Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) and Korean Statistical Information Service (KOSIS) for six solid cancer programs (stomach, liver, colorectal, breast, cervical, and lung cancer). Annual proxy rates per 100,000 screened or eligible persons were calculated. Pre-COVID (2010-2019) and post-COVID (2020-2024) means were compared using Welch t-tests with Mann-Whitney U sensitivity analyses. Ordinary least-squares (OLS) forecasts were generated for 2025-2028. Interrupted time-series analysis was not feasible owing to an insufficient post-COVID observation window.
RESULTS: Post-COVID changes in proxy rates were heterogeneous across selected programs. Breast cancer proxy rates increased by 17.1% (Welch p = 0.002) and liver cancer proxy rates by 83.6% (Welch p = 0.002); the liver cancer increase reflects denominator restriction to a high-risk population rather than a true epidemiological surge. Stomach cancer decreased by 23.3% (Welch p = 0.001), cervical cancer by 56.9% (Welch p = 0.005), and colorectal cancer by 25.8% (Welch p = 0.007). Lung cancer data were available only from 2019 to 2024 (program inception) and were interpreted descriptively.
CONCLUSIONS: Aggregate South Korean national screening data show pandemic-era temporal associations with heterogeneous changes in selected solid cancer program proxy rates. These f

candidates.title: Multimodal Transformer Integrating CT and Pathology for Postoperative Risk Stratification in Stage I Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
candidates.abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable, multimodal deep learning model to improve postoperative risk stratification and predict adjuvant therapy benefit in stage I non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Materials and Methods In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with stage I NSCLC, a multimodal model called the Deep Learning-Radiomic-Text Transformer (DLRTransformer) was developed by integrating multiview 2.5-dimensional deep learning features from CT scans, radiomics, clinical variables, and prognostic embeddings extracted from pathology reports using a large language model. A central transformer architecture fuses these features to predict disease-free survival. Model performance was evaluated on independent external datasets and compared with guideline-based risk stratification. Associations between model-derived risk scores and tumor microenvironment features were analyzed to assess biologic interpretability. Results A total of 1073 patients (mean age ± SD, 60.8 years ± 9.8; 550 male) were enrolled from five centers. On external datasets, DLRTransformer demonstrated robust prognostic performance (concordance index, 0.77-0.78), outperforming the guideline-based risk stratification (concordance index, 0.60-0.65). Risk scores were associated with tumor microenvironment phenotypes, including increased neoplastic cellularity and reduced tertiary lymphoid structures. A treatment-by-risk interaction was observed (interaction hazard ratio [HR], 0.14; 95% CI: 0.06, 0.32; P < .01). In propensity score-matched subcohorts, adjuvant therapy improved disease-free survival in high-risk patients (HR, 0.30; 95% CI: 0.11, 0.84; P = .02) but not in low-risk patients (HR, 1.70; 95% CI: 0.97, 2.99; P = .06). Conclusion The DLRTransformer improved postoperative risk stratification compared with guideline-based risk stratification and identified patients with stage I NSCLC who benefited from adjuvant therapy.

candidates.title: Lung Nodule Detection and False Positive Reduction Using Multi-View and Background Images.
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a lung nodule detection and false positive reduction approach based on YOLOv8x, multi-view CT representations, and background slices used as negative samples. Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and early detection is essential to improve patient survival. Although computed tomography (CT) provides detailed three-dimensional information about the lungs, the large number of generated slices increases the complexity of radiological analysis and can contribute to diagnostic errors. To address this challenge, Computer-Aided Detection (CAD) systems have been developed to assist radiologists in identifying suspicious regions. In this work, we combine axial, coronal, and sagittal representations in a single YOLOv8x detection pipeline, use additional LIDC-IDRI annotation clusters with fewer than three radiologist markings as auxiliary positive samples, and introduce nodule-free background slices as negative training samples. Detections are consolidated through intra-view clustering and weighted inter-view fusion. Experiments following the LUNA16 cross-validation protocol show that the proposed strategy improves detection performance while substantially reducing false positives. The axial baseline achieved a Competition Performance Metric (CPM) score of 0.553 with 32.61 candidates per scan, whereas the multi-view configuration with a nominal budget of 20,000 background images achieved a CPM score of 0.863 and reduced the average number of candidates to 9.11 per scan while preserving high sensitivity. These results show that the combined use of multiple anatomical views and background-negative training can substantially reduce spurious candidates in CT-based lung nodule detection.

candidates.title: Predicting lymph node metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer using clinical and PET/CT-derived morphological features: An interpretable machine-learning study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is crucial for staging and treatment planning. This study aimed to establish a standardized machine learning workflow based on routinely available clinical, serological, and PET/CT-derived parameters to enhance preoperative LNM risk stratification.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 255 patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC, all of whom underwent systematic lymph-node dissection. Patients were randomly divided, with stratification by pathological lymph-node status, into a training cohort (n = 178) and an internal held-out test test cohort (n = 77). Candidate predictors were screened using univariable and multivariable logistic regression in the training cohort. Six machine-learning algorithms were trained and optimized using repeated nested five-fold cross-validation. After model development was completed, all six models were applied without modification to the test cohort. Test-set AUCs were compared using paired DeLong tests with Holm correction. The primary model was further evaluated for calibration, clinical utility, and feature contribution using SHAP. A conventional multivariable logistic regression model using the same four predictors was added as a simple reference model, and its discrimination and calibration were compared with those of XGBoost.
RESULTS: Central tumor location, elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, elevated squamous cell carcinoma antigen, and solid nodule status were retained as predictors; none of the quantitative PET metabolic parameters remained independently associated with LNM. XGBoost achieved the highest cross-validated AUC among the six candidate machine-learning algorithms in the training cohort (0.735; 95% CI, 0.653-0.813) and was therefore designated the primary model. In the internal held-out test cohort, XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.747 (95% CI, 0.631-0.846). The conventional logistic regression reference model ach

candidates.title: Real-world before-and-after evaluation of AI support for lung cancer diagnosis at three US lung nodule clinics.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health systems and payers require evidence that artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support improves care delivery. Integrating AI into lung nodule management pathways may streamline workflows, improve identification and triage of patients with pulmonary nodules, and enable earlier lung cancer diagnosis. Yet real-world evidence of clinical utility remains limited. This study evaluated the impact of implementing commercially available AI software to support the lung nodule and lung cancer care pathway across three US health systems.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A real-world before-and-after study compared clinic activity during matched 12.5-month pre-implementation and post-implementation periods at three US lung nodule clinics. Primary outcomes were the number of new patients and the number of patients undergoing at least one invasive procedure. Secondary outcomes were numbers of lung cancers and early-stage (stages I-II) lung cancers, and time from baseline CT to diagnosis. Analyses used Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests, with medians and interquartile ranges (IQRs) reported for continuous measures.
RESULTS: Across sites, new patients increased from 138 before to 232 after implementation, equivalent to 11.0 to 18.6 patients per month (p = 0.0002), with the median rising from 9 (IQR 7-14) to 16 (IQR 13-21) patients. Monthly patients undergoing at least one invasive procedure increased from 4.9 to 8.0 (p = 0.0085). Monthly cancers increased from 3.0 to 3.8 (p = 0.3242), while monthly early-stage cancers rose from 1.4 to 2.4 (p = 0.125). Median time to diagnosis was 58 days (IQR 33-158) before and 57 days (IQR 27-85) after implementation (p = 0.26), with IQR narrowing from 125 days to 58 days.
CONCLUSION: Implementation of the AI-enabled software was associated with significantly increased throughput of lung nodule patients and procedural volume. These results, observed prospectively post-implementation, suggest AI-assisted identification a

candidates.title: Machine Learning, Radiomics, and Clinical Models Predicting Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis in Lung Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially fatal immune-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung cancer, and many machine-learning (ML), computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models have been proposed to predict it. This systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and SinoMed, supplemented by citation searching and other sources, with independent dual-reviewer screening throughout and a reproducible PubMed verification search updated to August 16, 2026. Twelve peer-reviewed lung-cancer CIP-occurrence models (4,875 patients, 1,057 events) formed the main analysis; validation C-statistics were pooled on the logit scale with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp intervals, stratified by validation design. The pooled validation C-statistic was 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.75-0.88) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 90.7%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 0.51-0.95, which is the decision-relevant quantity. By validation design, internal cross-validation pooled to 0.83, internal split-sample to 0.76, and only two studies reported external validation (0.84 and 0.92, described narratively). Imaging-based models (k = 8) showed numerically higher discrimination than clinical models (k = 4; 0.85 versus 0.78, moderator p = 0.46) without a statistically significant difference, and this comparison is confounded by design covariates. Estimates were stable on leave-one-out, alternative-model, cohort-overlap, and standard-error-source sensitivity analyses (range 0.80-0.84). Under the standard Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool, applied independently by two reviewers with consensus resolution, two studies were at high, nine at unclear, and one at low overall risk of bias; certainty of evidence was low (very low under a stricter appraisal scenario, which left the pooled estimate essentially unchanged). Current models separate risk groups on average but remain unready

candidates.title: Abolition by design: implementing the dismantling of the commercial tobacco and nicotine industry.
candidates.abstract: The commercial tobacco and nicotine industry continues to drive preventable disease and death globally. Despite progress in tobacco control, industry power, product diversification, market expansion, and policy interference have constrained the impact of incremental regulatory approaches. Downstream interventions, such as cessation supports and lung cancer screening, remain essential but respond to accumulated harms rather than preventing exposure at its source. This paper presents an implementation framework that positions abolition as a staged, governable, and legally supported public health strategy. Rather than a symbolic endpoint, abolition is conceptualized as a sequenced governance process through which industry structures can be dismantled using existing regulatory, fiscal, and enforcement mechanisms. These mechanisms are embedded within national systems and international instruments, including the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control and international human rights instruments. Abolition is mischaracterized as consumer prohibition. This reflects a category error that evaluates abolition using prohibition logics, obscuring its focus on dismantling corporate production, supply, and profit infrastructures through existing governance and regulatory tools. The framework conceptualizes the industry as an ecosystem spanning corporate structures, product categories, supply chains, science distortion, and political influence. Each domain is mapped to disruption levers and institutions, with the aim of reducing implementation risk and limiting industry adaptation. Abolition is framed as a coordinated governance project across local, national, and global levels, with Indigenous peoples and young people recognized as leaders shaping accountability, prevention pathways, and norms. This approach illustrates how abolition-oriented reform may be administratively feasible, legally defensible, and relevant to advancing health equity.

candidates.title: Pulmonary nodules: classification, biomarkers, signaling pathways, diseases, early diagnosis and management.
candidates.abstract: Pulmonary nodules are increasingly detected by thoracic imaging and low-dose computed tomography-based lung cancer screening, but most are benign, transient, or indolent. Clinically, the key task is to distinguish nodules that require timely cancer-directed evaluation from those that can be safely observed. This review summarizes the classification, disease spectrum, risk assessment, early diagnosis, biomarkers, signaling mechanisms, translational models, and management of pulmonary nodules. We first distinguish imaging phenotypes and disease entities, then differentiate the individual-level models used to select candidates for lung cancer screening from the nodule-level models and structured reporting systems used after nodule detection. Low-dose computed tomography remains the foundation of screening and surveillance approaches, whereas magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography, nonsurgical biopsy, surgical diagnosis, and local therapies play more selective roles depending on the probability of malignancy and patient fitness. Noninvasive biomarkers, including circulating cellular, nucleic acid, methylation, protein, autoantibody, extracellular vesicle, and metabolic analytes, are most likely to serve as adjuncts to imaging and clinical risk assessment rather than as stand-alone diagnostic tests. Artificial intelligence may support detection, workflow efficiency, malignancy risk reclassification, invasiveness assessment, and multimodal integration, but its value depends on external validation, calibration, implementation, and prospective evidence of management benefit. Mechanistic studies of adenocarcinoma spectrum subsolid nodules have implicated the involvement of early oncogenic signaling, genomic instability, immune escape, stromal and vascular remodeling, and adaptive survival pathways. Translational models can support mechanistic and procedural research, but do not r

candidates.title: Who participates in LDCT screening for the early detection of lung cancer after long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust? Results of the analysis of administrative and medical routine data from the German Social Accident Insurance.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer is one of the most common cancers in Germany and is predominantly detected at an advanced stage. To ensure early detection, the German Social Accident Insurance (DGUV) offers lung cancer screening including a low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) for individuals with long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust and a smoking history of at least 30 pack years. However, evidence remains scarce about what encourages this group of people to participate in LDCT screening after medical consultation.
METHODS: A secondary data analysis using routinely collected medical and administrative data between 2014 and 2024 was conducted in a cross-sectional design. This study aimed to investigate factors that could be used to predict the uptake of LDCT screening following a medical consultation. Exploratory logistic regression analysis was used to identify and assess possible predictors.
RESULTS: The sample included n = 14,491 individuals (97% male; average age 67 years; average asbestos dust exposure 21 years; average cigarette consumption 43 pack years). 74% of individuals underwent LDCT screening after medical consultation. 13 predictors were included in the regression model. The model demonstrated a low level of variance explanation (Nagelkerkes R2 = 0.026). Younger individuals (OR: 0.96, p < 0.001), individuals with prolonged exposure to asbestos dust (OR: 1.01, p = 0.011) and with a history of pneumonia (OR: 1.16, p = 0.011) were more likely to undergo LDCT screening.
CONCLUSION: The predictors showed only a low explanatory power. Further research should include non-participants and expand the exploratory model to include theoretically grounded predictors.

candidates.title: ReViT-RF: A hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with a Radiomic Feature Fusion framework for lung tumor classification and TNM-based stage prediction using CT images.
candidates.abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, emphasizing the need for accurate, automated, and clinically interpretable diagnostic systems. Although existing deep learning (DL) models have achieved promising performance in classifying lung nodules as benign or malignant, most approaches are limited to binary classification and provide insufficient support for detailed tumor characterization and TNM staging. Furthermore, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are effective in extracting local morphological features but often fail to capture long-range spatial dependencies. In contrast, transformer-based models can learn global contextual information but may compromise fine-grained local feature representation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with Radiomic Feature Fusion (ReViT-RF) framework for lung tumor classification and component-wise TNM stage prediction using thoracic computed tomography (CT) images from the publicly available Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. The primary clinical objectives of the proposed framework are to: (i) classify pulmonary nodules as benign or malignant, and (ii) predict individual TNM components, including primary tumor extent (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastatic status (M) for malignant cases. To improve tumor visibility and image quality, CT images are initially preprocessed using Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and intensity normalization. The proposed ReViT-RF architecture integrates the complementary advantages of ResNet-50 and Vision Transformer (ViT) for comprehensive feature learning. The CNN branch extracts local morphological, textural, and structural characteristics, whereas the transformer branch captures long-range spatial relationships and global contextual dependencies. In addition, handcrafted radiomic features, including shape,

candidates.title: Diagnosis and treatment of four cases of pulmonary cryptococcosis: case report and literature review.
candidates.journal: Journal of infection in developing countries
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cryptococcosis has attracted global attention due to its high mortality rate, unique geographical distribution, and tendency to cause severe and rapid disease progression. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) is a novel detection technology that provides diagnostic insights for identifying pathogens, particularly rare ones. The present article describes 4 individuals diagnosed with pulmonary cryptococcosis (PC) using mNGS of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF).
CASE PRESENTATION: Among these patients, 3 had cancer, 1 had sarcoidosis and diabetes, and 2 were exposed to pigeons and/or pigeon droppings. These patients experienced symptoms, including fever, cough, and chest pain. They were diagnosed with PC after mNGS of BALF. The patient was diagnosed based on mNGS test results. Subsequently, the patient was treated with fluconazole, and the patient's chest computed tomography scan showed significant absorption of the lung lesions.
CONCLUSIONS: mNGS of BALF can quickly diagnose PC. This diagnostic method has minimal trauma to the body and is worthy of clinical promotion. Fluconazole remains the preferred and best therapeutic drug for PC treatment.

candidates.title: Multimodal non-invasive ultrasound for predicting severe coronary artery stenosis in right coronary dominant patients.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess the predictive value of multimodal non-invasive ultrasound in detecting severe coronary artery stenosis (CAS) in patients with right coronary artery dominance.
METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled patients undergoing coronary angiography and non-invasive echocardiography at the Department of Cardiology, Luzhou People's Hospital, between December 2021 and August 2023. Severe CAS (SCAS) was defined as CAS ≥ 75% based on angiographic results. Patients were categorized into the SCAS group and the NSCAS group (non-severe CAS).
RESULTS: A total of 121 patients were included, with 98 in the NSCAS group and 23 in the SCAS group. Compared to the NSCAS group, the SCAS group showed a lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (49.3 ± 9.8% vs. 58.9 ± 5.2%, p = 0.028), a higher left ventricular end-systolic diameter(LVsd) (35.2 ± 7.7 mm vs. 29.8 ± 5.0 mm, p = 0.020), and a higher end-systolic volume༈ESV༉ (54.0 ± 23.0 ml vs. 35.7 ± 21.8 ml, p = 0.041). According to the receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, the optimal cutoff values for predicting SCAS are as follows: motion score, 1.5; ESV, 47.5 ml; LVsd, 30.5 mm; LVEF, 53.5%; mitral annular systolic velocity༈Smv༉, 8.5 cm/s; and global longitudinal peak strain༈GLPS༉, -16.5% (all p < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression showed that LVEF was associated with SCAS (OR = 1.600, 95% CI:1.037-2.468, P = 0.034).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that LVEF may play a role in predicting SCAS, validating non-invasive ultrasound as an effective early diagnostic tool for patients with right coronary artery dominance.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

candidates.title: Quantitative Flow Ratio- vs Angiography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Secondary Analysis of the FAVOR III China Trial.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Whether the association of quantitative flow ratio (QFR)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with long-term outcomes differs according to multivessel disease (MVD) status is uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association of QFR-guided vs angiography-guided PCI with 3-year outcomes according to MVD status.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this prespecified secondary analysis of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial, patients were screened across 26 centers in China from December 25, 2018, to January 19, 2020. Eligible participants were adults undergoing PCI for stable or unstable angina or for myocardial infarction (MI) occurring at least 72 hours before screening who had at least 1 lesion with 50% to 90% diameter stenosis in a vessel of 2.5 mm or larger. The analysis compared QFR-guided with angiography-guided PCI according to MVD status. MVD was defined by involvement of at least 2 epicardial vessels or the left main coronary artery. The primary analyses of the current prespecified secondary analysis were completed in October 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: Randomization 1:1 to QFR-guided PCI or angiography-guided PCI.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point of the FAVOR III China randomized clinical trial was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, MI, and ischemia-driven revascularization. The current analysis evaluated 3-year MACE.
RESULTS: Among 3825 patients in the intention-to-treat population (mean [SD] age, 62.7 [10.0] years; 2699 [70.6%] male), 2066 (54.0%) had MVD. In the MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 124 of 1023 patients (12.1%) in the QFR-guided group and 188 of 1043 patients (18.1%) in the angiography-guided group (hazard ratio, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.52-0.81; P < .001), driven by lower rates of MI and revascularization. In the non-MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 76 of 890 patients (8.6%) and 95 of 869 patients (11.0%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.04; P = .09)

candidates.title: Mitral Annular Disjunction: Regional Strain Abnormalities Associated With Life-Threatening Ventricular Arrhythmias.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) has been linked to malignant ventricular arrhythmias in mitral valve prolapse, but the mechanisms and risk predictors are not well established. We aimed to identify clinical and echocardiographic factors with a focus on left ventricular (LV) strain.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 69 patients with MAD confirmed on echocardiogram. Clinical data and echocardiographic measurements were collected, including chamber dimensions, MAD distance, mitral regurgitation grade, and 2D global and segmental longitudinal strain by speckle-tracking. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to determine independent predictors of arrhythmia.
RESULTS: All patients had preserved LV ejection fraction. Patients with arrhythmias demonstrated trends toward larger chamber dimensions and a larger MAD distance. Global longitudinal strain did not significantly differ between groups. Differences between patients with and without life-threatening arrhythmias localized specifically to the inferolateral region at the mid-ventricular level, where mid-inferolateral strain was significantly worse in arrhythmic patients (median -12.6% [IQR 13.5] vs. -18.9% [IQR 6.0], p = 0.0069). In univariate models, factors associated with arrhythmias included larger LV chamber diameters, greater MAD distance, a history of syncope, and worse strain in the mid-inferior and mid-inferolateral segments. On exploratory multivariate analysis, mid-inferolateral strain impairment appears to be independently associated with LTA (OR 1.11 per 1% strain increase, p = 0.012).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with MAD, impaired mid-inferolateral segment strain was associated with LTA, suggesting that regional myocardial deformation may provide incremental arrhythmic risk stratification beyond global measures. These findings are, however, exploratory, hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts with independent validation to asc

candidates.title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Acute Coronary Occlusion in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary occlusion (ACO) occurs in approximately one-quarter of patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is associated with adverse outcomes. This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model for ACO.
METHODS: Consecutive patients admitted with NSTEMI between January 2016 and June 2023 who underwent coronary angiography were enrolled. Demographic, electrocardiographic, laboratory, and echocardiographic data were collected. Patients admitted during 2016-2020 were assigned to the training cohort (n = 670), and those admitted during 2021-2023 were assigned to the validation cohort (n = 334). Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and a nomogram was constructed based on multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Among 1,004 patients, 262 (26.1%) had ACO. Seven predictors, including smoking history, ST-segment depression ≥ 1 mm, regional wall motion abnormality, left ventricular ejection fraction, admission cardiac troponin I, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, were incorporated into the model. The area under the ROC curve was 0.731 (95% CI, 0.688-0.773) in the training cohort and 0.715 (95% CI, 0.654-0.776) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA demonstrated favorable clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: This study developed and validated a multidimensional prediction model for ACO in patients with NSTEMI. The model showed acceptable performance and may aid early identification before coronary angiography, although reliance on IL-6, which is not routinely available in all centers, may limit its generalizability.

candidates.title: Transcatheter Intervention Is Associated With Visceral Decongestion in Patients With Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is frequently associated with severe venous congestion, increasingly recognized as a key factor in the development of cardiorenal syndrome. While transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI) has shown to be effective in TR reduction, their impact on visceral venous congestion remains unknown. The aim of our study was to investigate visceral venous congestion in patients with severe TR undergoing TTVI.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 30 patients undergoing TTVI for severe TR. Renal venous blood flow was assessed by Doppler ultrasound examination at baseline and 1 to 3 months after the procedure. A 5-grade rating scale was developed to categorize venous flow from continuous (Grade I°) through discontinuous to a pendulous venous flow (Grade V°) within the kidneys.
RESULTS: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER, n = 24) was performed in 24 patients; 6 patients underwent heterotopic caval valve implantation. At baseline, severe renal congestion was present in most participants, with 20 patients showing venous flow profiles IV or V. Venous flow profiles strongly correlated with invasively measured right atrial mean pressure and V wave (p < 0.01). At follow-up, venous renal blood flow profiles improved significantly (p = 0.003), reducing patients with profiles IV or V from 20 to 9. Portal vein flow showed comparable decongestive changes. In TEER patients, reduction of TR ≥ 2 grades was associated with improved renal vein profile at follow-up (p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: Successful TTVI leads to visceral decongestion. Renal venous flow currently represents a physiological marker of congestion that may complement conventional echocardiographic parameters; its role in guiding patient selection or timing of intervention remains to be determined in larger studies.

candidates.title: Mid-Term Clinical Outcomes According to CTO Revascularization Status in Patients With NSTEMI and Multivessel Disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical relevance of chronic total occlusion (CTO) revascularization in patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and multivessel disease (MVD) remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 632 patients with NSTEMI, MVD, and CTO were included. Patients were categorized into a complete revascularization group involving successful CTO recanalization (CR-CTO, n = 119) and an incomplete revascularization group without successful CTO recanalization (ICR-CTO, n = 513). The primary endpoints were major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 528 ± 201 days, the incidences of MACCE (11.8% vs. 28.5%) and MACE (7.6% vs. 24.2%) were significantly lower in the CR-CTO group than in the ICR-CTO group (both p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analyses, CR-CTO was independently associated with lower risks of MACCE (hazard ratio [HR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.20-0.61) and MACE (HR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.13-0.51). Among patients without successful CTO recanalization, additional revascularization of non-CTO lesions was not associated with improved outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with NSTEMI, MVD, and CTO, complete revascularization involving successful CTO recanalization was associated with improved mid-term clinical outcomes. In contrast, additional revascularization of non-CTO lesions alone was not associated with a prognostic benefit when CTO lesions remained unrevascularized. These findings suggest that CTO revascularization status may warrant specific consideration when revascularization strategies are evaluated in this patient population.

candidates.title: Inferolateral ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Secondary to Suspected Coronary Embolism in a Patient with Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Coronary embolism is an underrecognized nonatherosclerotic cause of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), most commonly associated with atrial fibrillation. We report a 76-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation who presented with acute substernal chest pain and inferolateral STEMI. Coronary angiography demonstrated a 100% thrombotic occlusion of the distal right posterolateral ventricular branch with otherwise nonobstructive coronary artery disease. In the setting of an abrupt distal coronary occlusion, minimal underlying atherosclerotic disease, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and fulfillment of the Shibata diagnostic criteria, coronary embolism was considered the most likely mechanism. Long-term anticoagulation was continued, and the patient remained asymptomatic at 1-month follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of suspected coronary embolism in patients presenting with STEMI, atrial fibrillation, and minimal underlying coronary artery disease.

candidates.title: Evaluation of Myocardial Blood Flow Using 18F-flurpiridaz PET: Established Applications with Pharmacologic Stress and Roadmap for Exercise Stress Implementation.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recently approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration, 18F-flurpiridaz for positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) enables high-quality assessment of myocardial blood flow (MBF). Its half-life of approximately 110 min supports regional distribution and allows unit-dose delivery. These features make this probe well suited for MBF quantitation and expand access to quantitative cardiac PET at smaller centers.
RECENT FINDINGS: During pharmacologic stress, absolute MBF and myocardial flow reserve provide incremental diagnostic information beyond relative perfusion imaging. These measures have been validated across multiple methods and software platforms. Further study of this tracer under peak exercise may provide clinically relevant assessment of myocardial demand-induced changes in flow. Potential investigational approaches include artificial intelligence (AI)-derived virtual MBF, exercise-adjusted standardized uptake value (SUV) ratio-derived myocardial flow reserve (MFR) surrogate, and direct kinetic modeling during in-scanner ergometry. While conceptually promising, limitations inherent to exercise-based approaches in stress MBF and/or MFR estimation highlight the need for pragmatic research strategies before potential clinical applicability.

candidates.title: Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Non-Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy: The Role of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to evaluate the contemporary and evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in arrhythmic risk stratification for patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, specifically focussing on dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). This review synthesises current data on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping, strain imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), and contextualises these among emerging genetic risk stratification approaches.
RECENT FINDINGS: Left ventricular ejection fraction has been the cornerstone for guideline-based arrhythmic risk stratification in patients with DCM, despite limited precision. Observational data and meta-analyses have established the presence of replacement fibrosis through LGE-CMR as a powerful independent predictor of ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) and sudden cardiac death. Crucially, the absence of LGE identifies a low-risk cohort. Much recent focus has been on understanding whether more precise characterisation of scar can further enhance arrhythmic risk stratification, for example through scar quantification. Although data exists supporting a potential role for T1 mapping for arrhythmic risk prediction in this cohort, further research is required to support its widespread adoption. Emerging multimodal approaches using artificial intelligence and personalised computational "digital twins" are areas of important interest, offering scope for integration of imaging, electrocardiographic and genomic data layers. Arrhythmic risk stratification in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathies remains challenging despite significant advances. Progressive refinement in precision has accompanied a shift from a restrictive, functional assessment towards an integrated, substrate-driven precision model. CMR represents the cornerstone of this evolution.

candidates.title: Early Prediction of Cardiomyopathy in Pediatric Cancer Survivors Using Echocardiographic Video-Based Deep Learning.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiomyopathy (CM) is a leading cause of late mortality in childhood cancer survivors, but it is often identified only after irreversible cardiac remodeling has already occurred. In this proof-of-concept study, we assessed whether deep learning applied to routine echocardiographic videos can identify features predictive of future CM.
METHODS: We analyzed parasternal short-axis clips from cancer survivors ≤21 years old at cancer diagnosis. 3D deep convolutional neural networks were trained to classify CM-positive versus CM-negative studies from echocardiograms conducted up to five years prior to CM diagnosis. The performance was assessed on internal hold-out validation (Center 1) and external validation cohorts (Centers 2, 3). The model's prognostic value was evaluated by stratifying patients into high- and low-risk groups for developing CM, and probability of future CM was assessed using cumulative incidence and proportional hazards regression analysis.
RESULTS: The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.87±0.05 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.74±0.07 on the internal hold-out set. External validation showed near-chance single-study discrimination (AUROC 0.55±0.02 and 0.60±0.03; AUPRC 0.22±0.02 and 0.21±0.03 for Centers 2 and 3, respectively). Nevertheless, analysis of the external cohort showed significantly higher probability of CM in high- versus low-risk groups (hazard ratio 2.78, 95% CI = 1.52-5.10, p = 0.00056).
CONCLUSION: Deep learning models have the potential to identify subtle echocardiographic markers years before CM diagnosis in pediatric cancer survivors and could serve as a preliminary step toward risk-guided CM surveillance. Further refinement and validation are needed to determine the utility of deep learning for early identification of pathologic cardiac remodeling in this population.

candidates.title: Comparative evaluation of serum TGF-β1 and PDGF-BB levels across patients with normal coronary arteries, stable coronary artery disease, and acute coronary syndrome.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare serum levels of Transforming Growth Factor-Beta (TGF-β) and Platelet-Derived Growth Factor-BB (PDGF-BB) among patients with normal coronary arteries (NCA) and those with coronary artery disease (CAD) subclasses [stable CAD and acute coronary syndrome (ACS)], and to evaluate their potential diagnostic value and discriminatory power, particularly in identifying stable CAD.
METHODS: This single-center, cross-sectional study included 176 patients who underwent coronary angiography. Participants were classified into normal coronary artery (NCA; symptomatic control), stable CAD, and ACS groups. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical data were recorded. Blood samples were collected for the analysis of TGF-β1 and PDGF-BB levels using ELISA kits.
RESULTS: Hypertension and diabetes mellitus were significantly more prevalent in the stable CAD group compared to others (p < 0.001). Both TGF-β and PDGF-BB levels were significantly elevated in patients with stable CAD compared to individuals with normal coronary arteries and those with ACS (p < 0.001). Multivariate regression analysis identified hypertension, diabetes, TGF-β, and PDGF-BB as independent predictors of stable CAD (p < 0.01 for all). ROC curve analysis demonstrated good diagnostic performance for TGF-β and PDGF-BB individually (AUC = 0.847, 0.798, respectively), with combined assessment further improving accuracy (AUC = 0.924).
CONCLUSION: Serum TGF-β and PDGF-BB levels are significantly increased in stable CAD patients relative to those with ACS and normal coronary anatomy. The combined evaluation of these biomarkers provides high diagnostic accuracy in distinguishing stable CAD, underscoring their potential role in the non-invasive assessment of chronic atherosclerotic disease. These findings support the use of TGF-β and PDGF-BB as complementary biomarkers for early identification and risk stratification in stable CAD.

candidates.title: Severe continuous prosthetic mitral regurgitation from chordal rupture after valve-sparing replacement: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: After mitral valve replacement with preservation of the subvalvular apparatus, prosthetic dysfunction resulting from retained native structures is extremely rare. When it occurs, it may directly threaten the patient's life. We report an unusual case of severe regurgitation resulting from preserved chordal rupture. The key distinction of this case is the presentation of late, severe continuous prosthetic regurgitation and reversibility.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man had undergone double mechanical valve replacement for severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with mild regurgitation and concomitant aortic regurgitation three years earlier. During surgery, the posterior mitral leaflet and its entire subvalvular apparatus were preserved. Current transesophageal echocardiography revealed a mobile, cord-like structure between the lateral occluder and the prosthetic sewing ring, interfering with leaflet excursion and preventing full closure. This was accompanied by severe prosthetic mitral continuous regurgitation. Surgical findings revealed a ruptured chordae tendineae at the papillary muscle attachment, with the remnant preventing leaflet coaptation. Surgical excision of the ruptured chordal remnant successfully restored normal leaflet function, with complete resolution of the regurgitation confirmed on intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography.
CONCLUSIONS: When obstruction or regurgitation develops after valve replacement with subvalvular preservation, uncommon causes-such as residual subvalvular tissue or ruptured chordal entrapment-should be considered after excluding more common etiologies. This case illustrates the critical role of transesophageal echocardiography in the diagnosis of chordal entrapment after mitral valve replacement and potentially in preventing complications. The potential benefit of preserving the subvalvular apparatus warrants thoughtful deliberation. Surgical removal of the offending tissue or valve replacement remains the def

candidates.title: A giant left ventricular aneurysm in an apparently asymptomatic child. the value of multimodality assessment for risk stratification.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital left ventricular aneurysm (LVA) is a rare abnormality most commonly located at the LV apex. It must be differentiated from left ventricular diverticulum (LVD). Congenital LVA is typically isolated, whereas the latter is often associated with other congenital heart disease and midline thoraco-abdominal wall defects.
CASE PRESENTATION: A large apical LVA was diagnosed in a 3-year-old girl referred after incidental cardiomegaly was detected on chest radiography. At this center, LVA was confirmed by echocardiography, magnetic resonance imaging, and angiography. The patient subsequently underwent surgical aneurysmorrhaphy. Notably, during surgical resection, the aneurysm was found to be filled with massive thrombotic material, composed primarily of extensive thin fibrous tissue and appeared highly prone to rupture. This case highlights the potential discrepancy between clinical presentation and disease severity, especially in a 3 year who is unaware of important clinical symptoms in this regard. The pathological report confirmed the diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Left ventricular aneurysm appears as an akinetic or dyskinetic protrusion composed primarily of fibrous tissue and lacking organized myocardium. Although some patients can be managed medically, others require surgical intervention to prevent lethal complications.

candidates.title: Diabetic retinopathy enhances coronary artery calcium-based cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with type 2 diabetes: insights from the ACCoDiab study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The coronary artery calcium (CAC) score is a validated imaging biomarker enhancing cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, residual risk persists, particularly among patients with moderate CAC scores. Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a microvascular complication of diabetes, may reflect systemic vascular vulnerability and provide additional prognostic information.
METHODS: This observational cohort study was conducted as part of the primary prevention ACCoDiab study. 424 patients with T2DM (175 females and 249 males, with a mean age of 61 years) and no history of cardiovascular events underwent CAC scoring and clinical assessments, including DR screening. Patients were monitored for seven years or until the first cardiovascular events, including nonfatal myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, hospitalization for heart failure, peripheral artery disease revascularization, and cardiovascular death. Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and net reclassification improvement (NRI) were used to evaluate the added prognostic value of DR to CAC scoring and to develop a simple integrated cardiovascular risk score.
RESULTS: Fifty patients (11.8%) had incident cardiovascular events. DR was significantly more prevalent among those who experienced events (58% vs. 25%, p < 0.001). Both CAC score and DR were independently associated with cardiovascular events. When incorporating DR into the CAC-based risk model, the predictive power was significantly enhanced AUC 75 [0.69-0.82] vs. 68 [0.61-0.75], p = 0.01). Further improvement was observed after adjusting for traditional risk factors (AUC 79 [0.73-0.86] vs. 73 [0.66-0.81], p = 0.04). The presence of DR reclassified a significant proportion of patients into higher-risk categories, particularly those with low and moderate CAC scores. Additionally, the severity of DR was also found to provide incremental prognostic

candidates.title: Inflammation-based phenotyping and prognostic implications in patients with non-obstructive coronary artery disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-obstructive coronary artery disease (NOCAD) represents an increasing proportion of patients presenting with angina, yet these patients face significant cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to explore distinct classes in NOCAD patients based on demographic characteristics, clinical comorbidities, and inflammatory biomarkers, and to investigate their associations with prognosis.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients diagnosed with NOCAD by coronary angiography for angina between January 1, 2023, and December 1, 2024, with follow-up until August 1, 2025. Latent Class Analysis (LCA) was employed to identify distinct classes based on demographic features, inflammatory markers, including 8 composite inflammatory indices. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the associations between different classes and individual inflammatory markers with clinical outcomes after multivariate adjustment. Prognostic discrimination compared with traditional risk factors was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.
RESULTS: Among 342 NOCAD patients, LCA identified three distinct classes: low-inflammation with few comorbidities (n = 156, 45.6%), elderly with multiple comorbidities (n = 126, 36.8%), and high-inflammation subgroup (n = 60, 17.5%). Over a median follow-up of 363 days (interquartile range, 193-613 days), 89 patients (26.0%) experienced MACEs. In fully adjusted models, the high-inflammation class was the strongest predictor of MACEs (HR 3.090, 95% CI: 1.614-5.919), followed by the elderly with multiple comorbidities class (HR 2.181, 95% CI: 1.224-3.886). Among 8 composite inflammatory indices evaluated, three demonstrated significant associations with MACEs: the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index (per unit increase in Z-score, HR 0.402, 95% CI: 0.230-0.703), neutrophil-to-albumin ratio (NAR) index (per unit increase in Z

candidates.title: [Usefulness of a Split-bolus Injection Protocol for Pediatric Cardiac CT in Congenital Heart Disease].
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: To propose a split-bolus contrast injection protocol for pediatric cardiac CT and to evaluate its usefulness by comparing it with the early phase protocol and systemic circulation protocol.
METHODS: Thirty patients were included in each of the following three protocols: the early phase protocol; the systemic circulation protocol, in which contrast medium was injected slowly over a prolonged period and CT was performed after systemic circulation; and the split-bolus protocol. CT attenuation values were measured in the ascending aorta, descending aorta, pulmonary artery, pulmonary veins, and superior vena cava and compared among the three protocols. In addition, two radiologic technologists independently assessed vascular visualization using a four-point visual scoring system.
RESULTS: CT attenuation values obtained with the split-bolus protocol showed no significant differences from those of the early phase protocol in the ascending aorta, descending aorta, pulmonary artery, or pulmonary veins (p=0.282, 0.174, 0.632, and 0.159, respectively), whereas significant differences were observed compared with the systemic circulation protocol (all p<0.001). In contrast, no significant difference in CT attenuation of the superior vena cava was observed between the split-bolus protocol and the systemic circulation protocol (p=0.923). In the visual evaluation, the split-bolus protocol achieved a median score of 4 for all evaluated vessels across all cases.
CONCLUSION: The split-bolus protocol may enable visualization of the superior vena cava while maintaining contrast enhancement of the aorta, pulmonary artery, and pulmonary veins, suggesting that it may be a useful contrast injection protocol for pediatric cardiac CT.

candidates.title: [Advances in Cardiac Sympathetic PET Imaging: Development and Clinical Translation of 18F-fluproxadine (18F-AF78)].
candidates.journal: Kaku igaku. The Japanese journal of nuclear medicine
candidates.abstract: The cardiac sympathetic nervous system plays an important role in the pathophysiology and prognosis of heart failure, ischemic heart disease, and arrhythmias. Cardiac sympathetic innervation has traditionally been assessed using 123I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine (123I-MIBG) SPECT and 11C-hydroxyephedrine (11C-HED) PET. However, these approaches have limitations related to spatial resolution, quantitative capability, physical half-life, and dependence on specialized facilities. 18F-fluproxadine, formerly known as 18F-AF78, is a novel PET tracer targeting the norepinephrine transporter (NET) at sympathetic nerve terminals. Preclinical studies have demonstrated its high NET affinity, favorable myocardial uptake, and potential to reflect intravesicular neuronal dynamics. In addition, structure-activity relationship analyses, investigations of interactions with organic cation transporters (OCTs), development of a clinical radiosynthesis method, and First-in-Human evaluation have provided a foundation for clinical translation. This review summarizes the development of 18F-fluproxadine PET and discusses future perspectives for cardiac sympathetic nerve imaging.

candidates.title: [Clinical characteristics and prognosis of patients with atrial functional mitral regurgitation].
candidates.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
candidates.abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinical characteristics and prognosis of atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR). Methods: This was a single-center retrospective study. Patients hospitalized at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University between January 2020 and March 2022 and diagnosed with significant functional mitral regurgitation were enrolled. According to the type of regurgitation, patients were divided into the AFMR group and the ventricular functional mitral regurgitation (VFMR) group. Clinical and echocardiographic data were compared between the two groups. The patients were followed up until April 2024. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, and the secondary endpoint was the composite of cardiac death and hospitalization for heart failure. Survival was compared between the two groups using Kaplan-Meier survival curves. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with all-cause mortality in patients with functional mitral regurgitation. Results: The study cohort consisted of 269 patients, with a median age of 66.0 (57.5, 76.0) years, among whom 172 (63.9%) were male. Patients were divided into the AFMR group (n=61, 22.7%) and the VFMR group (n=208, 77.3%). Compared with the VFMR group, the AFMR group had a higher proportion of female patients, older age, a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, lower prevalences of coronary artery disease, fewer patients with heart failure symptoms, and a lower proportion of prior visits to cardiovascular departments (all P<0.05). Compared with the VFMR group, the AFMR group demonstrated significantly larger anteroposterior left atrial diameter, right atrial transverse diameter, and right ventricular transverse diameter, along with a higher LVEF and a higher prevalence of moderate or greater tricuspid regurgitation (all P<0.05). candidates.title: [The predictive value of left ventricular strain on cardiac magnetic resonance for adverse events in children and adolescent patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy].
candidates.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
candidates.abstract: Objective: To investigate the role of left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS) derived from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature-tracking in evaluating left ventricular systolic function in children and adolescents with primary hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), as well as its prognostic value for adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Methods: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study. Patients with primary HCM aged ≤21 years who underwent standard CMR examination at Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between January 2010 and December 2018 were included. Baseline clinical and CMR data were collected, and follow-up was completed. The primary endpoint was composite adverse cardiovascular events, and the secondary endpoint was heart failure-related events. Patients were divided into the event group and the non-event group according to whether the primary endpoint occurred. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression models were used to identify independent factors associated with composite adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure-related events. Using the cohort median left ventricular GLS of -9.2% as the cut-off value, patients were stratified into the preserved GLS group (≤-9.2%) and the impaired GLS group (>-9.2%). Kaplan-Meier survival curves were plotted, and the log-rank test was performed to compare survival differences between groups. Results: A total of 249 children and adolescents with HCM were included, aged (14.81±3.71)years, of whom 163 were males (65.5%). The follow-up duration was (66.59±33.00)months. Composite endpoint events occurred in 37 patients, including 17 heart failure-related events and 20 sudden cardiac death events; 212 patients remained event-free. candidates.title: Cardiovascular Toxicity Across the Cancer Immunotherapy Spectrum: Mechanisms and Management in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (ICI) and Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell (CAR-T) Therapy.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review evaluates the evolving landscape of cardiovascular toxicities associated with two pillars of modern cancer treatment: immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. It examines their distinct immune-mediated pathophysiologies, clinical manifestations, and management frameworks.
RECENT FINDINGS: While ICIs carry a clinical trial incidence for cardiotoxicity of approximately 1%, real-world data suggest rates of 3-5%, with myocarditis sometimes manifesting early as part of a high-mortality "Triple M" or overlap syndrome. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) occur in nearly 50% of ICI-myocarditis cases. Diagnosis relies on clinical presentation, biomarkers and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) using the modified Lake Louise criteria, with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) detection sensitivity increasing from 21.6% to 72.0% when imaged after four days of symptoms. Conversely, CAR-T cardiotoxicity is predominantly driven by cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which affects 49-93% of patients with currently licensed products. Severe CRS more than doubles the risk of cardiovascular events, including a 6-10% incidence of LVEF decline and a 4-18% incidence of arrhythmias. Recent advancements include machine learning models to predict MACE and structured screening programs to risk-stratify candidates. Cardiotoxicity remains a significant complication, highlighting the need for vigilant monitoring and early intervention. Management relies on baseline risk assessment and rapid deployment of targeted therapies, such as high-dose methylprednisolone for ICI-myocarditis and IL-6 inhibition (tocilizumab) for CAR-T-related CRS. A multidisciplinary cardio-oncology approach is essential to mitigate risks.
