candidates.title: Cardiac papillary fibroelastoma arising from the right atrial septum: A rare case report.
candidates.journal: The Journal of international medical research
candidates.abstract: We describe an exceedingly rare case of an asymptomatic papillary fibroelastoma arising from the right atrial septum in a patient in his early 40s. Furthermore, we retrospectively reviewed previously reported right atrial and interatrial-septal papillary fibroelastoma cases. Papillary fibroelastoma is a benign primary cardiac tumor involving theoretical embolic risk, and right-sided lesions might precipitate pulmonary embolism. Considering the pedunculated morphology and high mobility of the lesion, the patient underwent surgical resection with an uneventful postoperative course free from perioperative embolic complications and remained asymptomatic without thromboembolic events during the 14-month follow-up. Transthoracic echocardiography serves as a robust modality for diagnosing and morphologically characterizing this rare cardiac neoplasm.

candidates.title: Metabolic, Atherogenic, and Anthropometric Markers for Discrimination of Premature Coronary Artery Disease in a Predominantly Statin-Treated Cohort.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) is increasingly recognized in younger adults and requires improved risk stratification. Conventional lipid markers may have limited discriminative value, particularly when lipid levels reflect ongoing statin therapy. This study evaluated the associations and discriminatory performance of metabolic, atherogenic, and anthropometric indices for PCAD and developed internally validated dynamic nomograms for PCAD case discrimination.
PATIENT AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective case-control study used data from the Iran Premature Coronary Artery Disease registry. A total of 3063 adults undergoing coronary angiography were included, comprising 1929 patients with PCAD and 1134 controls. Twelve metabolic, lipid-based, and anthropometric indices were calculated from fasting glucose, lipid profiles, and body measurements. Participants were randomly divided into training and validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. Logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration assessment, integrated discrimination improvement, net reclassification improvement, and decision-curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance.
RESULTS: Atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), and a body shape index (ABSI) showed consistent independent associations with PCAD. Individually, these indices showed modest discrimination. The conventional clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.677. Adding AIP and binary ABSI increased the AUC to 0.721, while the TyG plus binary ABSI model showed the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.724, representing modest but statistically significant improvements over the conventional model. Both final models showed favorable internal calibration, and improvement in reclassification metrics, and decision-curve net benefit. Two dynamic web-based nomograms were developed for individualized PCAD case discrimination.

candidates.title: Etiology and Left Ventricular Function in Right Bundle Branch Block: A Prospective Observational Study.
candidates.journal: The Journal of the Association of Physicians of India
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE OF STUDY: Right bundle branch block (RBBB) is a common ECG finding. It may be caused by coronary artery disease, dilated cardiomyopathy, chronic obstructive lung disease, or degenerative disease of the conduction system of the heart. The purpose of the study was to find out the etiology and left ventricular function in patients with RBBB coming to a tertiary care hospital.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: All consecutive patients coming to our hospital on an outdoor or inpatient basis with ECG showing RBBB were studied. Detailed history and physical examination were done. All patients were subjected to echocardiography.
RESULTS: 201 patients with RBBB were studied. Mean age was 61.01 ± 12.92 years. 157 were male (78.11%), and 44 (21.89%) were female. The most Common symptom was dyspnea in 81 patients (40.29%) and chest pain in 15 patients(7.46%). Four patients presented with syncope and were proved to have intermittent complete heart block. 95 persons (47.26%) with RBBB had no symptoms, 43 out of which had come for clearance for noncardiac surgery. On echocardiography, left ventricular hypertrophy was present in 32 patients (15.92%), regional wall motion abnormality in 45 patients (22.38%), and left ventricular global hypokinesia in 13 patients (6.46%). LV systolic dysfunction was present in 43 patients (21.39%), and 85 (42.28%) patients had a normal study.
CONCLUSION: The most common presentation in patients was dyspnea. About half of the patients were asymptomatic. Around 20% were detected to have RBBB when they came for clearance for noncardiac surgery. Common causes were coronary artery disease, dilated cardiomyopathy, and cor pulmonale.

candidates.title: Sudden cardiac arrest during diagnostic workup: a rare case of high-risk interarterial left anterior descending artery anomaly.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery anomalies are anatomical abnormalities involving abnormal origin, course, or termination of any of the three main epicardial arteries. These abnormalities may go unnoticed during a person's lifetime; however, they can occasionally present acutely or chronically as angina, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmias, or even sudden cardiac death.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 65-year-old woman with angina and stress-induced ST-segment depression in a treadmill test. Coronary angiography showed the absence of the left main coronary artery with separate origins of the left anterior descending artery and circumflex artery. During a planned cardiac computed tomography angiography scan, the patient presented with cardiac arrest secondary to ventricular fibrillation and was hospitalized. A high-risk interarterial course of the left anterior descending artery was identified, and coronary artery bypass grafting with surgical mobilization of the left anterior descending artery along its interarterial course, where it was ligated with a hemoclip prior to the first septal branch to prevent competitive flow. The postoperative course was uneventful.
CONCLUSIONS: When this rare anomaly is detected in the population, clinicians must identify the risk of fatal events and determine appropriate management based on age, symptoms, vascular anatomy, and the presence of arrhythmia.

candidates.title: The CML/esRAGE ratio as a potential biomarker of early diastolic impairment in asymptomatic type 1 diabetic patients without overt heart disease.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is a prevalent complication of diabetic microangiopathy, and early identification of myocardial dysfuntion is crucial. Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) bind to their receptor RAGE and further promote diabetic late complications as well as heart failure. Two soluble RAGE isoforms, endogenous secretory RAGE (esRAGE) and the cleaved extracellular fragment of membrane RAGE (collectively termed sRAGE), are believed to exert cardioprotective effects by acting as RAGE decoy receptors. This pilot study aimed to investigate the associations of AGEs, sRAGE and esRAGE with early cardiac dysfunction identified via advanced echocardiography.
METHODS: We enrolled 29 type 1 diabetic patients without known heart disease(EF ≥ 50%) and 31 healthy controls. Plasma levels of two major AGEs, carboxymethyllysine(CML) and methylglyoxal-derived hydroimidazolone 1(MG-H1), as well as sRAGE and esRAGE were measured using immunoassay. Conventional, tissue Doppler, and speckle-tracking echocardiography were performed.
RESULTS: In the diabetic group, global longitudinal strain (GLS) and peak early diastolic velocity at the lateral mitral annulus [e(lat)] were significantly lower, while E/e(lat) was higher. CML levels and CML/esRAGE ratio were increased, and esRAGE was decreased in the diabetic group. CONCLUSION: Elevated CML/esRAGE ratio is associated with

candidates.title: Refractory rapidly progressive diffuse in-stent restenosis with left main involvement: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-eluting stents (DES) have significantly reduced the incidence of in-stent restenosis (ISR). However, a subset of patients still develop refractory, rapidly progressive, and diffuse ISR, which poses substantial therapeutic challenges and reflects its complex underlying mechanisms.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 46-year-old male who underwent five percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) over five years, with repeated diffuse ISR in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). Initial PCI was followed by DCB therapy after first ISR, achieving temporary symptom relief. Four years later, ISR progressed to chronic total occlusion, requiring further stenting and DCB therapy. Within five months, he developed 99% LM stenosis and recurrent LAD ISR. Despite a SYNTAX score of 36 favoring CABG, the patient refused surgery. Under intra-aortic balloon pump support, a balloon-only PCI (stent-less) strategy was performed. IVUS revealed diffuse fibrous proliferation and neoatherosclerosis. During follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable overall.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights a potential systemic hyperproliferative phenotype, in which repeated vascular injury triggers accelerated neoatherosclerosis and intimal hyperplasia. It challenges the conventional view of ISR as a local mechanical problem and underscores the importance of mechanism-driven risk stratification and individualized management, particularly when standard surgical therapy is declined.

candidates.title: Cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes: insights from myocardial strain and renal Doppler assessment.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may be accompanied by subclinical cardiac and renal injury before overt disease appears. This study evaluated early cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early T2DM using myocardial strain imaging and renal Doppler assessment.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 180 participants: 60 with prediabetes, 60 with newly diagnosed T2DM (≤ 2 years), and 60 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography were used to assess left ventricular (LV) function and left atrial (LA) mechanics. Renal vascular resistance was assessed using the Doppler-derived renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI). Glycemic status and albuminuria were evaluated using fasting glucose, oral glucose tolerance testing, HbA1c, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, participants with prediabetes and T2DM showed early alterations in LV relaxation/filling indices and reduced LA strain. LV ejection fraction was modestly lower, while GLS became progressively less negative across the dysglycemic groups (p < 0.001), consistent with reduced longitudinal myocardial deformation. Renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI) were significantly increased in the dysglycemic groups. RRI correlated positively with E/e', linking higher renal vascular resistance with higher estimated LV filling pressure (r = 0.440, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Prediabetes and early T2DM were associated with subclinical abnormalities in myocardial mechanics and renal vascular indices despite preserved conventional cardiac and renal function. Myocardial strain and renal Doppler measures may provide complementary phenotypic information, but prospective validation is required before routine clinical application.

candidates.title: Association between coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance and ischemic stroke in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a devastating complication following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Coronary microcirculatory dysfunction (CMD) is implicated in adverse post-STEMI outcomes, but its relationship with subsequent stroke is unknown. We aimed to investigate the association of the coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (caIMR), a novel non-invasive tool for assessing CMD, for new-onset ischemic stroke in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI).
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study enrolled 602 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent successful pPCI between July 2020 and February 2025. The caIMR was calculated post-procedure using specialized software. The primary endpoint was new-onset ischemic stroke. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to assess the association between caIMR and stroke risk.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 29.3 months, 38 patients (6.3%) developed a new-onset ischemic stroke. In the multivariable Cox model, caIMR was independently associated with the risk of ischemic stroke (HR: 1.044, 95% CI: 1.022-1.065, P < 0.001), along with new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR: 9.113, 95% CI: 4.587-18.107, P < 0.001). A linear dose-response relationship was observed between caIMR levels and the risk of stroke (P for non-linearity = 0.975). Reclassification analysis showed that adding caIMR improved risk classification, with an IDI of 0.0307 (95% CI: 0.0031-0.0636; P = 0.030) and an NRI of 0.3887 (95% CI: 0.3156-0.4618; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Elevated caIMR is independently associated with an increased risk of long-term ischemic stroke in STEMI patients after pPCI. This easily accessible metric may serve as a valuable tool for future risk stratification in this patient population.

candidates.title: Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branches of Bifurcation Lesions: OCVC-BIF Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary bifurcation lesions remain one of the most challenging lesions. In particular, satisfactory clinical outcomes have not yet been achieved for side branches. The use of drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has demonstrated acceptable clinical outcomes in native coronary arteries. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of additional DCB inflation in the side branches of bifurcation lesions.
METHODS: The OCVC-BIF study (Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branch of Bifurcation Lesions) was conducted as a multicenter, randomized, open-label trial. Patients with bifurcation lesions scheduled for drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation in the main vessel followed by kissing balloon inflation were enrolled in the study. The patients were randomized to receive either additional dilatation of the side branch using a DCB after DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation (DCB group) or only DES implantation with kissing balloon inflation using conventional balloons (non-DCB group). The primary end point was restenosis of the side branch, assessed using scheduled coronary angiography at 9 months or symptom-driven coronary angiography during the 1-year follow-up. Restenosis was defined as ≥50% stenosis of the side branch, determined using 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography. The key secondary end points included major adverse cardiac events at 12 months, which were defined as a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, clinically driven target lesion revascularization, and stent thrombosis.
RESULTS: In total, 299 patients were randomized into the DCB (151 patients) and non-DCB (148 patients) groups between October 2019 and September 2024. Serial 3-dimensional bifurcation quantitative coronary angiography evaluation was performed in 262 (87.6%) patients. The restenosis rate was lower in the DCB group than that in the non-DCB group (8.1% versus 18.3%, P=0.012). However, the incidence of maj

candidates.title: Impact of Coronary Artery Disease on Long-Term Valve Function After the Ozaki Procedure: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study (2015 - 2020).
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Ozaki procedure reconstructs the aortic valve with autologous pericardium, but long-term leaflet durability remains uncertain. Coronary artery disease (CAD) may reflect a systemic atheroinflammatory milieu associated with impaired leaflet integrity.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 733 patients undergoing Ozaki reconstruction from 2015 to 2020 and assessed the association between CAD and aortic regurgitation (AR) ≥ 2 at last echocardiographic follow-up. Baseline heterogeneity was addressed using propensity-score overlap weighting based on age, sex, body mass index, body surface area, weight, diabetes, European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II, aortic stenosis, bicuspid valve, and peripheral artery disease. Effects were estimated as weighted risk ratios (RRs) using Poisson models with robust variance. Sensitivity analyses used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and an extended model including prior myocardial infarction/percutaneous coronary intervention.
RESULTS: Of 733 patients, 365 (49.8%) had CAD. Unadjusted AR > 2 rates were 10.1% in CAD vs. 5.7% in no-CAD patients (P = 0.037). After overlap weighting, weighted risks were 12.7% vs. 6.2%, yielding RR 2.05 (95% CI, 1.01 - 4.18; P = 0.048), with excellent covariate balance. IPTW showed consistent results: RR 2.22 (95% CI, 1.38 - 3.56; P = 0.001). Regurgitation-free survival was lower in CAD patients (log-rank P = 0.0087).
CONCLUSION: CAD was associated with an approximately two-fold higher risk of AR ≥ 2 after Ozaki reconstruction. This association likely reflects systemic atheroinflammatory processes rather than a direct mechanical effect, supporting closer postoperative surveillance in CAD patients.

candidates.title: Surgical Treatment of Rare Multiple Cardiac Myxomas: A 13-Year Clinical Experience at a Single Institution.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac myxoma (CM) is the most common primary cardiac tumor. Multiple CMs are rare and can lead to heart failure and arterial embolism. This study aimed to explore clinical characteristics, surgical treatment experience, and follow-up strategies for multiple CMs.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on eight patients with multiple CMs who underwent surgical treatment. Clinical characteristics were analyzed by extracting relevant clinical data, electrocardiography and echocardiography findings, surgical treatment details, and postoperative follow-up information. All patients had undergone cardiopulmonary bypass surgery. Pathological analysis was performed on all tumors, and postoperative cardiac ultrasound follow-up was also conducted.
RESULTS: Multiple CMs were uncommon, representing only 5.9% of all cases. Among 136 patients with cardiac tumors admitted during the same period, only eight had multiple CMs. All patients with multiple CMs underwent complete tumor resection. The size of the resected tumors was approximately 5-80 (39.3 ± 20.3) mm. The follow-up period ranged from one to nine years. The recurrence rate was 37.5% (3/8), and all recurrent cases underwent reoperation for tumor resection. There were no perioperative deaths, and overall surgical outcomes were satisfactory.
CONCLUSION: Our study reveals that surgery is the best strategy for multiple CMs. The tumor should be completely resected, and color Doppler echocardiography is recommended every six months postoperatively to detect tumor recurrence. Those cases of multiple myxomas have had high recurrence rate after resection (37.5%) but were submitted successfully to a new resection. Timely surgical resection provides favorable outcomes for patients with multiple or recurrent CMs.

candidates.title: Efficacy of tafamidis across age groups in ATTR-CM: insights from real-world data.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Elderly patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remain underrepresented in clinical trials. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of tafamidis 61 mg in patients with ATTR-CM across different age groups.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis 61 mg were stratified into age groups: < 75, 75-85, > 85 years. Clinical and echocardiographic data were collected at baseline and follow-up. The primary outcome - cardiovascular-related hospitalization and cardiovascular death - was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 89 patients with ATTR-CM were included: < 75 (n = 23), 75-85 (n = 40), and > 85 years (n = 26). Hereditary ATTR-CM was more prevalent in younger patients (p < 0.001). Older patients (≥ 75) were more often in NYHA class II/III (p = 0.009), required higher diuretic doses (p < 0.001), and had higher NT-proBNP (p = 0.002). At baseline, patients ≥ 75 years had greater maximal wall thickness (p < 0.001) and left ventricular mass (p = 0.034); global longitudinal strain was most impaired in those > 85 years (p = 0.039). Over a mean follow-up time of 27.4 ± 19.3 months, tafamidis treatment in patients > 85 years was associated with a greater reduction in NT-proBNP (p = 0.041) and in diuretic doses compared to those < 75 years (p = 0.044). No significant changes were observed in NYHA class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire scores, or echocardiographic parameters. The composite outcome of cardiovascular-related hospitalization and cardiovascular death did not differ significantly among age groups (Log-Rank 5.71, p = 0.06).
CONCLUSIONS: This study underscores the benefits of tafamidis in elderly patients, including those aged > 85 years, and supports its use across all age groups to improve cardiovascular outcomes in ATTR-CM.

candidates.title: Left ventricular dysfunction and massive intracavitary thrombus in unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot with endomyocardial fibroelastosis: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Left ventricular dysfunction and thrombosis in unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot are rarely reported. We report the case of a 9-year-old boy with unrepaired tetralogy of Fallot, severe biventricular dysfunction, large left ventricular thrombus, and diffuse subendocardial fibroelastosis. After surgical repair, recovery of ventricular function and thrombus resolution were observed. This case highlights the interplay between cyanosis, myocardial remodelling, and hypercoagulability and emphasises the role of multimodality imaging.

candidates.title: Heterotaxy Syndrome Combining Univentricular Heart, Polysplenia and Truncated Pancreas: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Univentricular heart is a complex congenital heart disease with rare survival into adulthood. It could be part of a heterotaxy syndrome when, apart from the cardiac malformations, there are associated abnormal arrangements of extra-cardiac organs like the lungs, spleen and pancreas. The syndrome is said to be rarer than the univentricular heart and to have a worse clinical outcome.
METHODS: After clinical assessment, the patient was investigated with Chest X-ray, Electrocardiography, Echocardiography, and contrast-enhanced CT scan of the chest and abdomen to make the diagnosis.
RESULTS: We hereby report the case of a 19-year-old female who survived into adulthood with a functional single ventricle, double outlet right ventricle, atrial septal defect and dextrocardia without surgical intervention. She also had other extra-cardiac congenital anomalies like a truncated pancreas and polysplenia.
CONCLUSION: Though survival to adulthood is rare without surgical intervention, the left isomerism subtype recorded here is milder and has better survival prospects.

candidates.title: Clinical spectrum and risk factors for severe arrhythmias in non-surgical pediatric patients: a single-center retrospective study.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the clinical spectrum and identify risk factors for severe arrhythmias in children.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective study was conducted on 428 consecutive children (0-18 years) diagnosed with arrhythmia between January 2021 and October 2025. Patients were classified as having severe arrhythmia-related clinical presentation (severe group, n = 107) or non-severe presentation (non-severe group, n = 321) according to the presence of hemodynamic instability, syncope, heart failure, or malignant arrhythmia features. Clinical spectrum characteristics were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for severe arrhythmias. Electrocardiographic (ECG), echocardiographic, and serological parameters were compared.
RESULTS: The severe group had higher proportions of infants/toddlers (0-3 years), underlying cardiac disease, syncope history, and class III-IV heart function (P < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified these as independent risk factors (P < 0.05): infant/toddler age [2.30 (1.08-4.89)], underlying cardiac disease [12.66 (6.01-26.68)], syncope history [45.84 (12.74-164.91)], and class III-IV heart function [32.97 (13.39-81.17)]. The prediction model showed good fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.171) and discrimination (AUC = 0.925, 95% CI: 0.893-0.958). The severe group also exhibited longer QTc, wider QRS, more third-degree atrioventricular block, higher ventricular premature burden, larger cardiac dimensions (LVEDD/LAD Z-score), higher pulmonary artery systolic pressure and myocardial injury/heart failure markers (CK-MB, cTnI, BNP, NT-proBNP), but lower heart rate variability (SDNN), left ventricular ejection fraction, and serum potassium (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Infant/toddler age, underlying cardiac disease, syncope history, and advanced heart failure are independent clinical risk factors for severe pediatric arrhythmias. A model incorporating these factors demonstrate

candidates.title: Left ventricular myxoma diagnosed by multimodal cardiac imaging with postoperative recurrence: a case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular myxoma is a rare benign cardiac tumour. Diagnosis relies on multimodal imaging, and postoperative recurrence is uncommon.
CASE PRESENTATION: A middle-aged woman with a two-week history of recurrent chest tightness and dyspnoea upon exertion was admitted to our hospital. Transthoracic and transoesophageal echocardiography revealed an irregular, hypoechoic mass (approximately 61 mm × 24 mm) in the left ventricular outflow tract. The mass had a broad base attached to the inferior and posterior walls of the left ventricle, involving the posterior mitral valve leaflet, partial chordae tendineae, and papillary muscles. It exhibited significant deformation and extensive mobility during the cardiac cycle, prolapsing towards the aortic valve orifice during systole and returning to the left ventricular inflow tract during diastole. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed a mass on the inferior and posterior walls of the left ventricle that involved the posterior mitral leaflet, partial chordae tendineae, and papillary muscles. The mass showed no significant enhancement, suggesting a benign lesion, with myxoma as the primary consideration. Whole-body positron emission tomography/computed tomography revealed a slightly hypodense patchy shadow within the left ventricular cavity adjacent to the mitral valve area, accompanied by calcification and mildly increased fluorodeoxyglucose metabolism. Therefore, malignancy could not be entirely excluded. Owing to the unusual location, extensive involvement, high mobility and deformability of the mass close to the aortic orifice, and the consequent risk of embolism, surgical resection of the cardiac myxoma along with mitral valve replacement was performed. At the six-month postoperative follow-up, tumour recurrence was detected by echocardiography.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the importance of multimodal cardiac imaging in the diagnosis of left ventricular myxoma, with echocardiography being the most

candidates.title: Early detection of myocardial fibrosis in patients with coronary microvascular dysfunction in the absence of late enhancement: role of T1 mapping and extracellular volume analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) can exacerbate myocardial fibrosis, which may further impair microvascular function. However, the relationship between CMD and the extracellular volume fraction (ECV) in patients with ischemia with no obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA) who are late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-negative remains undetermined. We used T1 mapping and ECV to assess diffuse myocardial tissue abnormalities and extracellular compartment expansion in LGE-negative patients with CMD. We then investigated how these markers correlate with global myocardial flow reserve (MFR).
METHODS: Between August 2024 and May 2026, we prospectively enrolled 86 LGE-negative patients with INOCA from a single center who underwent a positron emission tomography-magnetic resonance imaging (PET-MRI) protocol. Patients with significant epicardial stenosis (stenosis on coronary angiogram or computed tomography ≥ 50%), prior history of revascularization, known myocardial infarction, or heart failure were excluded. MFR and ECV were derived from PET perfusion imaging and pre- and post-T1 mapping, respectively. CMD was defined as PET-derived MFR of < 2.0 in at least one major coronary artery territory.
RESULTS: Among the 86 patients included, 39 (45.3%) were diagnosed with CMD. ECV was substantially higher in the CMD group (31.22 [29.93, 33.25]% vs. 26.66 [25.85, 27.55]%, P < 0.001), with a more modest but statistically significant elevation in native T1 (1225 ± 25 ms vs. 1212 ± 21 ms, P = 0.012). Multivariable linear regression revealed that only global MFR (β [95% confidence interval] = - 1.905 [- 2.489, - 1.321], P < 0.001) was an independent predictor of ECV in LGE-negative CMD patients. In the overall cohort, resting myocardial blood flow (MBF) (r = 0.539, P < 0.001) and global MFR (r = - 0.741, P < 0.001) were positively and negatively correlated with ECV, respectively. When participants were stratified into ECV tertiles, global MFR showed a progressive

candidates.title: Time-aligned segmental strain as a diagnostic marker for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chronic chest pain.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial strain curves provide valuable insights into coronary artery disease (CAD) beyond conventional peak strain measurements. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-aligned segmental strain and strain rate (S/SR) curves to identify obstructive CAD in consecutive chest pain patients.
METHODS: A total of 510 chest-pain patients referred to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were included. Segmental strain curves were time-aligned using aortic valve closure (AVC) and cardiac cycle length as reference points. Average S/SR curves were generated for 18 myocardial segments, establishing reference curves from a group of 314 chronic chest-pain patients without CAD (No-CAD). Deviations were defined based on thresholds of peak S/SR or average S/SR curve deviation over systole and the first half of diastole.
RESULTS: Significant differences were observed between groups, particularly between the revascularized MI, CABG, or 3-vessel CAD groups compared to the No-CAD group (p<0.05). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for CABG patients (AUC up to 0.933), while the detection rate for PCI was limited (AUC < 0.7). Global longitudinal strain rate in early diastole (GLSR E) and segmental peak SR E showed the highest diagnostic accuracy. These findings confirm that time-aligned strain analysis improves the detection of significant CAD but remains limited for identifying patients with mild disease.
CONCLUSION: Time-aligned segmental strain analysis improved detection of high-grade disease requiring CABG but could not distinguish single-vessel from non-obstructive CAD. Pathological strain patterns became significant only in advanced CAD, indicating that segmental resting strain analysis has clinical utility primarily for identifying advanced CAD.

candidates.title: Left-sided surgical approach for tricuspid valve replacement in congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis: A case report.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) is a rare congenital cardiac anomaly characterized by atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, resulting in a physiologically corrected circulation. When ccTGA is combined with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis, surgical management becomes particularly challenging because of the mirror-image anatomy and altered spatial orientation.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 61-year-old man presented with progressive dyspnea and was diagnosed with ccTGA accompanied by dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe regurgitation of the systemic atrioventricular valve (morphological tricuspid valve) with dilation and systolic dysfunction of the systemic right ventricle. Comprehensive preoperative imaging confirmed atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance, right-sided cardiac apex, and complete visceral inversion. Tricuspid valve replacement was performed via a median sternotomy with the surgeon standing on the patient's left side to accommodate the mirror-image anatomy. Cardiopulmonary bypass was established safely after meticulous identification of the great vessels. A mechanical prosthetic valve was successfully implanted. The postoperative course was uneventful, and follow-up echocardiography at six months confirmed satisfactory prosthetic valve function without complications.
CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates that tricuspid valve replacement can be safely and effectively performed in patients with ccTGA complicated by dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis. A left-sided surgical approach, combined with thorough preoperative imaging and careful intraoperative anatomical verification, may help restore operative orientation and reduce technical complexity in patients with mirror-image cardiac anatomy.

candidates.title: Emergency ascending aortic replacement for acute type a aortic dissection in a 31-week pregnant patient with Marfan syndrome.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute type A aortic dissection during pregnancy is a rare but life-threatening condition, with an estimated incidence of approximately 4 cases per 1 million women aged 15-45 years. Hormonal and hemodynamic changes during pregnancy are factors that may predispose to aortic dissection. These changes begin in the first and second trimesters but are most pronounced in the third trimester and the early postpartum period. Genetic syndromes, such as Marfan syndrome, significantly increase the risk of aortic dissection.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 41-year-old pregnant woman at 31 weeks of gestation with genetically confirmed Marfan syndrome presented with acute, severe, sharp retrosternal chest pain lasting four hours, radiating to the neck, accompanied by weakness and dizziness. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed dilation of the ascending aorta without significant aortic valve regurgitation. Computed tomography angiography confirmed the diagnosis of Stanford type A aortic dissection. Following a multidisciplinary team decision, an initial cesarean section with subsequent uterine artery embolization was performed, followed by emergency ascending aortic replacement. The patient and the newborn were successfully discharged on postoperative day 20.
CONCLUSIONS: Although aortic dissection during pregnancy is rare, clinicians must maintain a high suspicion index for pregnant women presenting with severe chest pain. Careful monitoring of patients with suspected or confirmed connective tissue disorders is essential. This case demonstrates that acute type A aortic dissection may occur in pregnant patients with Marfan syndrome despite only moderate aortic root enlargement and highlights the value of rapid multidisciplinary management, including coordinated obstetric, endovascular, and cardiac surgical intervention.

candidates.title: Association of the Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet Score with Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury and Mortality in Patients Underwent Coronary Angiography: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a frequent complication in patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG), which can cause deterioration of renal function and adverse clinical outcomes. This study aimed to explore the relationships between the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score and CA-AKI risk, as well as all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients undergoing CAG.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study enrolled patients undergoing CAG, including those receiving concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and stratified them according to the quartiles of the HALP score. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between HALP score and CA-AKI, and the Cox regression model was adopted to evaluate the relationship between HALP score and mortality.
RESULTS: This study included 42554 patients undergoing CAG. Among these, 5130 patients (12.1%) experienced CA-AKI. HALP score showed a significant inverse association with CA-AKI, with lower HALP score linked to higher CA-AKI risk. After adjusting for all the potential confounding variables, participants in the highest quartile of HALP score had the lowest risk of CA-AKI (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.73-0.90, p < 0.001). In Cox regression models, patients undergoing CAG with the highest HALP score exhibited the lowest risks of all-cause mortality (HR=0.65, 95% CI: 0.60-0.70, p < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality. (HR=0.65, 95% CI: 0.58-0.73, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The HALP score was independently associated with CA-AKI, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality among patients undergoing CAG.

candidates.title: Ten years of concomitant aortic and mitral replacement: trends, outcomes and the role of patient-prosthesis mismatch.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary data comparing double mechanical prostheses (DMP) vs. double biological prostheses (DBP) for concomitant aortic and mitral valve replacement are scarce, and the cumulative hemodynamic burden of simultaneous prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) at both positions has never been systematically assessed.
RESULTS: DMP recipients had lower in-hospital mortality (1.9% vs. 15.2%; P = 0.010) and superior 7-year survival (91.3% vs. 67.7%; P = 0.003), but significantly higher stroke rates (32.2% vs. 5.0%; P = 0.023). Combined PPM occurred in 64.6% of DBP vs. 14.8% of DMP (P < 0.001).
MAJOR FINDINGS: Concomitant double valve replacement confirmed its high-risk profile, with an overall in-hospital mortality of 10.5%. DMP demonstrated superior unadjusted survival (7-year: 91.3% vs. 67.7%; P = 0.003) but significantly higher stroke risk (32.2% vs. 5.0%; P = 0.023), without differences in major bleeding rates at follow-up (8.2% vs. 11.3%; P = 0.478), although baseline differences precluded definitive prosthesis-type recommendations after multivariable adjustment. Combined PPM is highly prevalent after DBP (64.6%) and emerged as a univariable mortality predictor (hazard ratio 1.97; P = 0.046); given the exploratory nature of the cPPM definition and its collinearity with prosthesis type, this should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrants validation in larger, ideally multicenter, cohorts.

candidates.title: Prevalence and prognostic role of left atrial reverse remodeling in patients undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: insights from the Multicenter Echocardiographic Registry of patients undergoing mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Atrial enlargement is a complex maladaptive process related to pressure and volume overload. Left atrial reverse remodeling (LARR) has been described as a result of medical and interventional therapies. We sought to explore LARR prevalence and its prognostic implications following mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER).
METHODS AND RESULTS: Four-hundred and twenty-five patients from the MERIT-TEER (Multicenter Echocardiographic Registry of patients undergoing M-TEER) who received a successful procedure from 2012 to 2024 with available left atrial volume (LAV) have been analyzed. LARR was defined as a reduction in LAV of at least 15%. LARR prevalence and its association with the risk of heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality at 4 years' follow-up were evaluated in the overall population and according to mitral regurgitation etiology.At short-term follow-up, LARR was observed in 124 patients (29.20%). LARR was more prevalent among primary mitral regurgitation (PMR) patients compared with those with ventricular secondary (vSMR) and atrial secondary mitral regurgitation (aSMR) (37.23, 27.19, and 18.33%; P = 0.017). At long-term follow-up, the composite outcome occurred in 153 patients (36.2%). LARR was independently associated with lower risk of events in the overall population [adjusted hazard ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43-0.85, P = 0.005] and among vSMR patients (adjusted hazard ratio 0.43, 95% CI 0.26-0.71, P = 0.001), but not in aSMR or PMR.
CONCLUSION: LARR was observed in less than one-third of patients undergoing M-TEER (29.2%), occurring more frequently in PMR. LARR was independently associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization in the overall population and particularly in patients with vSMR.

candidates.title: Trends in Use of Coronary Angiography, Percutaneous Coronary Intervention, and Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Over a Decade in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and coronary artery bypass graft are among the most commonly performed procedures globally. The influence of recent scientific evidence on national-level temporal trends remains poorly explored.
METHODS: The frequency, characteristics, and outcomes of elective and nonelective coronary angiography, PCI, and coronary artery bypass graft were described using the French National Hospitalization Database from 2014 to 2023 (covering a population of 67.0 million inhabitants), totaling 6 290 951 coronary interventions among 2 985 822 patients (mean age, 67.8±12.2 years; 69.9% men).
RESULTS: Over 10 years, the annual number of coronary interventions increased by 33%, driven by a rise in coronary angiography (+32%) and PCI (+40%), while coronary artery bypass graft decreased (-8%). The growth in PCI was predominantly related to an increase in elective procedures (from 53.5% to 56.9%, P<0.001), particularly among older patients (+73%), and in multivessel disease (from 16.7% in 2014-2015 to 19.0% in 2022-2023, P<0.001). Attempts to recanalize chronic total coronary occlusion doubled (from 1.9% to 3.3%, P<0.001). In-hospital death after PCI decreased (from 2.05% in 2014 to 1.58% in 2023, P for trend<0.001), with the most notable improvements observed in nonelective PCI. Similarly, in-hospital death after coronary artery bypass graft declined (from 3.5% to 2.9%, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore a significant increase in both coronary angiography and PCI over the past decade in France, particularly in procedures classified as elective among older patients. This trend raises questions about the influence of recent scientific evidence and guidelines on clinical practice in this country.

candidates.title: Residual Cardiovascular Risk Beyond Coronary Physiology: Complementary Prognostic Value of Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Patients Undergoing Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography With Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) enables noninvasive identification of flow-limiting coronary stenosis and is widely used for risk assessment. However, adverse cardiovascular events still occur in a subset of patients without functionally significant ischemia, suggesting that physiological assessment alone may not fully capture patient-level risk. We aimed to evaluate whether circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, provides complementary prognostic information.
METHODS: In this biobank-linked retrospective cohort study, 3978 patients undergoing clinically indicated coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR assessment were included. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured from cryopreserved samples obtained within ±30 days of imaging. Patients were stratified into high and low TMAO groups according to the receiver operating characteristic-derived threshold. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events during a median follow-up of ∼3 years. Multivariable Cox models evaluated associations between TMAO and outcomes, and incremental prognostic value beyond clinical variables and CT-FFR was assessed.
RESULTS: Event rates were similar across physiological strata (10.6% for CT-FFR ≤0.80 versus 10.0% for CT-FFR >0.80), indicating outcome heterogeneity beyond ischemia status. Higher TMAO levels were independently associated with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events after adjustment for clinical covariates and CT-FFR (hazard ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.44-2.31]; P<0.001). Addition of TMAO improved discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (C-index 0.552-0.591). Among patients with preserved CT-FFR, elevated TMAO identified a subgroup with higher event rates, whereas patients with preserved CT-FFR and low TMAO had the most favorable prognosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Physiological assessment and clinical outcomes are not synonymous in pat

candidates.title: En bloc excision of a large hydatid cyst originating from the posterior wall of the left ventricle.
candidates.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
candidates.abstract: Cardiac involvement in hydatid disease is rare and accounts for only a small proportion of all hydatid cyst cases. Owing to the risk of life-threatening complications, including compression of cardiac chambers, cyst rupture and anaphylactic shock, surgical resection is indicated. This case report describes the surgical management of a male patient with an incidentally detected cardiac hydatid cyst located on the posterior wall of the left ventricle. The cyst was completely excised en bloc through a left ventriculotomy. This video tutorial highlights the surgical techniques and technical considerations essential for the safe and effective en bloc resection of cardiac hydatid cysts.

candidates.title: 'Double-dunk' implantation of valveless ring-reinforced PTFE conduits for neonatal truncus arteriosus repair.
candidates.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
candidates.abstract: This case describes a neonatal truncus arteriosus repair using an 8 mm ring-reinforced, valved polytetrafluoroethylene conduit for right ventricular outflow tract reconstruction via the 'double-dunk' technique. The diagnosis was established prenatally in a patient with familial history of the disease. Anatomically, both pulmonary arteries arose adjacent to each other from the posterolateral common trunk; there was a mildly regurgitant quadricuspid truncal valve and an accidental finding of an intramural course of both coronary arteries.  Clinically, the neonate presented with mild cyanosis and pulmonary overcirculation. The postoperative course was complicated by ventilator-associated pneumonia requiring prolonged ventilation. Discharge echocardiography showed good biventricular function, unobstructed conduit flow and mild truncal valve regurgitation. At the 6-month follow-up, the patient remains clinically well.

candidates.title: Longitudinal Changes in Left Ventricular Structure and Function During a Dietary Weight-Management Trial in Adults with Heart Failure, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity: A Secondary Analysis of Pro-HEART.
candidates.abstract: Background: Obesity is associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in heart failure (HF), but changes during dietary weight management are not well described. We examined longitudinal changes in left ventricular (LV) structure and systolic function during a dietary weight-management intervention. Methods: Pro-HEART participants were randomized to high-protein or standard-protein hypocaloric diets. LV end-diastolic dimension (LVEDD), ejection fraction (LVEF), and posterior wall thickness (LVPWT) were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 15 months. Linear mixed-effects models tested time and diet effects. Results: At 15 months, LVEDD data were available for 31 of 92 participants (33.7%). Achieved protein intake was similar between randomized groups. Among 92 participants, LVEDD changed significantly over time (F(2, 51.20) = 7.45, p = 0.001), with model-estimated mean LVEDD decreasing from 59.00 mm at baseline to 54.56 mm at 15 months. LVEDD decreased from 3 to 15 months (-4.42 mm; 95% CI, -7.52 to -1.33; nominal p = 0.006; Holm-adjusted p = 0.012) and from baseline to 15 months (-4.44 mm; 95% CI, -6.86 to -2.02; nominal p < 0.001; Holm-adjusted p = 0.002). LVEF did not change significantly over time (overall p = 0.074); an exploratory baseline-to-15-month contrast was +4.11 percentage points (95% CI, 0.55-7.67; Holm-adjusted p = 0.072). LVPWT did not change significantly, and no diet group × time interactions were observed. Conclusions: LVEDD was lower at longer-term follow-up. LVEF did not change significantly over time, although an exploratory baseline-to-15-month contrast suggested an increase. Because both groups received hypocaloric diets, there was no non-dietary control group, and longitudinal HF medication data were unavailable, the observed cardiac changes cannot be attributed specifically to weight loss or the dietary intervention.

candidates.title: Tracking Active Fibroblast-Mediated Tissue Remodelling in Cardiomyopathies: Translational Insights from FAPI PET Imaging.
candidates.abstract: Myocardial fibrosis is a major pathological component of cardiac remodelling and contributes to ventricular stiffness, impaired myocardial function, heart failure progression, and arrhythmic vulnerability across a broad spectrum of cardiomyopathies. In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), fibrotic remodelling encompasses both diffuse interstitial matrix expansion and focal replacement fibrosis and is closely associated with disease severity and adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and quantitative parametric mapping, is central to non-invasive myocardial tissue characterization. LGE primarily identifies focal areas of replacement fibrosis and scar, whereas native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) mapping provide complementary information on diffuse myocardial and interstitial tissue abnormalities, including extracellular matrix expansion. However, these techniques characterize the structural and tissue-level consequences of myocardial injury and remodelling rather than directly visualizing the cellular processes underlying fibroblast activation. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography (FAPI PET) has emerged as a promising molecular imaging approach for assessing active fibroblast-mediated tissue remodelling. By targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a cell-surface serine protease upregulated in activated fibroblasts and myofibroblasts. FAPI radiotracers may provide a molecular readout of accessible FAP expression that complements structural and tissue characterization by CMR. This review examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying active myocardial remodelling, with particular emphasis on transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/Smad signalling, fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, FAP expression, and extracellular matrix turnover. We critically evaluate the current clinical evidence for FAPI PET/CT and hybrid PET/CMR across cardiomyopathies, focusi

candidates.title: Explainable machine learning and unsupervised anatomical phenotyping of mitral valve prolapse in patients with severe mitral regurgitation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) is increasingly recognized in mitral valve prolapse (MVP), but its anatomical embedding within degenerative MVP remains incompletely defined. We assessed whether explainable supervised learning and unsupervised clustering could identify MAD-associated MVP phenotypes.
METHODS: We analyzed a public surgical cohort of 979 patients with MVP and clinically significant mitral regurgitation. Etiology was classified as Barlow disease (BD) or fibroelastic deficiency (FED). Logistic regression, Random Forest and XGBoost were evaluated for MAD prediction using nested cross-validation with threshold optimization, and assessed for discrimination, calibration and net benefit (decision-curve analysis). XGBoost explainability was assessed using SHAP. UMAP-based clustering using anatomical and clinical variables (excluding MAD and etiology from the input) was performed, with prespecified cluster-number and stability sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Unsupervised phenotyping identified three anatomical clusters. The smallest cluster (n = 91, 9.3%) showed the highest MAD prevalence (36.3% vs. 12.0% and 15.8%), marked BD enrichment (95.6%), universal bileaflet prolapse and ≥ 4-scallop involvement, larger MV diameters and less chordal rupture; this phenotype was reproducible across UMAP settings. Supervised models showed only moderate MAD discrimination (XGBoost AUROC 0.695 ± 0.057; PR-AUC 0.314 ± 0.066), with modest calibration (Brier 0.13-0.20; slopes < 1) and limited net benefit, and were therefore interpreted as explanatory rather than diagnostic. SHAP identified BD status as the strongest contributor, followed by number of prolapsing scallops, mitral valve diameters, LV volumes and bileaflet prolapse.
CONCLUSION: Explainable and unsupervised analyses concordantly identified a MAD-enriched, BD-dominant bileaflet/multiscallop MVP phenotype, supporting the concept that MAD is embedded within broader annular-leaflet remodeling rather than being

candidates.title: [Prognostic value of angio-based microvascular resistance on left ventricular systolic function in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction].
candidates.journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the correlation between angio-based microvascular resistance (AMR) and impaired left ventricular systolic function in patients with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and to assess its predictive value for left ventricular systolic function.
METHODS: A study was conducted, enrolling consecutive STEMI patients who underwent primary PCI at the Department of Cardiology, Peking University Third Hospital from May 2023 to June 2024. Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) and AMR were calculated from coronary angiography images immediately after PCI, and myocardial biomarker or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) assessed by echocardiography at half-year follow-up were collected. The correlation between AMR, QFR, myocardial biomarkers, and LVEF after half a year was analyzed. The STEMI patients were divided into normal or reduced left ventricular systolic function with LVEF 0.5 as the boundary. The accuracy of AMR in diagnosing reduced left ventricular systolic function was analyzed by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC).
RESULTS: A total of 194 patients were enrolled, with an average age of (63.3±13.6) years, and the average AMR value was (246.99±57.18) mmHg·s/m. Age, peak creatine kinase (CK), troponin T (TnT), N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and AMR were identified as independent predictive factors for LVEF at half-year follow-up (β=-0.160, t=-2.533, P=0.012; β=-0.271, t=-3.068, P=0.002; β=-0.191, t=-2.157, P=0.032; β=-0.280, t=-4.515, P < 0.001; β=-0.162, t=-2.711, P=0.007). ROC curve analysis showed that AMR had a certain value in predicting reduced left ventricular systolic function [area under curve (95% confidence interval) was 0.631 (0.543-0.718), P=0.006], and the optimal cut-off value for predicting an LVEF < 0.5 was 250.5 mmHg·s/m.
CONCLUSION: AMR is an independent predictor of LVEF at half-year post-procedure and has significant predicti

candidates.title: Relationship between Endothelial Activation and Stress Index and Coronary Artery Ectasia.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is characterized by abnormal dilatation of the coronary arteries and is associated with endothelial dysfunction and systemic inflammation. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) has emerged as a novel biomarker reflecting endothelial activation and inflammatory stress.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between EASIX score and the presence of CAE.
METHODS: A total of 300 patients who underwent coronary angiography between July 2018 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The study was designed as a case-control study. Patients were divided into two groups according to the presence of CAE (150 CAE, 150 controls). The EASIX score was calculated using the following formula: EASIX = LDH × Creatinine / Platelet . Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine the predictive value of EASIX for CAE. Youden index statistical analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic power of ROC analysis and to calculate the optimal cut-off value. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Patients with CAE had significantly higher EASIX score compared with controls (1.46 ± 0.33 vs. 0.98 ± 0.74). In the ROC analysis, EASIX score had 72% sensitivity and 58% specificity when the cut-off value for EASIX≥ 0.74 (AUC=0.688, 95% CI:0.618-0.759, p<0.001). In Multivariable logistic regression analysis, the EASIX score was identified as an independent predictor of CAE (OR =2.12, 95% CI: 1.35-3.34, p=0.001).
CONCLUSION: The EASIX score was independently associated with the presence of CAE and demonstrated moderate discriminative ability.

candidates.title: Circulating microRNAs as potential candidate biomarkers of left ventricular reverse remodeling after myocardial infarction: A pilot study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction (MI) induces cardiac remodeling and lead to heart failure. Some patients experience reverse remodeling, characterized by improved LV function. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression and play a crucial role in remodeling processes.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate the role of miRNAs in cardiac reverse remodeling after MI and identify candidate miRNAs that could predict better response to cardiac rehabilitation.
METHODS: The study enrolled 39 patients following their first MI. For final analysis, 10 patients meeting echocardiographic criteria for LVRR at 8-week follow-up (absolute LVEF increase ≥ 10% or LVESV reduction ≥ 15%) were matched with 10 patients with stable LV status (SLVS). All patients completed a cardiac rehabilitation program. Expression of 375 circulating miRNAs was quantified - those with higher baseline accumulation in the LVRR group were identified as candidate biomarkers and their target genes were analyzed.
RESULTS: Twenty patients (mean age 57 ± 9 years) were analyzed. At baseline, the SLVS group exhibited significantly higher LVEF compared to the LVRR group (53% vs. 44%, p = 0.013). Baseline regional contractility impairment in all LVRR patients was reversed in 70% of them at follow-up. Fourteen miRNAs (-15b-5p, -24-3p, -29c-3p, -99b-5p, -127-3p, -146a-5p, -199a-3p, -361-5p, -502-5p, -625-5p, -376c-3p, -18b-5p, -342-5p, and -429) were identified as candidate LVRR biomarkers. Enrichment analysis linked their targets to PI3K-Akt, MAPK, FoxO, and HIF-1 pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies 14 candidate miRNAs as LVRR biomarkers post-MI. These findings highlight the biological relevance of non-coding RNA and support the need for further research and validation in large, non-pooled cohorts.

candidates.title: Opportunistic Detection of Hepatic Steatosis Using Postcontrast Liver Attenuation at Coronary CT Angiography.
candidates.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic performance of postcontrast liver attenuation measured with coronary CT angiography (CCTA) for opportunistic detection of hepatic steatosis and to assess the impact of tube potential variation on optimal attenuation thresholds and overall performance. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included adult patients who underwent CCTA with concomitant unenhanced coronary Agatston scoring (January to December 2025). Moderate-to-severe hepatic steatosis was defined as unenhanced liver attenuation less than 40 HU. Postcontrast liver attenuation was measured using standardized regions of interest. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with Youden index-based threshold determination. Associations between hepatic steatosis, Agatston score categories, and Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categorizations were evaluated using likelihood ratio χ2 tests. Results Among 300 included patients (mean age ± SD, 55.6 years ± 12.0; 170 males), moderate-to-severe steatosis was present in 109 patients (36.3%). Postcontrast liver attenuation demonstrated high diagnostic performance across all settings (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.88, 0.95, and 0.89 at 100, 120, and 140 kVp, respectively). Optimal thresholds decreased with increasing tube potential (54, 47, and 40 HU at 100, 120, and 140 kVp, respectively). Patients with steatosis had a lower frequency of coronary artery calcium scores of zero (43.7% vs 57.6%) and a higher frequency of coronary artery calcium scores of 101-300 (11.7% vs 4.9%; P = .042), whereas CAD-RADS distribution was similar (P = .12). Conclusion Postcontrast liver attenuation measured with CCTA demonstrated promising diagnostic performance for opportunistic identification of moderate-to-severe hepatic steatosis across different tube potential settings. candidates.title: Diagnostic Performance of a Deep Learning Model Using Phonocardiogram and Single-Lead ECG Signals for Detecting Moderate-or-Greater Aortic Stenosis: Multicenter External Validation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Valvular heart disease, particularly aortic stenosis (AS), often remains asymptomatic until advanced stages, making early detection challenging. Although cardiac auscultation is a traditional screening tool, its diagnostic accuracy is limited. We aimed to externally validate a deep learning-based model (eAS model) using phonocardiogram (PCG) and single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) signals to detect moderate-or-greater AS.
METHODS: PCG and ECG recordings were acquired using a PCG device (Cardio-EGG). Transthoracic echocardiography served as the reference standard. The external validation cohort consisted of 951 patients from 3 medical institutions, including 70 with moderate-or-greater AS. The primary outcome was sensitivity for detecting moderate-or-greater AS; secondary outcomes included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios (LR).
RESULTS: The external validation cohort (n = 951, median age 73 years, male 65%) exhibited more advanced valvular disease than the training/development cohort. The eAS model achieved an AUROC of 0.9632 (95% CI: 0.9471-0.9774). Using the pre-determined threshold, sensitivity was 92.9% and specificity 87.9%, yielding a positive LR of 7.65 and negative LR of 0.08. Model-derived probabilities showed strong associations with echocardiographic measures of AS severity (adjusted R2 = 0.5051 for peak transvalvular velocity). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed generally consistent performance, although estimates were imprecise in small subgroups.
CONCLUSION: The eAS model demonstrated high diagnostic performance for detecting moderate-or-greater AS in a multicenter external validation cohort. AI-based PCG/ECG analysis may support the decision to refer patients from auscultation to echocardiography for AS evaluation.

candidates.title: Association of Neutrophil-To-Lymphocyte Ratio and Atherogenic Index of Plasma With Angiographically Confirmed Coronary Artery Disease.
candidates.journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
candidates.abstract: BackgroundThe neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) have been associated with coronary artery disease (CAD). We investigated their associations with angiographically confirmed CAD and lesion severity.MethodsThis retrospective study included 2,933 patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD at Wuhan Third Hospital. CAD was defined as ≥50% luminal stenosis in at least one major coronary artery or branch. Lesion severity was assessed using the Gensini score. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed.ResultsAmong 2,933 patients, 1,615 had CAD and 1,318 had no significant stenosis. NLR and AIP were higher in patients with CAD and increased across Gensini score categories (all P<0.05). After adjustment, AIP remained independently associated with CAD (OR=1.557, P=0.042), whereas NLR did not (OR=1.019, P=0.581). AIP alone showed limited discrimination (AUC=0.537). A multivariable model including age, blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, and AIP showed an AUC of 0.779. Adding AIP did not significantly improve AUC (DeLong P=0.153) or NRI (0.071, P=0.106), although IDI improvement was significant (0.002, P<0.05).ConclusionsIn patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD, NLR and AIP were associated with CAD and angiographic disease burden. AIP remained independently associated with CAD, whereas NLR did not. However, AIP showed limited discrimination and no clear incremental improvement beyond conventional variables. These findings do not support population screening or routine clinical implementation.

candidates.title: Human vs Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Coronary Occlusions in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Retrospective Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) on the electrocardiogram (ECG) can present as ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), non-STEMI, ST depression, or other patterns (eg, de Winter T waves and hyperacute T waves), posing a diagnostic challenge. Even experienced physicians may overlook OMI on ECG, leading to delays in catheterization laboratory activation. Recently, smartphone apps using AI have been shown to exhibit promising accuracy in ECG interpretation in large datasets.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of our study was to retrospectively compare the diagnostic performance of an AI-based application (PMCardio) with that of interventional cardiologists in interpreting nonpathognomonic ECGs that generated debates about diagnosis.
METHODS: In total, 33 ECGs that were diagnostically challenging upon patient admission to the emergency department were included. A group of 3 interventional cardiologists, blinded to the final diagnosis, independently assessed whether the ECG suggested OMI requiring immediate invasive coronary angiography. The diagnostic performance of the cardiologists was compared to that of the AI application, using the results of coronary angiography as the gold standard and considering any lesion with ≥90% stenosis as positive.
RESULTS: Of the 33 patients, 29 (88%) had a final diagnosis of cardiac origin for their chest pain, including 23 acute coronary syndromes, of which 13 (57%) were OMI. The 3 cardiologists achieved sensitivities of 62%, 85%, and 62%; negative predictive values (NPVs) of 74%, 83%, and 69%; specificities of 70%, 50%, and 55%; and positive predictive values (PPVs) of 57%, 52%, and 47%. Their overall misclassification rates were 33%, 36%, and 42%. In contrast, AI analysis demonstrated a sensitivity and NPV of 100%, a specificity of 60%, a PPV of 62%, and an overall misclassification rate of 24%.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study of challenging ECGs, an AI application demonstrated better diagnostic performance of OM

candidates.title: Pulmonary Valve Amyloid Deposition Mimicking Infective Endocarditis in Val30Met Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
candidates.abstract: A 53-year-old man with Val30Met hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (hATTR) developed a highly mobile pulmonary valve mass with severe pulmonary regurgitation. Concomitant methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia raised suspicion for infective endocarditis. Echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging characterized the lesion but could not establish its etiology. Surgical excision and pulmonary valve replacement were performed, and histopathological examination demonstrated Congo red-positive amyloid deposition. This case highligts that atypical cardiac manifestations beyond myocardial infiltration can occur in patients with hATTR. We present a case of isolated pulmonary valvular amyloid infiltration without overt myocardial involvement in Val30Met-associated hATTR.

candidates.title: Restoration of frequency-dependent myocardial reserve after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis: an invasive hemodynamic study.
candidates.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
candidates.abstract: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) and chronic pressure overload may impair frequency-dependent myocardial reserve despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We investigated whether acute afterload reduction with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) restores force-frequency relationships (FFR) and relaxation frequency relationships (RFR). In this prospective study, patients with severe normal-flow, high-gradient AS and preserved LVEF underwent invasive left ventricular pressure recording during incremental atrial pacing at 80 and 100 beats/min before and immediately after TAVI. Systolic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmax and preload-adjusted indices [dP/dtmax/left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) and left ventricular peak systolic pressure (LVSP)/LVEDP], whereas lusitropic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmin, the relaxation constant τ, and LVEDP. Echocardiography was performed at baseline and 3 mo. Forty-six patients completed the pacing protocol. Before TAVI, pacing produced only a modest increase in dP/dtmax (Δ + 150 mmHg/s; P = 0.004), without improvement in dP/dtmin (P = 0.329) or τ (P = 0.182). Immediately after TAVI, pacing increased dP/dtmax (P < 0.001), dP/dtmax/LVEDP (P = 0.004), and LVSP/LVEDP (P = 0.031), while improving dP/dtmin (Δ + 56 mmHg/s; P = 0.050) and τ (P = 0.033) and reducing LVEDP (P = 0.017). Correlation analyses supported the emergence of physiological FFR and RFR after valve implantation. At 3 mo, echocardiography showed lower pulmonary artery systolic pressure (P = 0.002), improved left atrial reservoir strain, and lower diastolic dysfunction grade (P = 0.006). Thus, acute afterload relief with TAVI reveals preserved dynamic systolic and lusitropic reserve in severe AS, with subsequent group-level improvement in diastolic function.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study provides direct invasive human evidence that frequency-dependent myocardial reserve is acutely restored after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis.
