candidates.title: Endoscopic secondary chordae transfer and edge-to-edge repair for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse.
candidates.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
candidates.abstract: Anterior leaflet prolapse remains a challenging lesion in mitral valve repair, particularly in the presence of asymmetric degenerative disease. We present the case of a 59-year-old patient with severe mitral regurgitation due to asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse in the setting of Barlow's disease, treated through a totally endoscopic right minithoracotomy. Intraoperative valve analysis demonstrated prolapse of the A2M2 and A3 segments with elongated secondary chordae. Mitral valve repair was performed using secondary chordae transfer, followed by asymmetric edge-to-edge repair at the A2-P2 scallops and ring annuloplasty. Intraoperative assessment showed satisfactory leaflet coaptation with trivial residual regurgitation. Postoperative echocardiography confirmed the absence of residual mitral regurgitation and no evidence of clinically significant mitral stenosis. This report describes the technical aspects of endoscopic secondary chordae transfer combined with asymmetric edge-to-edge repair and ring annuloplasty for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse, demonstrating the feasibility of this repair strategy in a complex mitral valve anatomy.

candidates.title: Beyond Atrial Fibrillation: Clinical and Echocardiographic Predictors of Ischaemic Stroke and Systemic Thromboembolism in Rheumatic Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the best-established thromboembolic risk factor in rheumatic heart disease (RHD), but stroke and thromboembolism also occur without documented AF. We systematically synthesised associations between non-AF clinical/echocardiographic predictors and thromboembolism in RHD, comparing AF-adjusted with unadjusted estimates.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched, supplemented by Google Scholar and citation screening. Eligible studies evaluated RHD patients with ≥1 non-AF predictor of stroke or thromboembolism. Two reviewers performed selection, extraction, and QUIPS risk-of-bias assessment; certainty was graded using GRADE. Unadjusted, adjusted, and AF-adjusted estimates were extracted separately, and random-effects meta-analysis was performed when feasible.
RESULTS: Nineteen studies (∼8,206 patients) met eligibility criteria. SEC, LA size/volume, LA/appendage thrombus, LA appendage flow, LA mechanical function, mitral valve severity, age, and previous thromboembolism were most frequently examined. Four studies provided comparable crude ORs for SEC (pooled OR 8.27, 95% CI 3.21-21.29; I2 = 66%), substantially attenuated after AF adjustment (as low as OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.1-3.0). Older age and previous stroke remained associated with thromboembolism in AF-inclusive models, and LA mechanical/reservoir function showed consistent inverse associations, including in sinus rhythm. Certainty was low for SEC, age, and LA function; moderate for previous stroke/thromboembolism; very low for anticoagulation non-use.
CONCLUSION: In RHD, thromboembolic risk extends beyond documented AF. SEC showed the strongest unadjusted association but was substantially attenuated after AF adjustment, likely partly reflecting subclinical AF; it is TEE-dependent and inconsistently graded. Older age, previous thromboembolism, and impaired LA mechanical/reservoir function showed more persistent associations after AF-inclusive adjustment;

candidates.title: Advanced Rheumatic Heart Disease Complicated by Pregnancy, Mitral Valve Disease, Pulmonary Hypertension, and Left Atrial Thrombus: A Multidisciplinary Case Report from Resource-Limited Settings.
candidates.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality among pregnant women in resource-limited settings. Pregnancy induces significant hemodynamic changes that can decompensate pre-existing valvular heart disease, leading to life-threatening complications for both mother and fetus.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 27-year-old pregnant woman (gravida 6, para 5) at approximately 34-38 weeks presented with progressive shortness of breath, palpitations. Based on the modified World Health Organization (mWHO) classification, she was categorized as Class IV (extremely high risk) bilateral lower limb swelling, cough, fatigue, and reduced appetite. Cardiovascular examination revealed a systolic murmur, loud S1 and S2, with bilateral basal crepitations on respiratory examination. Echocardiography demonstrated an enlarged left atrium (5 cm), moderate mitral stenosis, mild mitral regurgitation, with fixed mitral valve leaflets, pulmonary hypertension, poor right ventricular function, a large left atrial thrombus, Labor occurred spontaneously while on low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH). Mild pericardial effusion, and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (58%). Laboratory investigations showed elevated CRP (48.8 mg/L), thrombocytopenia (platelets 99 ×109/L), mild coagulation abnormalities (INR 1.5), and urinalysis findings consistent with hematuria and proteinuria. Electrocardiography revealed sinus tachycardia, left atrial enlargement, right ventricular hypertrophy pattern, incomplete right bundle branch block, and prolonged QTc interval. The patient received multidisciplinary care including furosemide, metoprolol, and enoxaparin. She delivered a 2.1 kg neonate with good Apgar scores.
DISCUSSION: This case illustrates the severe maternal and fetal risks associated with advanced RHD during pregnancy. The presence of a large left atrial thrombus in a pregnant woman poses significant thromboembolic and hemodynamic risks. Multidis

candidates.title: Screening for Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Sepsis Using a Smartphone ECG Analysis Application: A Multicenter Validation Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced left ventricular (LV) dysfunction complicates fluid resuscitation, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema and worsening outcomes. Echocardiographic assessment is often delayed, and natriuretic peptides such as N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) have limited diagnostic accuracy in this setting. We evaluated a smartphone-based electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis application for screening LV dysfunction in patients with sepsis.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective observational study, we included 425 adult sepsis patients from three university hospitals who underwent both a 12-lead ECG and transthoracic echocardiography within 72 hours of emergency department admission. ECG images displayed on a monitor were photographed and analyzed using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based smartphone application (ECG Buddy™), which generated a quantitative digital biomarker for LV dysfunction (quantitative electrocardiogram scores for LV dysfunction [QCG-LVDys]). LV dysfunction was defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%. The diagnostic performance of QCG-LVDys for detecting LV dysfunction was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). A predefined comparison with NT-proBNP was performed in the single center where NT-proBNP was routinely measured.
RESULTS: In the overall multicenter cohort, QCG-LVDys showed high diagnostic performance for LV dysfunction, with an ROC-AUC of 0.901. Using an optimized threshold (37.35), QCG-LVDys achieved a sensitivity of 89.6%, specificity of 75.1%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 97.5%. In the NT-proBNP subset, QCG-LVDys outperformed NT-proBNP (ROC-AUC 0.911 vs. 0.637, P < 0.001). Higher QCG-LVDys values were associated with increased lactate levels (P = 0.002) and 28-day in-hospital mortality (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: AI-driven ECG analysis via a smartphone app provided a rapid, accessible, and accurate screening tool for LV dysfunction in se

candidates.title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A PRO-TAVI Substudy.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR.
METHODS: This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed.
RESULTS: The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17

candidates.title: Frequency and Prognosis of Alternative Definitions of Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Across the Whole Spectrum of Acute Coronary Syndromes.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) refers to a myocardial infarction caused by a persistent or transient, complete or near-complete coronary artery occlusion. Multiple definitions have been proposed, yet their frequency and comparative prognostic relevance remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the frequency and prognosis of previously proposed OMI definitions across the whole spectrum of acute coronary syndromes (ACS) from the MATRIX trial.
METHODS: Five alternative OMI definitions were assessed: 1) culprit artery (CA) TIMI flow grade 0; 2) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-1; 3) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2; 4) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >30× upper reference limit; and 5) CA-TIMI flow grade 0-2 or CA-TIMI flow grade 3 with cardiac troponin >100× upper reference limit. The endpoint of interest was 1-year all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Among 6,558 patients with ACS, OMI frequency ranged from 37.8% for definition 1 to 76.1% for definition 4. OMI was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality according to definitions 1-4 (adjusted HR: 2.08 [95% CI: 1.56-2.78], 1.97[1.47-2.63], 1.70 [1.25-2.32], 1.47 [1.01-2.12], respectively) but not according to definition 5 (adjusted HR: 1.26 [0.90-1.75]). OMI definitions exclusively based on impaired CA flow (ie, definitions 1-3) improved discrimination, reclassification, and model fit when added to the conventional STE/NSTE-ACS classification. One-year mortality did not differ among patients with NSTE-ACS with OMI definition 1 or 2 compared with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI) patients.
CONCLUSIONS: OMI defined by impaired CA flow confers prognostic implications beyond the presence or absence of ST-segment elevation in a broad ACS population and identifies patients without ST-segment elevation with 1-year mortality similar to that of STEMI.

candidates.title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria: A DIFOCCULT-3 Substudy.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE.
METHODS: This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO.
RESULTS: Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001). Adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently under the OMI/NOMI approach (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001), without reduction in angiographic yield.
CONCLUSIONS: An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.

candidates.title: Complex Cardiac Tumor with Concomitant Pericardial Effusion and Hemodynamic Compromise in a Septuagenarian: Case Report of Anesthetic and Surgical Considerations.
candidates.abstract: Primary cardiac tumors are rare, and cardiac lymphomas are particularly uncommon. Their presentation can mimic benign tumors, but perioperative management is highly challenging due to risks of tumor-related obstruction or invasion of surrounding cardiac structures. We present a 76-year-old woman with rapidly progressing dyspnea, found to have large biatrial masses, significant pericardial and pleural effusions, and evidence of tamponade. The patient underwent successful surgical resection of bilateral atrial tumors after careful anesthetic preparation and intraoperative monitoring. Histology revealed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and systemic chemotherapy was commenced. This case highlights the critical importance of multidisciplinary collaboration, preoperative hemodynamic stabilization, careful anesthetic planning, and prompt histological diagnosis in managing primary cardiac lymphoma presenting with tamponade physiology.

candidates.title: An Extremely Rare Association of the Giant Right Atrium with Uncorrected Tetralogy of Fallot in an Adolescent Male Patient.
candidates.abstract: Uncorrected tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) can be associated with widespread abnormalities, but the giant right atrium (RA) is an extremely rare one. The giant RA can cause additional problems causing atrial arrythmias, thromboembolism, and compression of adjacent structures. Tricuspid regurgitation is common with annular dilatation. In symptomatic cases, reduction atrioplasty is recommended. Sternotomy should be careful to avoid damage to the giant RA. In asymptomatic cases, anticoagulation should be carried out. We report a rare case of uncorrected TOF associated with the giant RA and got successfully treated with surgery.

candidates.title: Anesthetic Challenges in Interarterial Right Coronary Artery Anomaly from the Left Sinus of Valsalva: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Coronary artery anomalies are rare but clinically significant malformations, particularly when involving an interarterial course, which predisposes to ischemia and sudden cardiac death. We report the case of a previously healthy 22-year-old man who suffered out-of-hospital cardiac arrest associated with recreational inhalant use. Imaging revealed an anomalous right coronary artery originating from the left sinus of Valsalva with interarterial trajectory. Surgical reimplantation was performed under tailored anesthetic management emphasizing hemodynamic stability. The patient recovered uneventfully. This case discusses and highlights anesthetic priorities and the potential role of external triggers in vulnerable coronary anatomy.

candidates.title: Effects of adenosine on oxidative stress and inflammation in patients with coronary heart disease underlying percutaneous coronary intervention.
candidates.journal: The Journal of international medical research
candidates.abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether rapid intracoronary adenosine administration attenuates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)-induced systemic inflammation and oxidative stress in patients with coronary artery disease.MethodsThis prospective, randomized controlled trial enrolled patients undergoing coronary angiography (coronary angiography group) or PCI. Patients undergoing PCI were assigned to receive intracoronary adenosine (PCI + adenosine group) or placebo (PCI group). Blood levels of inflammatory markers (e.g. cytokines), anti-inflammatory mediators, and oxidative stress indicators (superoxide dismutase and malondialdehyde) were measured before and 24 h after the procedure.ResultsCompared to the coronary angiography group, patients undergoing PCI who received placebo exhibited concurrent elevations in inflammatory and anti-inflammatory markers at 24 h. Intracoronary adenosine significantly suppressed the rise in the levels of inflammatory markers (e.g. interleukin-6 reduced by 35% vs. placebo) and enhanced anti-inflammatory responses (e.g. interleukin-10 increased by 40% vs. placebo). Following PCI, oxidative stress was evident in placebo-treated patients, as reflected by decreased superoxide dismutase activity (15% reduction) and increased malondialdehyde levels (30% elevation). Adenosine restored superoxide dismutase activity to near-baseline levels and reduced malondialdehyde elevation by 85% compared to placebo.ConclusionsIntracoronary adenosine mitigates PCI-associated systemic inflammation and oxidative stress by rebalancing inflammatory pathways and preserving redox homeostasis. These findings highlight its potential as a therapeutic adjunct for improving clinical outcomes following PCI and warrant further validation in large-scale trials.Clinical Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR); identifier: ChiCTR1800019349.

candidates.title: Longitudinal Left Atrial Remodeling With Pharmacological Rhythm Versus Rate Control in Paroxysmal and Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
candidates.abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence regarding left atrial (LA) remodeling with pharmacological rhythm control remains limited, particularly in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) outside heart-failure-specific populations.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 156 adults with paroxysmal or persistent AF receiving mutually exclusive pharmacological rate-control (n = 92) or rhythm-control (n = 64) therapy who underwent two transthoracic echocardiograms. LA remodeling was assessed using serial echocardiography, and clinical outcomes were evaluated after the second examination.
RESULTS: Among 74 patients with paired left atrial volume index (LAVI) measurements, LAVI increased from 39.9 to 50.3 mL/m2 with rate control (p < 0.001) but remained unchanged with rhythm control (44.9 to 43.4 mL/m2; p = 0.465). After adjustment for baseline LAVI and clinical covariates, rhythm control was associated with a 9.38 mL/m2 lower follow-up LAVI (95% CI, -15.53 to -3.24; p = 0.003). The association with lower follow-up LAVI was also observed among patients without heart failure and remained similar in sensitivity analyses. During post-landmark follow-up, rhythm control was associated with a lower hazard of all-cause mortality or stroke hospitalization (adjusted HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.24-0.88; p = 0.019).
CONCLUSION: Pharmacological rhythm control was associated with more favorable longitudinal LA remodeling than rate control, including among patients without heart failure, and was also associated with a lower hazard of subsequent all-cause mortality or stroke hospitalization.

candidates.title: Rupture of Left Ventricular Aneurysm in Infant: Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Rupture of ventricular aneurysm is an unusual pathology in children. This case describes a preterm infant who had been in the hospital since birth due to necrotizing enterocolitis, which was complicated by narrowing of the ascending colon that required surgery. Throughout the entire period, the infant exhibited signs of infection, first caused by Staphylococcus haemolyticus and subsequently by Staphylococcus epidermidis. Several echocardiographic examinations did not reveal any significant changes; however, the final echocardiography revealed a structure connected to the left ventricular cavity. The infant experienced sudden cardiac arrest due to significant pericardial effusion. Despite continued resuscitation efforts, including emergency pericardiocentesis, the asystole recurred, further advanced life support measures were unsuccessful, and death was pronounced. Autopsy revealed a small outpouching on the anterior wall of the left ventricle, associated with thinning of the myocardium and a linear rupture with uneven edges. Histological examination showed that the aneurysm wall was composed of myocardium and connective tissue, exhibiting signs of inflammation, necrosis, and hemorrhage.

candidates.title: Perioperative Myocardial Injury and Infarction: Thrombotic Mechanisms, Diagnostic Challenges, and Antithrombotic Management.
candidates.journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
candidates.abstract: BackgroundPerioperative myocardial injury (PMI) and perioperative myocardial infarction (PMIn) are common, often clinically silent complications after noncardiac surgery and are associated with substantial short- and long-term mortality. Surgical stress promotes a prothrombotic milieu through platelet activation, coagulation cascade amplification, impaired fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and plaque destabilization.PurposeThis narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the thrombotic mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and antithrombotic management of PMI/PMIn, with emphasis on risk stratification using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and thrombogenicity biomarkers.MethodsMajor perioperative cohort studies, randomized trials, scientific statements, and international guidelines were reviewed, including VISION, MANAGE, POISE, PANDA, the 2021 American Heart Association scientific statement, the 2024 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) perioperative guideline, and the 2022 European Society of Cardiology guideline.ResultsMost perioperative ischemic injury is clinically silent and frequently reflects oxygen supply-demand mismatch, whereas atherothrombotic plaque rupture with coronary thrombosis represents an important minority. Serial high-sensitivity troponin surveillance is central to detection, but interpretation requires exclusion of nonischemic causes and integration with electrocardiography, echocardiography, clinical context, and coronary anatomy. CCTA identifies vulnerable coronary anatomy, whereas D-dimer and thromboelastography-derived platelet-fibrin clot strength characterize a complementary vulnerable-blood phenotype. candidates.title: Left Atrial Enlargement Identifies Risk of Stroke Independent of Atrial Fibrillation.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) enlargement has been proposed to increase stroke risk independent of atrial fibrillation (AF), but evidence accounting for AF over time is limited. We tested whether the association between LA enlargement and stroke persist independent of new-onset AF.
METHODS: In this observational study, participants from the Copenhagen General Population Study underwent cardiac computed tomography from 2010 through 2018 and were followed until December 2022. LA volume was indexed to body surface area. LA enlargement was defined using sex-specific cutoffs. The primary outcome was incident stroke. Secondary outcomes were incident AF, heart failure, dementia, and all-cause mortality. Individuals with baseline AF were excluded. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using cause-specific Cox models with AF modeled as a time-varying covariate.
RESULTS: Among 10 024 individuals (mean age 60 years, 57% women), 684 (6.8%) had LA enlargement. Over a median follow-up of 7.3 years stroke occurred in 356 individuals (3.6%). LA enlargement was associated with a higher absolute risk of stroke (11.1% versus 4.6%, risk difference 6.5% [95% CI, 2.4-10.6]) and an increased hazard (adjusted HR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.09-2.05]; P=0.013), which remained similar after adjustment for incident AF, and in separate models using the CHA2DS2-VA score and P-wave terminal force in lead V1. LA enlargement was also associated with higher risk of AF (HR, 3.77 [95% CI, 3.00-4.73]) and heart failure (HR, 3.59 [95% CI, 2.54-5.06]) but not with dementia or all-cause mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: LA enlargement was associated with incident stroke independent of incident AF, supporting LA enlargement as a marker of thromboembolic risk.

candidates.title: Body Mass Index, Valsartan, and Myocardial Remodeling in Early-Stage Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Secondary Analysis of the Randomized VANISH Trial.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is associated with adverse outcomes in overt hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but the prevalence and impact of elevated body mass index (BMI) in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is uncertain.
METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the randomized VANISH (Valsartan for Attenuating Disease Evolution in Early Sarcomeric Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy) trial, participants were categorized according to baseline BMI (nonelevated or elevated [≥85th percentile if age <18 years; ≥25 kg/m2 if age ≥18 years]). Exercise capacity (peak oxygen uptake [milliliters per kilogram per minute]) and cardiac imaging parameters were evaluated by baseline BMI and 2-year change in BMI.
RESULTS: Among 171 (96%) participants (mean age, 23±10 years; 39% female sex; 97% White), 82 (48%) had nonelevated BMI and 89 (52%) had an elevated BMI. After covariate adjustment, higher baseline BMI was associated with lower peak oxygen uptake; lower left ventricular systolic and diastolic function; higher left ventricular mass; and higher atrial, ventricular, and extracellular volumes. Similarly, greater 2-year increases in BMI were associated with greater declines in peak oxygen uptake and greater increases in left ventricular mass. Participants with elevated BMI were more likely to develop late gadolinium enhancement over 2 years (adjusted odds ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-11.9]; P=0.033). Valsartan appeared to modestly attenuate 2-year increases in body weight versus placebo (adjusted mean difference, -3.1% [95% CI, -6.2 to -0.1%]; P=0.042). Baseline BMI did not appear to modify the effect of valsartan on cardiac remodeling (Pinteraction=0.96).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated BMI was common and associated with greater hypertrophic, eccentric, and fibrotic remodeling in early-stage hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. candidates.title: Left Ventricular End-Diastolic Diameter Predicts Clinical Outcomes in Patients Supported With Surgically Implanted Microaxial Flow Pump.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study sought to determine the impact of left ventricular size on clinical outcomes after a microaxial flow pump was surgically implanted.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included patients who received a surgical microaxial left ventricular assist device from May 2020 to February 2024 at 2 high-volume centers in the United States. Patients were categorized into 2 groups based on their preimplant left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD): "small LVEDD," defined as LVEDD ≤5.5 cm, and "large LVEDD," defined as LVEDD >5.5 cm, respectively. End points were all-cause death at 30 days after device implantation, in-hospital death, death 30-days after discharge, and survival at 30-month follow-up.
RESULTS: Two-hundred sixty-two patients received an Impella 5.5. Preimplant LVEDD was documented in 194 (74%) patients, where 50 patients had LVEDD ≤5.5 cm and 144 patients had LVEDD >5.5 cm. Patients with a small LVEDD had a higher rate of all-cause death at 30 days after device implantation (32% versus 11.8%, P=0.002), in-hospital death (42% versus 20.1%, P=0.004), and death 30 days after discharge (44% versus 20.8%, P=0.003). In adjusted analyses, patients with a greater LVEDD had 62% decreased risk of long-term death (hazard ratio, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.19-0.76]; P=0.001), compared with patients with a smaller LVEDD.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, all-comer study, we found that patients with reduced left ventricular dimension who required an Impella 5.5 had worse outcomes. Further research is warranted to recapitulate our observations across more centers.

candidates.title: Thoracic Intermuscular Adiposity, Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction, and Prognosis After Cardiac Surgery.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body mass index is a widely-used yet imprecise measure of adiposity. Thoracic intermuscular adiposity is reported to be related with coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD), but their prognostic implications after cardiac surgery are not clear. This study aimed to investigate whether computed tomography-derived thoracic intermuscular adiposity and CMD provide better prognostic information than body mass index in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This study consecutively enrolled 666 patients undergoing elective surgery from 3 centers. Using computed tomography at the T12 vertebral level, we quantified the cross-sectional areas (cm2) of skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, and intermuscular adipose tissue. Intermuscular fat fraction was calculated as intermuscular adipose tissue/(intermuscular adipose tissue+skeletal muscle)×100%. CMD was defined by a coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance >25. The primary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and rehospitalization for heart failure.
RESULTS: A total of 63 MACEs (9.5%) occurred during a median 17-month follow-up. Obesity defined by body mass index (10.7% of patients) was not associated with MACE (P=0.187). Each 1% increase in intermuscular fat fraction was significantly associated with CMD (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.14-1.31]; P<0.001), whereas body mass index showed no such correlation (P=0.964). CMD independently predicted MACE (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.03; [95% CI: 1.15-3.61]; P = 0.015), whereas intermuscular fat fraction did not (P=0.516). The annualized MACE rate was significantly higher in patients with CMD (11.0% versus 5.2%, P=0.004).

candidates.title: Cardiac Reverse Remodeling and Clinical Outcomes Following Angiotensin Receptor-Neprilysin Inhibitor Therapy in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
candidates.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac reverse remodeling and associated clinical outcomes following angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) therapy in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction (EF) remain unclear. We investigated differences in 1-year echocardiographic response after ARNI therapy and predictors of clinical outcomes.
METHODS: This study involved patients with HF with reduced EF and ARNI therapy for more than 6 months, using data from a 2-center registry. Echocardiographic data were analyzed at baseline and 1 year after ARNI initiation. Responders were defined as patients with a ≥30% reduction in left ventricular end-systolic volume at 1 year; all others were nonresponders. The primary outcome was cardiovascular death, and secondary outcomes were hospitalization for HF and all-cause death. Time-by-group interactions in echocardiographic parameters were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Among 1002 patients (mean age: 64.2±13.7 years; 70.8% men), 451 (45.0%) were responders and 551 (55.0%) were nonresponders. Responders had a lower baseline left ventricular EF but higher left ventricular EF at 1 year (27.0% [95% CI, 22.0-33.0] and 48.0% [95% CI, 42.0-55.0]). Both groups showed improvements in diastolic parameters, with more pronounced changes in responders. In multivariable analysis, nonresponders had a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for HF, and all-cause death (all P<0.001). Male sex and a higher baseline left ventricular EF were independent predictors of nonresponse, whereas systolic blood pressure ≥110 mm Hg and atrial fibrillation were associated with better outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac reverse remodeling after ARNI therapy varies among patients with HF with reduced EF. Positive responders to ARNI therapy at 1 year experienced more favorable clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Multimodality imaging and surgical management of a rare combination: type 2A bridging bronchus, pulmonary artery sling, and atrial septal defect, a case report.
candidates.abstract: We report the case of a 15-year-old female presenting with exertional syncope and a history of refractory respiratory symptoms. Comprehensive preoperative multimodality imaging-including echocardiography, multi-detector computed tomography (MDCT) with three-dimensional reconstruction, and bronchoscopy-revealed a rare complex of congenital anomalies: a type 2 A bridging bronchus (BB), a pulmonary artery sling (PAS), and an atrial septal defect (ASD). Crucially, imaging confirmed the absence of significant tracheal stenosis, thereby obviating the need for tracheoplasty. The patient successfully underwent surgical repair via median sternotomy on cardiopulmonary bypass, which included reimplantation of the left pulmonary artery and patch closure of the ASD. Postoperative MDCT confirmed patency of the reconstructed pulmonary artery and the patient's symptoms resolved. This case underscores the indispensable role of advanced imaging in the diagnosis and surgical planning of complex congenital cardiopulmonary anomalies, particularly for guiding a tailored surgical approach in the setting of rare associations like BB and PAS.

candidates.title: NoduleFlow: Automatic 3D Lung Nodule Detection and Segmentation
candidates.abstract: Low dose Computed Tomography (CT) is the standard imaging modality for lung cancer screening. On CT scans, lung cancer typically manifests as pulmonary nodules, whose manual identification is time-consuming and prone to observer variability, image quality limitations, and suboptimal reading conditions. Moreover, subtle temporal changes are often difficult to quantify reliably in CT scans from the same patient across follow-up examinations. Deep learning-based approaches for the automatic detection and segmentation of lung nodules have demonstrated improved accuracy and efficiency. However, most existing approaches provide only coarse region-of-interest localisation, rely on prior lesion annotations or human supervision, or treat detection and segmentation as separate tasks. In this work, we present NoduleFlow, a framework for lung nodule detection, classification, and segmentation directly from series of CT volumes. Our proposal consists of four interconnected modules and operates in an automated manner at inference time, without requiring prior lesion annotations, manual initialisation, or region-of-interest pre-selection. We further investigate whether nodule localization benefits from the propagation of candidate regions across follow-up scans through inter-scan registration fields, as opposed to conventional independent per-scan analysis. The generalisability of the framework is systematically evaluated across four independent datasets. The results underscore the potential of automated pipelines for lung nodule analysis in screening and diagnostic settings.

candidates.title: Focus, Align, and Diffuse: Time-Series-Aware Keyframe Diffusion for Cardiac Dynamic Synthesis from Sparse Observations
candidates.abstract: Dense cardiac dynamics are essential for assessing cardiac function, yet in practice clinicians often observe only extremely sparse measurements. However, recovering full dynamics from such sparsity is a highly ill-posed problem due to the lack of temporal cues. While auxiliary time-series signals like ECG provide physiological guidance, effectively exploiting them is challenging due to the cross-modal representation gap and phase misalignment. In this work, we present CardioFAD, a Focus--Align--Diffuse paradigm that reformulates sparse cardiac dynamic synthesis as a recoverability--alignability anchor discovery problem. Our core insight is that resolving extreme temporal ambiguity requires a compact set of anchor states that are both sufficient to recover the visual trajectory and reliable for ECG--visual alignment. We therefore learn motion-salient keyframes under two complementary principles: trajectory sufficiency, which preserves trajectory-critical intra-modal motion content, and anchor alignment, which promotes consistent inter-modal correspondence at these anchors. We implement the Focus and Align modules optimized by the two aspects. Diffuse then performs two-stage generation by first synthesizing keyframes and subsequently interpolating the remaining frames. Extensive experiments on cardiac MRI and echocardiography videos demonstrate superior visual quality, temporal coherence, and improved functional consistency under the extreme one-shot regime.

candidates.title: Deep Learning-Based Anatomical Level Classification of Craniofacial CT Slices: Comparison of CNN Architectures and Ensemble Methods
candidates.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) interpretation requires recognition of the anatomical level of each slice. Classification may facilitate preprocessing and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. We developed deep learning models to classify craniofacial CT slices into six anatomical categories. A total of 11,769 images were collected from a multicenter database involving 10 Japanese university hospitals and the public Head-Neck-Radiomics-HN1 dataset. Patients were divided into training (70%) and evaluation (30%) sets. Five CNN architectures were trained from scratch, and hard- and soft-voting ensembles were evaluated. Individual-model accuracy ranged from 94.72% to 96.09%; the hard-voting ensemble achieved 96.46% accuracy (Cohens {kappa} = 0.954). Although performance differed among individual models (Cochrans Q = 99.29, p < 0.001), the ensemble did not significantly outperform EfficientNetV2B1 (McNemars p = 0.163). Errors occurred mainly between adjacent anatomical regions. Deep learning can classify craniofacial CT slices accurately and may support automated dataset organization and AI-assisted fracture diagnosis. External validation is needed.

candidates.title: Deep Learning and Radiomics Models for Predicting 90-Day Outcomes in Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
candidates.abstract: BackgroundAccurate prediction of 90-day outcomes following ischemic stroke is crucial for optimizing clinical strategies. This study aimed to systematically review and meta-analyze studies using deep learning (DL) and hand-crafted radiomics (HCR) models for predicting 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) outcomes after ischemic stroke. MethodsWe followed the PRISMA guidelines for systematic reviews. Four databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library) were searched comprehensively for studies published up to September 2025. Inclusion criteria encompassed original research focusing on ischemic stroke patients with mRS at 90 days as the primary outcome and predictive models utilizing imaging biomarkers from CT or MRI. Quality assessment of the included studies was conducted using the PROBAST and and METhodological RadiomICs Score (METRICS) tools. ResultsSeventeen studies were included in the quantitative meta-analysis. Models demonstrated good prognostic performance for 90-day outcomes, with pooled AUCs of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.80-0.86) for internal and 0.74 (95% CI: 0.67-0.89) for external validation sets, with no significant difference (p=0.42). Deep learning and hand-crafted radiomics models showed comparable diagnostic accuracy in the primary analysis (p=0.667); a difference in sensitivity favouring hand-crafted radiomics emerged only in a post-hoc analysis after exclusion of one outlier study. Models incorporating clinical variables significantly outperformed imaging-only models (p<0.01). CT- and MRI-based models showed similar performance. Treatment-specific analyses revealed higher sensitivity for IVT-based models and higher specificity for combined MT+IVT models. ConclusionsDL and HCR models demonstrate robust potential for predicting 90-day outcomes in ischemic stroke. Future research should focus on standardizing model evaluation metrics and incorporating explainable AI techniques to improve clinical applicability.

candidates.title: Reporting of Pericardial Adverse Events with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Disproportionality Analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System
candidates.abstract: Background. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can cause immune-related adverse events in almost any organ. While myocarditis has received the most attention, data on pericardial disease with ICI use are limited. We examined pericardial adverse event reporting with nine ICIs using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). Methods. We combined legacy AERS and current FAERS quarterly files from January 2011 to June 2026 into 18,629,240 unique cases, deduplicated by case number, and removed cases the FDA had listed as deleted. ICI exposure was identified from generic names, brand names, development code names and the active-ingredient field. Pericardial events were defined by seven MedDRA preferred terms. We estimated reporting odds ratios (ROR), proportional reporting ratios (PRR), Bayesian information components (IC) and empirical Bayes geometric means (EBGM). We also examined myocarditis co-reporting, time trends, a comparison with other antineoplastic agents, a MedDRA query-based outcome, and 14 alternative definitions. Results. The analysis included 18,514,045 cases: 277,434 involved an ICI, 34,792 carried a pericardial term, and 1,680 had both. Pericardial events were reported disproportionately with ICIs (ROR 3.35 (95% CI 3.19 to 3.52); PRR 3.34; IC025 1.62). Eight of nine agents had a ROR above 1 (3.32 to 5.63). Among the most frequently reported terms, estimates were highest for cardiac tamponade (5.59 (95% CI 4.98 to 6.28)), followed by pericardial effusion (3.83 (95% CI 3.60 to 4.07)) and pericarditis (2.09 (95% CI 1.89 to 2.31)). After removing cases that also reported myocarditis, the ROR was 3.13 (95% CI 2.98 to 3.30). Most sensitivity analyses gave similar estimates (ROR 3.13 to 3.47); defining exposure by generic drug names alone, which identified only 44% of exposed cases, gave 3.99. candidates.title: Cardiac MRI at 3.0T in the presence of implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs)
candidates.abstract: Patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) often are excluded from receiving CMR scans at 3.0T due to ICD-induced image artifacts. This work aims to transfer sequence protocols established for CMR imaging in the presence of ICDs at 1.5T to a first human application at 3.0T. All measurements were performed on a clinical 3T MRI scanner. Phantom measurements were used to establish and optimize wideband PSIR LGE imaging at 3.0T. Volunteer measurements with externally placed ICDs were used for optimization of CINE imaging and wideband PSIR imaging. Thirdly, patients with implanted ICD were examined with the optimized protocols. Human measurements showed that SA stacks obtained with spoiled GRE after contrast agent showed a markedly lower artifact burden than the conventional approach. For scar imaging, a wideband PSIR with a bandwidth of 3kHz and a frequency offset of +750Hz allowed a sufficient suppression of relevant artifacts in the majority of scans. No strong correlation between the image quality and the distance between the cardiac silhouette and the device was detected. The presented work shows the feasibility of clinical cardiac MRI at 3.0T including GRE-CINE and wideband PSIR-LGE for patients with ICDs.

candidates.title: Left Ventricular Diastolic Intraventricular Pressure Differences and Propagation Velocity with 4D-Flow MRI in Patients with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
candidates.abstract: BackgroundTransthoracic echocardiography (TTE) remains the gold standard for assessing left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction (DD), but noninvasive alternatives are needed to overcome geometric and acoustic limitations. 4D-Flow MRI enables comprehensive assessment of intraventricular pressure differences (IVPDs) and flow propagation velocity (VP). We aimed to evaluate 4D-Flow-derived IVPDs and VP in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). MethodsThirty-eight HCM patients and 38 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent TTE and 4D-Flow MRI. Spatiotemporal maps of velocity and IVPDs, decomposed into inertial and convective components, were derived along the main inflow streamline from the mitral valve to the apex. Peak early filling rate (PEFR) was used to normalize IVPDs and VP. ResultsWhile absolute peak flow rates were comparable, HCM patients exhibited significantly faster VP (100.4 vs. 60.2 cm/s, p < 0.01) and higher positive early E IVPD (1.40 vs. 0.92 mmHg, p < 0.01) compared to controls. Normalizing IVPDs by PEFR amplified group differences, revealing a markedly increased flow-normalized E-IVPD (5.13 vs. 2.94 x 10-3 mmHg{middle dot}ml-{superscript 1}{middle dot}s, p < 0.001) and deeper reverse ER IVPD (-6.06 vs. -4.61 x 10-3 mmHg{middle dot}ml-{superscript 1}{middle dot}s, p < 0.01) in HCM. These differences were primarily driven by the inertial components. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that ER IVPD is independently determined by PEFR and the TTE E/E ratio (r = 0.65, p < 0.001). Conclusions4D-Flow MRI-derived, flow-normalized IVPDs and propagation velocity provide robust, noninvasive markers of altered LV chamber stiffness and impaired diastolic filling in HCM, offering deeper 3D hemodynamic insights into diastolic dysfunction. candidates.title: Prevalence and Clinical Correlates of Coronary Perivascular Inflammation in an Asymptomatic Adult Primary Prevention Population: An Assessment of the CT-Derived Fat Attenuation Index Score (FAI-Score)
candidates.abstract: BackgroundCoronary perivascular fat attenuation index score (FAI-Score) on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) quantifies vascular inflammation and predicts cardiac mortality in symptomatic cohorts. However, its prevalence, anatomical distribution, and clinical correlates in asymptomatic primary prevention populations remain uncharacterized. MethodsIn an IRB-approved prospective study across two clinical sites, 84 consecutive asymptomatic adults (mean age 53.7 {+/-} 8.6 years; 63.1% men) with no prior coronary artery disease underwent screening CCTA and comprehensive clinical, metabolic, and biomarker profiling. AI-standardized FAI-Score was quantified across three epicardial vessels (LAD, LCx, RCA). High and very high perivascular inflammation were pre-specified as any vessel [≥]75th and [≥]90th percentiles, respectively. Luminal stenosis and plaque were graded using CAD-RADS 2.0. ResultsElevated FAI-Score ([≥]75th percentile) was present in 42.9% of participants (36/84; 95% CI 32.8% - 53.5%), with 17.9% (15/84; 95% CI 11.1% - 27.4%) exhibiting very high inflammation ([≥]90th percentile). Multi-vessel inflammation was identified in 17.9% (15/84), with the RCA most frequently involved ([≥]90th percentile in 13.1%). Standard circulating biomarkers, including ApoB, non-HDL-C, HbA1c, and PREVENT-ASCVD 10-year risk showed no association with binary inflammation. Systemic hs-CRP (median 0.8 mg/L) exhibited an inverse correlation with maximum vessel FAI-Score (Spearman {rho}=-0.27, p=0.014). Men demonstrated higher rates of elevated FAI-Score than women (52.8% vs. 25.8%, p=0.016; [≥]90th percentile: 26.4% vs. 3.2%, p=0.007). Strikingly, 46.2% (30/65) of participants with normal luminal anatomy (CAD-RADS 0) and 47.2% (25/53) with zero plaque burden harbored elevated FAI-Score; all 15 individuals with very high FAI-Score had CAD-RADS 0 (Fishers exact p=0.018). candidates.title: Narrow Is Slow: CT-Derived Anatomic Isthmus 3 Width and Arrhythmogenic Substrate in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot
candidates.abstract: BackgroundAnatomic isthmus 3 (AI 3) is defined as the myocardium between the pulmonary valve annulus and the ventricular septal defect patch that persists after tetralogy of Fallot (ToF) repair. Ventricular tachycardia (VT) propagated through slow conducting AI 3 (SCAI 3) represents a significant cause of morbidity in ToF. There is an unmet need for non-invasive identification of SCAI 3 in patients with ToF. ObjectivesTo assess whether the anatomic features of AI 3 as derived from cardiac computed tomography (CT) can predict slow conduction velocity during EP study. MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included patients with ToF who underwent an electrophysiologic study and had AI 3 width measured from the pre-procedure cardiac CT. All patients underwent programmed ventricular stimulation, and electroanatomic. Logistic regression was performed to assess the relationship between AI 3 width and the presence of SCAI 3. ResultsOf 27 consecutive patients with ToF, twelve patients were found to have SCAI 3, and ten patients were found to have SCAI 3 mediated VT. The AI 3 was significantly narrower in patients with SCAI 3 compared to those with normal AI 3 conduction (18.4 {+/-} 6.6 mm vs. 29.2 {+/-} 9.0 mm; p = 0.001). An AI 3 width above 21.5 mm carried a negative predictive value of 80.0%. ConclusionIn adults with repaired ToF referred for electrophysiology study, a narrower CT-derived AI 3 width was associated with SCAI 3 identification. AI 3 width measured on a CT obtained before PV replacement could help guide invasive risk stratification.

candidates.title: Results of a Community-Based Coronary CT Angiography Screening in Asymptomatic Adults With Cardiovascular Risk Factors: The Broward County Heart Project
candidates.abstract: BackgroundCoronary CT angiography (CCTA) and calcium scoring detect subclinical coronary atherosclerosis, but the results of community-based screening in asymptomatic adults with cardiovascular risk factors are poorly described. ObjectiveTo describe the results of the first phase of a county-funded CT screening program and their variation by demographics, health system, time, and ZIP code. MethodsRetrospective analysis of aggregate reports from the Broward County Florida Heart Project (May 2023-September 2025). Eligible residents were those with insurance coverage, age 45-70 years (limited exceptions), free of known cardiovascular disease and symptoms, with at least one risk factor. Examinations at six hospitals in four health systems were classified by the program team as normal (Category 1), abnormal (Category 2), or very abnormal (Category 3), with a separate flag for other non-coronary abnormality. We used Wilson confidence intervals and chi-square, trend, and Mantel-Haenszel tests. ResultsAmong 7,135 participants (58.3% men; 79.0% White, 8.0% Black, 17.2% Hispanic), 43.2% had Category 1, 45.4% Category 2, and 11.4% Category 3 results; 56.8% (95% CI, 55.7%-58.0%) had abnormal or very abnormal results. The proportion rose from 39.3% at 45-55 years to 78.5% at 71 or older (trend P<0.001) and was higher in men than women (68.9% vs 39.8%; odds ratio [OR], 3.36; 95% CI, 3.05-3.71). Rates were lower in Black than White participants (38.9% vs 58.6%; hospital-adjusted OR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.38-0.54) and in Hispanic than non-Hispanic participants (51.0% vs 57.8%). Abnormal results ranged from 39.5% to 60.3% across health systems (P<0.001). Variation across the 50 highest-volume ZIP codes did not exceed chance (P=0.53). ConclusionsMore than half of insured, asymptomatic adults with risk factors screened in this community program had abnormal results, with steep age and sex gradients and unexplained variation across health systems.

candidates.title: Cardiomyocyte-Derived Cell-Free DNA in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
candidates.abstract: IntroductionIn hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), wall stress and subclinical myocardial injury related in part to pathological hypercontractility, which in turn are associated with worse outcomes. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is released from cardiomyocytes (cfDNA-CM) through irreversible cellular injury and death. We investigated the feasibility of quantifying cfDNA-CM and its relationship to HCM patient characteristics. MethodsWe analyzed 57 plasma samples from stable patients with HCM and 10 plasma samples from patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Plasma cfDNA was isolated from both groups. Whole genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) libraries were generated and sequenced with short-read sequencing. Methylation patterns were used for tissue deconvolution analysis and cell-specific cfDNA quantification. ResultsYields of cfDNA (p = 0.003) and cfDNA-CM (p = 0.002) fractions were higher in AMI controls than HCM, supporting the validity of the assay. Within the HCM cohort, the median cfDNA yield was 12.22 ng [IQR: 7.77, 18.94]. The cfDNA-CM fraction in this cohort ranged from 0% to 6.4% of total cfDNA. Higher cfDNA-CM tertiles were associated with higher body mass index (BMI, p=0.001), a greater prevalence of BMI [≥]30 kg/m{superscript 2} (p<0.001), and a higher prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (p=0.038). No significant differences were observed in other demographic, genetic, and laboratory characteristics. Higher cfDNA-CM tertile was numerically associated with higher New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, while circulating biomarkers of wall stress (NT-proBNP) and myocardial injury (troponin) did not differ across tertiles (p=0.83 and p=0.29, respectively). ConclusionIsolation and quantification of cfDNA as well as detection of cfDNA-CM in chronic stable patients with HCM are feasible. candidates.title: Machine Learning-based Prediction of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Underlying Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
candidates.abstract: BackgroundPacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) is a major complication of chronic right ventricular pacing and develops in up to 25% of patients. Reliable prediction of PICM may facilitate individualized pacing strategy selection; however, currently available approaches demonstrate limited discriminative performance. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting PICM in patients with atrioventricular block (AVB) underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction. MethodsIn this multicenter prospective study derived from the RISK-PICM registry (January 2002 to January 2026), 125 patients with AVB who underwent pacemaker implantation were analyzed. PICM was defined as a [≥]10% reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) resulting in an LVEF <50%. Four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost, were trained using stratified 4-fold cross-validation with hyperparameter optimization and model discrimination was evaluated. ResultsPICM developed in 41 patients (32.8%) during a median follow-up of 4.8 years. Male sex, pre-implant minimum QTc interval, and post-implant maximum QRS duration were significantly associated with PICM in univariable Cox regression. XGBoost achieved the highest discriminative performance (AUROC 0.831; sensitivity 0.805; specificity 0.845). Feature importance analysis identified baseline LVEF and post-implant maximum QRS duration as the most influential features. Model-derived risk stratification significantly differentiated high-risk and low-risk groups on Kaplan-Meier analysis (P < 0.001). ConclusionsML-based models, particularly XGBoost, demonstrated clinically meaningful performance for PICM and may support individualized pacing strategy selection in patients with AVB and underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction. candidates.title: Age-, sex-, and ethnicity-stratified CMR strain reference ranges and centile-based categories from the Healthy Hearts Consortium
candidates.abstract: BackgroundThis study presents reference ranges for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial strain from the Healthy Hearts Consortium, while evaluating variations by demographic characteristics (age, sex, and ethnicity) and technical factors (scanner vendor, magnetic field strength). We derived reference ranges and centile-based categories for ventricular, atrial, and rapid strain parameters. The prognostic relevance of these categories was assessed by examining their associations with incident cardiovascular events. MethodsThe dataset included 9,088 CMR studies. Automated image analysis pipelines were established using suiteHEART (NeoSoft Inc.) and cvi42 (Circle Cardiovascular Imaging). A three-step quality control framework was applied including exclusion of incomplete data, visual assessment of image and segmentation quality, and statistical outlier removal. Ventricular strain and strain rate were measured using both software solutions. Additional cvi42-derived metrics included velocity and displacement, annular plane systolic excursion metrics, and rapid strain parameters. Age- and sex-specific reference ranges were generated using lambda-mu-sigma (LMS) modeling with penalized splines. Reference ranges were defined as values between the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. For lower-tail classification, values below the 2.5th percentile were considered mildly out-of-range and values below the 0.5th percentile at least moderately out-of-range. Differences across scanner vendors (Siemens, Philips, GE) and magnetic field strengths (1.5 T vs. 3 T) were evaluated using adjusted linear models. The prognostic relevance of selected cvi42-derived categories was evaluated in approximately 45,000 UK Biobank participants using Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. candidates.title: Efficacy of Disease-Modifying Treatments in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Five Phase III Randomized Controlled Trials
candidates.abstract: BackgroundSeveral disease-modifying agents for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) have been investigated, but differences in trial design and background stabilizer use complicate interpretation of their efficacy. This meta-analysis assessed their efficacy overall and by background stabilizer use. MethodsPubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through September 2026 for phase III randomized, placebo-controlled trials of disease-modifying therapy in ATTR-CM. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary (KCCQ-OS) score, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), pooled with a random-effects model. Treatment effects were compared between the monotherapy and baseline stabilizer strata using a mixed-effects model. ResultsFive trials (ATTR-ACT, APOLLO-B, ATTRibute-CM, HELIOS-B, CARDIO-TTRansform; N=3497) were included. Disease-modifying therapy reduced all-cause mortality (risk ratio, 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66-0.87; I2=0%) and improved 6MWD (pooled standardized mean difference [SMD], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.20-0.67), KCCQ-OS score (SMD, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.19-0.55), and NT-proBNP (SMD, - 0.53; 95% CI, -0.89 to -0.18). The mortality benefit was similar whether therapy was given alone or added to a background stabilizer (pooled risk ratio, 0.77 vs. 0.71; P for interaction = 0.59), but treatment effects on 6MWD (pooled SMD, 0.49 vs. 0.14), KCCQ-OS score (0.44 vs. 0.07), and NT-proBNP (-0.65 vs. -0.13) were smaller among patients receiving a background stabilizer (P for interaction = 0.012, <0.001, and 0.029, respectively). ConclusionDisease-modifying treatments reduced all-cause mortality and favored functional capacity, health status, and NT-proBNP outcomes in patients with ATTR-CM.
